I am a native Russian speaker, and they ignored me. I can only imagine what they do to others. ALL employees seemed like they were working in a gulag! I echo what others have said online. Customer service is NON EXISTENT. It's not that they are rude, they are aloof towards customers. 
        .   
They don't even make eye contact. Either those employees are seriously working against their will (slave labor or family pressure) or they've picked the least friendly people in the universe!

Meh. It's "okay". We have been here once for lunch and once for dinner; both pre-COVID times. Service was good. Nothing memorable about the food or that stood out at all. With so many places to eat and explore with your taste buds it just doesn't make sense to go back to a place more than a couple of times unless something struck you as a reason to go back and honestly I couldn't tell you that I would go back unless I had some buy one get one or 50% off deal to try them again.

I am into trying new workout options and not fads. Cyclebar opened in Meridian at the Village last week and their first two weeks open all rides were free, so I figured I would give it a go. I didn't know what to expect but as soon as I walked in, I was greeted by JP, who was super pleasant and welcomed me with a handshake and concierge service as if I were a VIP. He walked me through the check in process, where everything was and even showed me how to properly clip into my bike so I was set for an awesome class. Cyclebar is an experience and worth every penny I plan on spending here in the future. They provide towels, water bottles, shoes, fruit for before and after and the energy levels of the instructors is top notch. 

I entered an auditorium with 48 bikes. The instructor was Gonzalo and his energy was through the roof. He cheered everyone on and motivated through smiles, stellar music and a light show to reflect the mood. His story telling abilities allows you to visualize actually riding somewhere other than there to truly push through it. I walked out feeling rejuvenated, motivated and my metabolism on fire! I was dripping sweat and was greeted with a cool lavender towel to refresh before leaving. I didn't walk away tired, I walked away ready for more and CANNOT wait to go back!

Well, after almost a year from the opening, I still find this store great in some aspects, but the pits in others.
First, stay away on weekends. It is so crowded that parking there is painful to the say the least. If you want to really shop it's aisles, go on a weekday.

Yes, this is the store to go find things you won't find at any other grocer, even the Coop.  For example, they have Rancho Gordo beans that we can't find in any other store around here. And not just one or two types of their beans, but at least a half dozen heirloom types. They have great local pork cuts. We can't find hog jowls in any other store, or great ham hocks.

The help is very cordial and helpful in finding items in this cavernous store.

We did find the Pharmacy less than well staffed on this Saturday. We finally had to leave when the one person working in the pharmacy couldn't get to us in 20 minutes and our frozen foods were getting defrosted. We won't be using them again. the McMillan store seems 10X more efficient.

So for the curiosity factor, one visit seems enough, but not for a steady diet for us.

This was the only Mexican restaurant with good food we could find two years ago. It is busy now and the food and service are awful. The orders are wrong and the waitress is rude. I purchased a drink that seemed to have no alcohol in it. We thought it might be a fluke, but our last three visits have been very disappointing. I think the increase in business is encouraging them to not be friendly or serve the same good food, they are scrimping.
Best ever, love the staff and selection, love same as cash. My whole house and i mean every single room is furnished in some way by RC Willey. Appliances too.

The curb has a ton of potential. It has a great location and the layout and feel can Definitely set a great atmosphere. 

I do feel a bit out of place here when I go alone or with a friend. The food is also hit and miss. Several times I've noticed inconsistencies with the food and that makes trusting the location difficult. I want to know what to expect in my food profiles. 

I have found myself only visiting during football Sunday lunch hour. Seems to be my best fit for this location.   With a bit more work in the kitchen you'd have a top 20 bar and grill.

We experienced nothing but fantastic service at RC Willey.  To date we have stocked our new house with a Tempur Pedic bed, leather couch/love seat/chair and full line of LG appliances from here.  Pricing, service and delivery were all on point.  My wife and I will always stop here first when looking for new home furnishings.

I love this place! Everybody knows Albertsons-, the name, the brand but this location is a real gem! It has everything you could ever imagine! It has a pharmacy, a deli, a huge selection of wine with winetasting, , a full bar called Talon, a local popcorn vendor, a bakery, a florist, and every single other type of "bar" you can imagine- Olives, chicken wings, Mexican food, hot foods! I think they had a Mochi  ice cream display too! They also have a hamburger counter and a poke bar!! Amazing!! 

Their produce is the best I've seen and their meat selection is unsurpassed!! SRF beef is really superb!!  

Staff are always available and super friendly asking if you need help finding things and they always escort you to the aisle instead of just telling you where you can find it.  Their guacamole is really good and they even have a spicy version ! 

Coming here is not like going to an ordinary grocery but a full blown shopping experience that'll exceed your expectations!  It's definitely worth it!

We are Chip lovers usually! I drove by Crumbl and holy crap they are so good! The Nutella- peanut butter. Get out. I like how they offer a few different flavors....really a good company that competes well with chip!
Holy Cluck! Amazing food and amazing people!!! I truly enjoy this place and the atmosphere. This place is a must try!

A friendly and knowledgeable technician stopped by my house to inform me that my tree was dying and they could help. They were offering a deal and I was impressed (and concerned for my tree). I rec'd an email saying that I would be charged over $300 for a year's service. I called the tech, who reassured me that I would only be charged for each service as it occurred. I was told they would come early the next week. It's been three weeks and I've left 3 voicemails. My tree is stilling dying and I have not been serviced.

Friendly staff, they get my drinks correct every time, the location is clean and spacious. Good place to work/study. Music at normal level. I've come here 10 continuous days and have nothing but praise for this place and the people working here. Thanks for helping me work remote while visiting family during the holidays

We had a very favorable experience at RC WILLEY. They answered all of our questions. And tried very hard in pleasing us. Going through customer service was fast and efficient. RC WILLEY is my go to store.

Anniversary Sale.  Bought a recliner with microfiber for $249.

Love the furniture here. Very reasonably priced for the quality, lots of friendly helpful staff. I will say I was asked if I needed help just s but too often.  Staff were honest in NOT recommending a particular recliner due to consumer complaints about durability of the product.

They have many gorgeous bedroom sets that seem to be very high quality and for a third of the price as stores in my city (Portland).

I wish they had a store back home. I will definitely consider buying here in the future.

Newly opened - March 8 - this behemoth of roughly 100,000 SF is the  largest Albertsons store ever to be built anywhere.  The second store in the new Market Street line for Albertsons this makes the huge first launch of that concept - the Albertsons Market Street flagship in Boise which opened last summer - look small by comparison.   So know that before you go.  Expect yuuugggggeeee.

In spite of brightly lit wide aisles - well stocked with almost anything you could imagine and some things you couldn't - and just as super helpful and friendly staff as the Boise store - all terrific for making shoppers feel that our business matters to the them - I found the store too overwhelmingly big to want to shop here regularly.  But there are specialty items here that will make this destination shopping for me when I need those things.  Noting 5 star reviews are from Yelpers who got prepared food and sat in the bar for a drink but who didn't shop the store, it may be different strokes for different folks applies if eating in and having a drink is what you're there for. 

A good way to take a look inside the store before you go is to see the photo layout in the Boise Dev website or to watch the local news channel video.  Both are linked below.

https://boisedev.com/news/2019/03/07/albertsons-market-street/

https://www.ktvb.com/article/news/local/worlds-largest-albertsons-store-set-to-open-in-meridian/277-17c9be87-90ce-4716-b4f6-49177d39d8f7

FULL BAR:  This Market Street, like the one in Boise, has a full bar.  I don't get it - a bar in a grocery - but different strokes apply since it was packed in mid afternoon on a weekday.  If you're looking for it, it is called Talon, go right when you enter the store from any door.

TONS OF TAKE AWAY FOOD OPTIONS:   It was clear from the crowds in the side of the store with many prepared food take away stations that many shoppers find this just right for them.  Prepared foods available for take out include "restaurant style" (their description) hot dishes on a hot table as well as lots of options behind counters with people to assemble them for you.  From build your own salad, to bbq - smoked meats like ribs, to sushi, to other Asian hot foods, to deli sandwiches...the list goes on.  I've never a fan of food courts anywhere and this is as if a big gourmet one.  If that is your thing this will be a good thing for you.  And a good for them thing is that it is - like all of  the store - sparkling clean.

FAB FLORAL: If you're looking for fresh flowers, in arrangements and bunches, I can't imagine any grocer with a more wonderful selection.  Since the floral counter is straight ahead when you enter one of the doors you'll see them in full display.

UNIQUE CHARCUTERIE:  This is a reason to shop here for me - the charcuterie and cheese sections.  The guy who manages both came from Fred Meyer, just as did the manager of the great Boise Albertson's Market Street cheese - charcuterie department.  This man also has Italian heritage and his Italian dad used to own a butcher shop so he is well acquainted with the delights of really good charcuterie.  You will find in the  case here things you will likely not find anywhere else in the Treasure Valley including braesola, speck and Serrano ham, all of which are sliced to order.

SAY CHEESE:  Adjacent to charcuterie, this section has a great selection of cheeses both imported and domestic - although I still give the nod to the Boise location for most variety.  The special 'hook' for this Meridian location is the making fresh mozzarella right there at that counter.

PRODUCE:  Large assortment,  beautifully displayed and friendly staff who can answer questions about unique things.  A minority of options are organic but they're getting better at that for sure.

GASTON'S IS IN THE HOUSE:  In addition to full in-house bakery, this store carries some artisan loaf varieties by local baker Gaston's.  You can also buy Gaston's local milled Idaho wheat flour here.  Being a bread 'snob' - if I'm going to eat it I want it to be artisan - I applaud them for bringing Gaston's in.

LAND & SEA:  The butcher section is as broad and deep as Boise's store and the same is true for the fish section.

BASQUE BITS:  If you appreciate that the Albertson's Market Street in Boise has some selections from Boise's Basque Market in that store you will SO appreciate the expanded selections here.  On egin! 

VINO:  The wine section is perhaps the largest I've ever seen in a grocer.  Aisles and aisles from cheap basics to spendy specials.  There is even a temp controlled room for high end wines with a bottle over $2,000 in price. No kidding.  I'm wed to the Boise CoOp's north end Wine Shop or Meridian store for my local wine buying outside of local wineries, but this is an big choice resource.

PHARMACY:  In store and it looks as if there will be drive in window for pick up open soon too.

Been here quite a few times and I always leave happy. Staff is very friendly and on top of it. Everything I've ever ordered off the food menu is delicious! I love their sliders especially. Fun atmosphere and you can see the staff enjoy being here. Good vibes!

I heard about this place from my daughter-in-law who went there for some chicken soup, the cure all when your are ill.  She told me that all of their soups are gluten free and that they have gluten free bread for all of the sandwiches they offer. I was intrigued and vowed I would try it out soon. 
Today, being afflicted myself with a wonderful winter cold, I sought them out. I tried their buffalo chicken soup and it was absolutely delicious! I read in several of the reviews that folks thought the soups were bland but I did not think so. I also bought the Gouda grilled cheese sandwich and it also was delicious! They put a ton of cheese on there along with grilled onions and grilled red peppers. My only regret was not picking up a couple of the 32 oz containers of soup to take with me!
I will say that this is kinda of a pricey lunch with my 16 oz bowl of soup and a full sandwich coming out to $13.75. It was filling though and actually, I only ate half and had the rest for dinner. So for two meals, that is a good price.
They do have a dining area but it is rather small and wouldn't be conducive to a large group of friends meeting for lunch.
The location is prime for this Mom and Pop business to do well and maybe expand with another location. The service is friendly and quick. 
I will return again to try another of their soups.
Our go-to place for a sushi special occasion! The friend avocado lobster roll and  mango tango sushi roll are an essential to every visit!

I normally don't eat at a "fast food (FF)" restaurant, but there are times when limited time and hunger meet and a FF place fits the bill.

CFA is the best of those FF choices, IMHO. Quick service, help that can understand multiple orders, and know their menu so as to make informed suggestions makes them a good place to eat FF. Maybe the fact that they hire more than just entree level teenagers (even seasoned citizens) has something to do with the quality of their employees. And they keep the place clean and actually wipe down the tables soon after someone leaves. But, don't go on Sunday, they are closed so the employees can spend time with their families or go to church.

The food is good, but you better like chicken, as the cow advertising mascot implies. Don't like fried, try the grilled sandwich. Don't want the bun, try the chicken strips. Breakfast biscuits, with chicken-of course, are also available. No french fries, but waffle fried potatoes make for a nice change. Many swear by the CFA special sauce for a dip for these potatoes. The orders are quickly filled and brought to your table. Their lemonade, diet and sugar, is tops.

Seating is accessible for those with mobility issues and the restrooms are clean and meet ADA requirements. An ADA parking access ramp is close to the entrance. While CFA keeps their sidewalks and lot well plowed after a snow, with ice melt, the lot is on the North side of the building and the parking lot may be icy after a warm day and cold night, so heads up is in order.

They will even make the sandwiches so you can travel with them or even have them arrive at home for freezing. Now that CFA is showing up in WA, maybe our friends and relatives won't have to smuggle them into that "uncivilized state".

Recently got my Stor Mor shed. What a great process. Staff was helpful and friendly when I picked it out. My HOA had restrictions for paint colors. No problem for Stor Mor. Add a window. No problem for Stor Mor. Delivery and set up in one day. Installation was no problem for Stor Mor. All the joints are tight and good build quality. Way to go Stor Mor!!

I have gone to this restaurant for several years. Live their mango tacos and rice. Sadly I may never return since last time I was there a couple of women brought their dog in to sit under their table.   Dogs should never  be allowed in restaurants not even "companion or therapy dogs. Come on.

When u have her mom and her plus her moms friend there all with valid ids all u do is cost ur self money. Get a scanner and stop harassing people about the direction of their license. Great eggs Benedict. Only complaint is the eggs were not runny! However the amazing sauce made up for it. Great spice on the potatoes. Wait staff 5 stars
Amazing food!!!! Large portions. Coffee very good. Our server Stacy F was superb!!!! Will be back.

They say it's the best Italian food in the treasure valley and they ain't kidding!! Fresh food, great customer service and over all a really great place to sit down relax and have a nice evening. I highly recommend it!

I shop here often. The staff is very helpful and courteous. Selection is good and prices are average among regular grocery stores.
This review is for the deli counter and perhaps its new policy. The last several times I visited the deli counter I noticed that the weight of the deli items I received was more than I what I had ordered. If I asked for a quarter pound, I got a third. If I ordered a half, it was almost a pound.  This has happened to both me and my hub.  Normally, they ask if the overage is okay. They no longer do this.  The last time it happened I mentioned it to the staff member, she just shrugged her shoulders and said, "it's not that much over."  I told her the next time it happens I will ask them to remove the excess. Interestingly, the weight has never been under.  Hoping that this isn't something that the employees have been asked to do because it puts them in an awkward situation with their customers.
Leave Idaho if you don't want to be around guns. Saw sign on door and left.

So, my husband & I visited K-Fusion Korean BBQ again last Friday and we were pleasantly surprised at the improvement of their services and the tastiness of their food.  The waiteress/waiters kept calm although they were pretty busy on a Friday night.  The amount of food they gave was a lot more than I expected, and the food wavery tasty!  We ordered BIbim bap, Jap Chae and bulgogi.  Good job K-Fusion, you have come a long way since the grand opening!!! 
PS: If you could work on decresing the price of the "side dish buffet", that'd be great!!!

Well, it wasn't A-OK but it wasn't horrible. Even with the discount, I want better than what we got for our money. 

I'll start with the good things. The beds were exactly how I like them, so that was nice. The rooms were dark, so when I woke up, sportin'  the hangover from hell, I was really grateful for that. I wasn't thrilled that the blankets that I pull up to my face when I sleep, that weren't covered by a comforter I could remove. So I tried to keep my slightly germaphobe mind from wondering what might be on those blankets that don't get washed as often as I would like. 

The service was alright. I shouldn't have to comment on the friendliness of the staff, that should just be. But since it usually isn't, I'll say that the staff was definitely friendly. 

Now for the bitches.... Continental breakfast, my ass. Pancakes from a bag that come out some conveyor type system? Really? You know they suck, I know they suck, everyone knows. The only people that dig on bagged pancakes that come out a funky machine are kids that are fascinated by shiny objects. I'm on vacation, for the sake of Pete, I DON'T want LIGHT cream cheese for my bagel. I did NOT just work my ass off to vacation with light cream cheese and funky bagged pancakes. It's an insult and worse yet, made me puke up all the alcohol I drank the night before. Maybe it was a blessing.

Ok, all jokes aside. It was alright but if you're gonna offer a continental breakfast, do it right.

We are visiting from out of town and I found Moe Joes on Yelp. IT IS FANTASTIC!!! Home cooked feel good food, so good we went 2 days in a row! You have to try the grilled biscuit and the chicken fried steak doesnt disappoint!
Back in town again. The food here is just incredible. Never fails to deliver fresh, innovative dishes. Yum.

Probably the BEST breakfast I have ever had ( besides my wife's lol). The food was very fresh.  Very well put together menu and the execution of the dishes by the chef was beyond what was expected.  The wait staff went beyond their job description also in aiding me in finding locations of other businesses in town.  5 of 5 stars all the way!!!

Almost 6 years ago I needed affordable, high-quality carpet FAST. I had to choose something in-stock. These guys explained all the different carpet features and got me no-interest financing.

I'm getting ready to sell my house and I couldn't be more pleased with how the carpet has held up. It looks great, and I have 3 pets and a toddler! I will definitely be back if my next house needs new flooring.

I have seen Mo Joes around for a while, but I have never tried it till today. I took my family as always to eat breakfast. It was a nice morning, so we sat outside. I was very happy as the inside is small.

The tables on the outside are plain plastic with gaps between the plastic planks. My fork fell in between one of these gaps onto the ground. I was about to just wipe it off and continue using it, when my wife noticed this and offered me hers. 

Ok, onto the food. Mo Joes has a Chicken Fried Steak on their menu. Being from Texas, anytime I see this, I just cant resist it. 

I love Chicken Fried Steak (CFS) and consider myself an authority on them. So far, my search for a good CFS in Boise has led me to Good Wood. Chili's used to have a pretty decent one, but they took it off the menu a year of so ago.

The CFS at Goodwood is pretty good, so I just had to try the one here to find out if the cooks here knew how to make one.

When I fist looked at the steak, it looked pretty good from the outside, though It is shaped weird. Traditionally CFS is more round. The one here looks like an oversized steak finger, but I am not going to count them down for that. {;us I am not sure what sized fingers it would take to pick it up

It seemed to have a nice crust that was well browned and did not look greasy.  I had to use a knife to cut it, which is the first test to a good CFS. A good CFS should be fork tender and not require a knife.

I could not really tell what cut of beef it was, but I am sure it was not round steak. I think it was some cut of actual steak, but it did not look like any cut I was familiar with. I did rank them down a bit on this as the cut of beef looked a little strange to me. I recommend listing the actual cut of beef on the menu.

I remember the old days of Mystery meat that McDonalds serves and maybe still does. So that made me into a bit of a stickler on knowing what exactly it is that I am eating.

I took a bite and it was not bad. The meat was greasy and in some parts not done at all, which is why I left most of it on the plate. The meat was way to thick. They should have tenderized it and made it a bit thinner. A thinner cut would cook quicker and not be greasy. The meat was so greasy that it oozed out and made the nice crispy crust a gooey mess.

So on my 1-10 Texas scale, I could give their CFS a 3 because it was not tender and way to greasy. On a 1-10 Idaho scale, I would give it a 6 mainly because very few in Idaho have a clue how to make one. So far their only competition is Good Wood, which ranks a 7 of the Texas scale and a 10 on my Idaho Scale.

I think with some tweaking, the CFS at Moe Joes has promise. 

Next I have what was supposed to be scrambled eggs. I cant rank them down much here because I have yet to find a single place in Idaho that can make scrambled eggs. Scrambled eggs should be nice and fluffy, with some flavor, not just a cut up very bland omelette, but that is what I got.

Good scrambled eggs should be a good mixture of around 60/40 eggs to milk. Then something mixed in like herbs, salt, pepper, or other to give them some flavor.

The star of my breakfast by a landslide was the potatoes. They had good flavor, were crispy, and were not greasy at all.

My wife had the Breakfast for Beginners.  4 pieces of flabby and very greasy bacon was part of it. I did not taste the rest of her breakfast, but my wife said that she did not like it at all.

My daughter had the pancakes, which I thought tasted fine, but she said she did not like them. I think the problem here is that she has an issue with gluetin. 

I would not mine trying this place again, as a friend of ours swears by this place, and recommended the Corn Beef Hash. So if I can convince my wife, I might want to come here and give this place a 2nd chance.

I love going to Gino's. I have always had a great experience here. The staff is wonderful and the owner is extremely friendly and he is always interacting with his customers. The food is amazing and well priced. My wife and I enjoy the house bread and sauce. They make it fresh daily. We have come a few times for just the bread and a few glasses of wine. I ordered the margarita pizza and it was fantastic. We will be back often.

Not impressed. Ordered take out and they said 30 min. Got there in 40 and waited 20 more minutes. Paid $40. For two apps and two main dishes. Ordered cheesy crab puffs, lettuce wraps, honey almond shrimp and vegetables chow fun. The crab puffs and shrimp we're good the rest was not. The chicken lettuce wraps were all onion and pepper with minuscule bits of chicken. 
I won't go back. There has got to be better out there.

Gino's is hands down the best Italian food I've had in the Treasure Valley to date.  

Came here on a Thursday night with a large party.  Originally, I had called on Monday to make reservations for 10 that Thursday.  Over the next few days, that number grew to 16. Gino's was perfectly lovely about the shifting reservation party number and at the appointed reservation time, they were ready for us.

Gino's is larger than it looks from the outside.  Our party of 16 were seated comfortably together (several tables placed together) and there was also a wedding party enjoying their rehearsal dinner and a third large celebration party and we were all comfortably seated with plenty of room (enough space that it was never overly loud).  

I began my dining experience with a particularly finely mixed Old Fashioned.  We were also served a delicious, fresh made flat bread with a mix of garlic, olive oil, and red pepper to dip it in (amazing).  I then ordered their gnocchi with creamy pesto.  My main dining companion ordered their gnocchi with a four cheese sauce, which I also tried.  Both were stellar.  Though, my preference was the gnocchi with the four cheese sauce.  It was the absolute pinnacle of deliciousness.  As a member of our party put it, it'll leave you wanting to lick the bowl.  

It is just that good.

As if that weren't enough--we ordered dessert.  I ordered their chocolate mousse, which came with shavings of beautifully dark and rich chocolate blended in.  My main dining companion ordered their creme brulee, which looked amazing (the top is caramelized at the table).  I REALLY wanted to try some--but that would have meant sacrificing a bite of my chocolate mousse in return--which, as it turned out, I was unwilling to do (it was REALLY good...like...smack-any-hand-that-tries-to-come-near-it--good!).

The service was absolutely perfect and they kept up with our large party quite well.  The owner, Gino, came over to our table and checked on us more than once.

Finally, the location.  Yes....it's WAAAAAY the heck out Mcmillan road in Meridian.  It's easily a 25 minute drive from my house (depending on traffic--it could be even longer).  Which, if you know me at all, you know that I'm hard pressed to leave my little cocoon of awesome in downtown Boise.  But, my people, it is ABSOLUTELY worth it. 

In short?  Gino's:  it's worth the drive.

Get to it!

A tasty sandwich delivered in a timely fashion, by a company dedicated to consistent quality. I normally avoid corporate chains at all costs, but they are one of the few that deliver to the office. Highly recommended.

I have found true chocolate-dipped old-fashioned donuts in exactly three places:  NYC's Donut Pub, a billion sad boxes of Entemann's, and this particular Fred's. Of the three, Fred clearly takes the cake. 

The chocolate is a little weird and waxy, not unlike what you'd get on one of Entemann's aforementioned donettes, but the way it interacts with the super-crisp cake donut is kind of awesome. For whatever reason, it makes for a crunch that has only ever existed in those weird rice krispy-impregnated Krackle candy bars. It's not the best characteristic for a donut to have, but it's totally a unique one. So, it's got that going for it.

Also, their French cruellers aren't bad, and I hear there's a perfectly lovely supermarket beyond the donut case.

Been coming here for awhile now. Love the freshness of the food. Haven't tried one thing that I have not liked. Big fan of the rumbi rice. The service is always great. The food is always good. Nice that you can also call your orders in and pick them up

My wife and I went there for a date night during the concert series at The Village.   I found the pizza to be moderately good, not knock your lights out.  The menu is really Ala Cart everything, even your pizza toppings.   So be careful if you're on a tight budget.   It's a thin crust pizza that I like, but would like better with more toppings.    Because of the price per topping I felt too restricted.

The workers are friendly enough and the atmosphere was nice. It is a tad pricey at $18 (plus tip) to get a middle schoolers hair cut. The wait list is not accurate. It noted that our wait time would be 27 minutes and it was 45 minutes. However, the cut turned out well and my son is happy. I'm sure that we will return -- with an understanding that we will have to wait a while for service.

This is the honest truth as always, I've avoided this place for years and years. My first couple of experiences in Minnesota wasn't good and then they came to Texas near where we lived and they didn't survive in Texas, so why bother if you can make it in Texas with BBQ, right? 
Well I was pleasantly surprised today, a bit worried walking in at 12:45 and about 6 couples dinning and no staff to be seen for more than 2 minutes. Finally someone came from the back and we were seated. I was impressed with the cornbread muffins, the rib tips were really nice, bbq chicken was good, and roasted chicken great taste and super moist. Loved all of the sauces. So I'll stop being so stuck up about my BBQ I guess

Nice people, bad food. We just had ours boxed up and took it home to get rid of as we didn't want our server to feel bad. Weird, chewy meat....both the chicken and beef.  Maybe boiled? I was sad for the owners!
Amazing pho! Probably some of the best I've had in Boise along with Pho Bac. Great portion size and they don't skimp out on the meat. Friendly staff with fast service! Would definitely recommend!

I've stayed here a couple of times. I really like this KOA it's clean and the people are always friendly. The best thing is that it's pretty well located and relatively close to everything. Great shopping, restaurants etc. The only thing I didn't care for is that their internet is terrible. Outside of that you'll enjoy your stay!
Delicious breakfast! The doughnut pancake is crazy good! They also have really good mimosas

Moe Joe's is such an amazing breakfast spot! The food is great, the service is excellent, and the restaurant is clean. The only downside is that the inside of the restaurant itself is a little small but turnover is quick here. If you go to Moe Joe's for breakfast on the weekend, expect a wait. But the wait will not be too long!

Traveling states with the family and had arrived in Boise in the late afternoon. After checking into our hotel we began heading towards the best sounding Italian restaurant we could find. After a short debate on whether or not to dress up from our car travel attire, we arrived at Gino's. Quickly discovering we should have dressed up, we walked up to the front desk where three nice hostesses greeted us. They asked us if we had a reservation at which we said no. They frowned and we feared for having to choose a new place, more in line with our 'on the road' rags. However, one of the girls promptly found her manager and tried to find out if they could squeeze us in, as it was a busy night. Within ten minutes we were seated in the beautifully decorated back room and were served promptly. The servers, food runners, and even Gino himself were quick to answer any questions we had. Excellent food at a mildly fair price. Complementary bread is served with an oil and spice mixture that is delicious. An overall nice experience, just remember to dress up!

I've only ever ordered delivery and it has never taken less than an hour to have our food delivered. If you order delivery expect to wait an hour to an hour and a half. No joke. 

The food is okay. Not mind blowing but it's the best in the area that delivers. The reason we choose to order Joy Garden even though they're crazy slow is because their Boba smoothies are AMAZING. They use to have raspberry which was sooo good but they do not have that flavor anymore. Pretty lame... I'll keep ordering here but if there is EVER a better Chinese food place that has delivery in the area I'll change up who we order from.

Decided to give Mekong another go. I'd had great food the two previous times and it's close to work and easy to pickup. I called in and ordered the same thing I had the first time I tried it; Mok Kai. A banana leaf wrapped chicken with a ball of sticky rice on the side. What I picked up was a small styrofoam container with a loose concoction of chicken and other ingredients that on my previous order was in a tightly gathered ball. The rice...oh the rice (now this is a 1st). The rice was in a quart size plastic ziplock baggie. A sandwich baggie!!! I really couldn't believe what I was seeing. When I asked about why the chicken was loose and the rice wasn't in a ball as it previously had been, the cashier/server simply said "oh...well...it must have been the other cook that day". I've worked in enough restaurants (front and back of the house) to know the importance of consistency. I will also mention that the owner was standing right in front of me. One might anticipate a friendly "hello" or something. I am patronizing your business. Unfortunately he was too consumed with the HVAC guy and his toddler who was running loose through the kitchen to extend even a smile. I will probably try Mekong again (the food is delicious) I just hope they get situated and trained before more people take notice, like I have.

I feel bad rating this Hokulia as just two stars, but I have a hard time viewing it objectively as just a shave ice place. I have to compare it to the Hokulia in Provo (where we live), where we have been ordering shave ice for three summers and which I would consistently rate 5 stars. Maybe these guys were having a bad day.

First off, they were supposed to open at 3, but when we got there, the tables were all still chained together sitting in the hot sun, not completely cleaned off from the day before, and this locations tables no longer have holes cut into the tabletop to place your shave ice in (though according to past reviews they used to), and they don't have umbrellas for the tables, so you're just sitting on hot benches in the hot sun. There is a little strip of grass with a few trees next to where the Hokulia truck was, but it had rained the night before, so the grass was damp and it was a little muddy at the base of the trees (not awesome if you have toddlers, which I do). There were people there who brought blankets to sit on, which is smart, but as visitors to Boise, we had never been to this location before and didn't come prepared.

Secondly, it's next to a very busy street (Fairview). If you have young children, this is a major stressor. I would recommend different placement within the parking lot, or as the Provo Hokulia does, set up little portable chain ropes between the seating area and the street so that kids can't easily get too close to the street.

Thirdly, the pricing structure is a bit different. Water in Boise is $3 (hello there, state fair pricing) and water in Provo is $1. That's a big difference. They also don't offer the same sizes--at least not advertised on their board. I had an 18 month old, a 3 year old, a 5 year old, and a 10 year old with me. This was a special treat, so I got them each their own of the smallest size with ice cream ($5 a piece, $4 without ice cream). As we were waiting for our shave ices, I heard an employee tell someone they could make a smaller kids size. Lame. Would've been nice to know when she saw me asking my toddlers what flavors they wanted.

Fourthly, they were slow. I think they only had 2 employees. Maybe this was a high demand day, maybe someone called in sick. I don't know. In Provo, they have 3, 2 people making the shave ice and one person at the register taking orders. This makes it go pretty fast. It was a bit of a wait at the Meridian location.

Fifthly, I'm not sure how this is possible, but the flavors were just off. They didn't taste as sweet and when I asked for a double sno cap, I'm pretty sure it wasn't a double. We went to the Meridian location on Tuesday and then went to the Provo location on Thursday. I ordered the same thing (and waited to write my review) to make sure it wasn't my imagination. It wasn't. The flavors weren't right. I don't know if it's the ice? Maybe it has a different mineral makeup? I don't know.

Sixthly, the ice cream tasted chalky. I know it's the same as what they use in Provo, but it tasted grainy in Meridian and my lovely ice cream puck didn't melt. My 3 yo managed to drop her shave ice, so I gave her mine and right before we left, I bought myself another one and ate the ice portion on the way home. 20 minutes later in 90 degree weather, my ice cream had just barely started to melt. I couldn't even scoop a spoonful of ice cream. It was like chopping just a little off the top.

Anyway...I had really high hopes to recommend Hokulia to my sister who lives in Boise since we're half Polynesian and grew up in elementary school on Oahu, but...I just didn't like this one. I'll give it another chance during my visit next summer, but for now...major disappointment.
Pricey, not very big portions, and meat is fatty. Best thing was the sauce.

This was by far our least pleasant KOA camping, or heck even all time worst in general, experience we've ever had. 

We are moving cross camping and caravanning with the in laws who have a small camper trailer. A couple days before we were due to arrive in the Boise area, they recommended the KOA. We have a toddler and a tent, and were a little disappointed we couldn't be closer to grandma and grandpa who were traveling, but oh well. They said they'd hold a tent spot for us. 

We arrived and immediately knew that the spot had to be a joke. It had a patch of grass about 2-3' wide, and the asphalt immediately beside it had a picnic table and Babrbeque chained to the spots so we couldn't move it. The rest was gravel that was easily 102° that afternoon. We also noticed that the site was right on the corner of a busy turning spot for the RVs, directly under a super bright street lamp, and right across from the dumpster and bathrooms. Lovely. Looking around, there was another empty tent spot a couple sites down. So we decided to ask up front if we could move. 

When my husband was in the front office, the woman in front of us was checking in when we hear her say, "wait, you didn't give me my 10% discount!" right after putting her card away when it sounded like it was something they had discussed before. The woman at the counter just said, "well, the transaction already went through, nothing I can do now." And the woman was quite upset. We come up and explain our situation. We are a family with a young kid and our larger 8'x8' tent won't fit in the grass spot and it will be hard with a toddler. The front desk woman, Shirley, then says, "oh, well you're not supposed to use the grass, you use the gravel." My husband replied, "you mean the hot 102° gravel?" Which she replied, "it's a special gravel, it's like a cushion." (BTW, it's not). We explained that there was a much larger spot with more grass and shade and away from the street lamp only about 3 spaces down. She tells us that she's reserved that one for another person. My husband brings up that we are there now and they are not, and she just refuses to move us. My husband is upset at the blatant lack of empathy or care the staff have off. 

So we wait until after its dark to hopefully cool down and we put up our tent on the gravel under the sun-bright street lamp. Turns out we can't stake our tent down in the gravel as it bends our stakes. There's only 1-2" of gravel. This SUCKS. There is also a wind store and so here we are with a larger tent in a wind store with a site we can't stake down and under a street lamp that is as bright as day oh, and we had a 2 year old and a cat with us we were moving. Lovely. The spot a couple sites down didn't get anyone in it until 10 that night. Our toddler couldn't go to sleep and kept waking up terrified because the sides of our tent kept blowing in on him because we couldn't stake down our tent. He gravel was so poky and uncomfortable that I couldn't believe you could camp without an air mattress and I was worried about it puncturing our mattress. It hurt too much to even roll my tent up in the morning!

The facility was nice, but the tent camping was ridiculous. The RVs are packed in like sardines, and don't expect more than a 3-4' patch of grass unless you snag a select few of he corner lots. 

The site cost $27 for the night and it wasn't worth half that. If my inlaws weren't with us, we'd rather park in a damn city park and camp that the KOA for tents.

My first choice for breakfast on a Saturday morning! Love everything I've tried here. A few of my personal favs: Eggs Benedict, Garden Hash, Biscuits and Gravy, Poppyseed pancakes, and my absolute favorite thing... THEIR JAM/JELLY. To die for. Staff is always very attentive and helpful. Prices are fair for the quality of food. The environment is small and welcoming. Love Moe Joes!

I'm going to start off saying that I have been to famous Dave's twice before and enjoyed both visits.  I'm starting a new job tomorrow and thought we would celebrate and BBQ sounded good so.....

The atmosphere was off tonight. Someone kept changing the station in the middle of the songs it would vary between pop, country and older pop. It was annoying but nothing too painful. 
We ordered the nachos which were the best part of the entire meal. Our food came and it was just really gross. My husbands food looked like it had been sitting around for awhile and his bread was mushy. My food looked good but by my second bite all I could taste was BBQ sauce, that peppery taste not flavor. I tried my very small portion of mashed potatoes and they tasted like boxed potatoes with garlic salt. I'm done and starting to get irritated that we paid $20 a piece for this meal. What tipped me over the edge was the waitress . She was young and sweet but really inexperienced. She couldn't give us any real tips on what to order and would just be wandering around the djinn groom. She held our bill in her hand while she chatted with some other people for over 5 minutes. 

So now I'm nauseous from the over abundance of pepper sauce, broke and irritated.
Very delicious food here. Great taste, fair price and satisfying. Portions are generous too. No let down on the food here. I bit cold (temperature wise) in the restaurant though. Will be back.
I've been to Kfusion a couple of times. I can't say enough about this restaurant. The service was pretty good, and the food to cost ratio is spot on in my opinion.

We had an amazing experience at Moe Joe's over the Thanksgiving holiday! We had a huge family group--21 people total--descend on the restaurant during prime breakfast time. We only had to wait around 30 minutes for them to seat our group and our server was incredible. She easily took all of our orders, kept our coffee cups full, and happily accommodated every request. The food was amazing, too. Excellent selection and quality. Everyone left full and satisfied! We really appreciated being able to eat together at a delicious local restaurant, and would definitely return again.

Wow what can I say? This is a great place to take care of you skin needs. I finally came to the conclusion that I needed to do something about my bad acne breakouts, I have dealt with acne since I was a teen and now into adulthood.  Staff was friendly and  Stephen is a great doctor, I feel comfortable and cared for when I am there. I usually don't end up waiting that long, combined with seeing the doc paired with the lab visit across the hall its about an hour. No complaints! THANK YOU!

Very similar to cafe rio. I have four stars simply because I believe cafe rio is much better minus how they are cheap on sour cream and guacamole. Food seems to always be fresh which is a big plus. Convenient location. Good chicken
This is the best placeI have eaten in a long time and for sure best thing in Boise! The loco Moco was amazing and the sweet tea was made perfectly.

The $1.50 cinnamon rolls were very fresh and tasty. 
the donut pancake and coffee was creative and delicious. 
The corned beef hash was good but could have been better if it was just a touch less greasy. 
The Fiesta was also creative and a great combination of flavours and could easily be shared by two of us. The smokehouse was very delicious with another combination of flavours highlighted by the tasty smoked sausage. 
The ham and cheese omelet with hash browns on the early bird menu actually stole the show from the more flashy meals with its outstanding freshness and excellent flavors. 
Our service was excellent from the communication by the hostess to our great waitress. 
i will be back.

I absolutely love the Voodoo salad. When I lived in Arizona I frequented that Rumbi Island Grill there so when I moved back to Idaho there wasnt one and I was sad. Then about 2 years ago the Rumbi Grill came here. I must say I was overjoyed. I have gone to this particular location several times and ordered the Voodoo salad each time. I'm not one to try new things once I have found something I like. The prices are a little spendy but the food is so wonderful. I like to take a friend with me when I go.

Tried this place last night. The selection of sushi is huge. Great menu- alit to choose from and reasonable prices - given this is a Japanese sushi/steakhouse. The staff was AWESOME. Place is very clean. Will be back!!!
Second time this week. Chicken and waffles are legit. Better than Roscoe's in LA. Just about to dig in to some of the best sausage gravy ever. Love this place!!
Best sushi in Meridian!! The customer service is amazing. Order any sushi roll & you won't be disappointed. Everyone that's works there makes you feel you are family.

Fresh spring rolls were delicious! Staff was very friendly. Large selection of menu items. I had the spicy chicken. Not the best I've had but still good. Husband had a spicy beef dinner and it was delicious.
Great place and great team.  Bought my ATV & plow and it's been a lifesaver.  The team is knowledgeable and professional.  You won't go wrong.
We had a great family dinner. A full bar made dad happy, a great salad for mom and a great kids menu for the little one. I even got cheesecake to go!

So many places in the area are closing, I feel for Famous Dave's trying to compete with all the new places around.  On the plus side, it wasn't very busy and the service was good.  We hadn't eaten here in a while and found some new items.  We tried these rib bite things that were very good and nicely seasoned.  Our food was cooked great for us, we like things well done; though it was all still tender and moist.  I'm glad we stopped in.

I really enjoyed my lunch at the red Pavillion.  our cha gio pork was good and  the "sinus-clearing mustard" that accompanied it was nice.  It had been years since I had Mongolian beef that was cooked correctly, the beef not swimming in a cornstarch sauce but rather crispy fried with stir-fried onions on a bed of cellophane rice noodles with just a light coating of the teriyaki style sauce. while the beef was very flavorful and texturally appealing, i would have enjoyed some spiciness, and while the dish was decorated with flame-kissed dried, red peppers they did nothing but add decoration to the entree.  the fried rice was also nicely seasoned and they didn't skimp on the veggies in it.  I found the cup of hot and sour soup to be flavorful , but too thick and a tad slimy, a bit too heavy handed on the cornstarch slurry but it still tasted good.  I was also able to try their sweet and sour chicken which I could taste the ginger in the sauce,it was slightly zingy, not my favorite sauce but the chicken was well fried and crispy, would probably try generals tso chicken instead, but not bad.  the staff was efficient and helpful and the food came out quick and hot.  the prices were reasonable and comparable to other Chinese restaurants.  I will definitely come back here again as it was such an enjoyable meal!

We moved to the Boise area from Seattle and this is the best sushi restaurant we have ever been to.  We had the fried oysters, salad with ginger dressing, udon/tempura, and the spicy tuna sushi roll (18 huge pieces)...service and atmosphere was great and the food was perfectly delicious.
This place is great 7.79 for the breakfast buffet plenty of good food and super nice servers I'm only in town a few days and I don't think I will be going anywhere else.
Nice to have Sarah back behind the bar. Great food and drinks as always. Best beer selection in town.

Definitely not impressed with this restaurant, am amazed at all of the good reviews. The pizza was very average  (and I'm a lover of all types of pizza), calzone just OK, and everything was extremely over priced (granted , isn't every place at the Village?)...but 90 bucks for 1 pizza, 1 calzone, 1 salad, 1 glass of wine, and 2 iced teas seems a bit ridiculous...especially when you take into account the mediocre food. Probably will not give it another try.
Exceptional, very good. Great staff, great restaurant. Just read the other reviews.

Pizza was alright.. Not worth the high price. They have the strangest pricing systems.. If u want to split the pizza in half w different toppings in each half, you pay double (full cost of pizza for each half). 

THEY DONT SERVE RANCH. The owner wants to keep it a NY style.. But I believe you need to cater to the customer. Server said people always ask for ranch. Calzone sauce I got to replace it was gross but it was my first time having calzone sauce. 
Great service, beautiful restaurant .. Boo on the price and weird quirks.

For a Red Robin this specific location hits some speed bumps. I believe it's not part of the national chain and appears to be a franchise. This causes some issues as the training doesn't seem to be on par with most Red Robin locations. RR prides itself on stellar wait service with quick touch times and accurate ordering. For what ever reason this location seems much slower on getting to tables quick after you're sat. 

The food is on par with most RR locations and will have some good days and bad days. I enjoy the royal burger here. 

Expect to see a good amount of families here and a family friendly location
Great family atmosphere. Fun lounge for the adults and the food is really good! If you're looking for a great place to take the family, this is it!
I'm mixed with my emotions on this. The caprese salad was nice but the calzone was too full of ricotta and not enough flavor. Pizza was probably a better choice.

Hands down our favorite place in the area. Our family prefers the Alfredo/cream sauce (can't remember what they call it)  to the red sauce. It is absolutely amazing. Hubby and kids usually get pasta and the cream sauce and hubby adds sausage to his. I get the parmesan chicken and then get the cream sauce instead of red sauce on my pasta. My meal comes with a fabulous salad and the fresh bread and olive oil are superb.

Gino's is only slightly pricier than the Olive Garden and is miles above and beyond OG. 

Gino himself is usually there and what a pleasant man who appreciated his customers. Hands down the best restaurant in the area.

Hot n sour soup was disgusting. I usually never complain but it was seriously gross. It tasted like 60% vinegar. I nicely explained this to the waiter but she still charged me for it. The rest of the food was great but they seriously need a new soup recipe and attitude check. I've had about 100 different soups from Chinese and none have tasted this weird and bad.
just about what you expect from Red Robin. Good fries okay burgers.

This is not your typical restaurant food.  Taste just like home cooked.   Cornbread with ever meal.  Super good.  We tryed the fried green tomatoes just because we saw the movie.   And they were as good as a chick flick..  Not sure  I'm supposed to say things like that.. Anyway the spicy ranch dip was very tasty.   But the star of the night goes to the fried chicken and the gravy was Awesome!   I would actually drink the gravy. :)    The is a small neighborhood restaurant with good service.    

The downside.... The sweet tea is good,  but a big beer or a glass of wine would be better..  Or even 2 beers.  Just sayin.   Chicken this good should be offered as takeout.

It did not disappoint!  So good!  The ice was fine and soft, the choice of flavors plentiful, the snow cap cream topping awesome, and the choice of three ice creams (macadamia, coconut, or vanilla) amazing.  The only place I've been to as good as Purple Penguin in Henderson, NV.

Maybe slow down a little. I would gladly wait a bit for a correct order. Ordered three sandwiches... two weren't correct when we arrived home. We added items on to the sandwiches... not sure why they decided not to put any lettuce on. Extra cost for avocado, but could BARELY see a tinge of green and on only one one half of one side of the sandwich. Jimmy johns used to be my favorite ...but they have gotten sloppy and skimpy on ingredients, while still charging the same.

Came in to have a nice dinner with the wife and was sorely disappointed. After sitting at our table and waiting for our food to come out for quite a while I realize me and my wife are both sweating... come to find out the air conditioning is broken and the restaurant is HOT. Finally get our food and my wife's plate which was a plane burger and fries has several random food items scattered in her fries and on the side of her burger. So hot in the restaurant we can't sit and wait for a new plate, poor experience and will never come back to this place.

Probably one of the top 5 breakfast spots in the Boise area. The corned beef hash is my favorite, but I hear the French Toast is to die for. I just can't get past the corned beef hash when I go there. Best service in Idaho and the coffee is gourmet. Get there early on weekends or go late, otherwise you may wait, but it's worth it.

I went to the Divine Wine Bar with a friend of mine. It was the first time visit for the both of us. Someone from Ontario recommend it. It was warm and charming.  Greeted by a friendly server Chantel! It has a wonderful ambiance. The front enter is filled with all types of wines. They had live music and tunes to make you sing along. Our dinner was very tasty!  I will definitely be back. I sat next to a window and got to see the 1st snow fall! Magical! 
I'll be back very soon.
Liza M.

I guess like many other people, I have seen this place and always assumed they were auto battery stores for the most part but as it turns out, I was very wrong. As I've noticed a lot of the "bulb/battery" stores have closed I looked into who  could replace auto key fob batteries and found out these guys do along with a multitude of other specialty batteries. I stopped in, all the guys were great and I had new key fob batteries in 10 minutes. Besides that, their Interstate auto batteries are as good as you can get!

3.5 stars! Went in a group of 6, everyone liked what they ordered. Philly sandwich had good flavor, and I'm picky when I order these! Tater tots were great!! Mom enjoyed her cowboy Sando. Husband enjoyed his Rudy Burger! Only complaints iced tea wasn't the best and the food could have come out faster! Waitress was pleasant and did a good job.

Last Friday morning, we decided to get a quick breakfast burrito and share it before I had to be at work.  We arrived at Los Betos at around 7:45 at the Eagle location.  Ordered our burrito and sat down.  Another two people came in and ordered after us and a bunch of car orders went through and got their food.  All we did was order 1 burrito and those other orders were for a ton of food and we sat and watched them happily go on their way.  We had to wait a full 30 minutes before our burrito came up.  The guy that got his burrito ahead of us (he ordered way after) said that we should get our food for free.  If I had been working there, that's what I would have done.  The food is still great, but I will say that they need to do something about their service.

I love me some good burritos and in the Boise area, Los Betos is usually the place to go. The only complaint I have about this specific Los Betos is, it's hit and miss. When you get good food, it's really good, but when you miss, the steak is dry and the the fries in your burrito are soggy. 
The Los Betos in Caldwell and the one on State street are consistently tasty. And this particular Los Betos can be great... or not so much. Depends on the day I guess.
Amazing breakfast place. Corned beef hash is house made along with most everything else on the menu. Great service too.

Consistent, excellent customer service across the nation! My grumpy pants was greeted by several "Good Mornings" and friendly faces and the smell of fresh popcorn wafted through the room ... at 8 AM My car is newer so it doesn't even have Les Schwab tires on it... yet my service was free! Why would anyone go anywhere else to buy tires or to just get assistance? I haven't had the need to do price comparisons, but if LS was the more expensive choice, it would be well worth the price. They took the grump right out of me!

Great coffee and fast drive thru. Wish I had one here in AZ but will definitely enjoy stopping by when in town. I had a hot camel macchiato and it was perfect. Their sizes are huge also. Enjoy and thank you
My tacos tasted like spring rolls from Panda Express, not necessarily a bad thing just wasn't what I was expecting

Dr Mark and his staff are amazing! We brought in our new rescue dog from the ahumane Society for a checkup and he was SO thorough and took extra time to let us ask all our questions and guide us through this new adventure with our fur baby. They are incredible. They will be our vet for life. A+++

Food is consistently good. Have options for large and small fresh made tortillas with white or wheat. Sweet pork salad is my favorite and a large portion. I just get the small with tomatillo ranch dressing on the side. Great for lunch or dinner.
Best biscuits and gravy I've ever tasted. No frills restaurant but tasty and reasonably priced.

Three words. Biscuits and Gravy. 

This place is busy but well worth the wait. The staff is friendly and the food is phenomenal.
Best authentic food in the area! Try to speak Spanish and it goes a long way.

Gino's lives up to the hype and reputation. Excellent quality food in a pleasant atmosphere. I had simmered lamb shank, and wife had seafood lasagna. Daily special prices are high, but you get what you pay for, and this means chef-prepared cuisine of superior quality.

I was in town on a three week business trip. A co worker took me here. If I could rate it 3.5 stars, I would here is my review.

PROS: 

- Good beer selection. Had lots of local beers. Didn't have Kokanee, but a lot of other places didn't have it either.

- The Nachos were good. I didn't order them I tried them from someone else. 

CONS:

- Pretty busy. This may be a good thing. It was busy both times I went there and the parking is kinda hard.

- I had the turkey club. It came with massive amounts of pork and bacon. I am not a fan. 

I would go here again. This is a safe bet.

I'm a big fan of Famous Dave's. The atmosphere is great and I personally feel that the food just edges out Goodwood, though you can't go wrong with either one. If you are looking for good BBQ in the Boise/Meridian area you cant go wrong with Daves!

This sports pub really knows how to cater to the fans.

First... they have a nice patio where the smokers can still go an puff on their tobacco.  Cheers!

Second, they have lots of screens, and if your game isn't on, they will try to find a screen just for you.

Finally, the prices are good (Pitcher of PBR just $5 last night) and the wings are amazing.
Good food and service but a very limited beer selection. If you are looking for a micro brew to drink with your meal this not the place.

Wonderful and attentive service. Ordered veggie hash with no eggs and no cheese. The veggies were doused in a little too much oil for my liking. Got a box for leftovers and after a few hours the oil had drenched the box and made it floppy. 

Seems like a nice little place though, I would give this restaurant another shot and try something else if I ever was in town again.

Best breakfast place in Boise HANDS DOWN! So happy we live so close to it. Any of their hash dishes are off the charts. We do the smokehouse but instead of sausage we get chorizo. They do mimosas too. Best place ever!!

When I left the restaurant, I was prepared to give it just two stars. However, the food was good enough that I am willing to forgive the terrible (lack of) service, and the fact that I had to secure napkins, chopsticks and wasabi for our 3-person party. Walking into a sushi-boat facility starving is the best way to go. Instant gratification with relatively great sushi (face it: there are not many good sushi joints in the Treasure Valley). The downfall for me was when I was chatting with our sushi maker/manager, who was quite busy, and noticing him serving what appeared to be his friends the newest sushi. That was forgivable, until my boyfriend asked him for some Sirachi sauce for his Nigiri and the manager was short with him, saying, "I'm kind of busy here." So, as has been said in other reviews, they appear understaffed or simply unprepared for how popular they are. After the rush, the manager did come over and make nice  with us. Oh, one downfall: the sake (salmon) was chewy and sinewy. As a obsessive salmon/sake eater, I was quite disappointed. They didn't take it off my bill, but they did say they would compensate me next time I came in. Which I definitely will! For a nice spicy tuna roll, a few different tasty sauces, and the joy of plucking little goodies of the sushi boats, I will definitely be back. A few flaws are forgivable.

Wow! Stopped by after hitting up the Farmer's Market, and was pleasantly surprised by how many people were there. 80% of the seating was taken, but there was only a 5 minute wait to be seated, and it was so worth it!

The Two Egg Breakfast is fantastic! Great portion size (she didn't even finish it), and the Veggies on the Round was amazing. When they say "The Lighter Side" on the menu, they mean it, but even though the portions are small the ingredients justify the price.

Our waitress was friendly and funny, the food was hot, and the atmosphere was cozy, but we could still have a private conversation. The only downside was that the wait between ordering and serving was a bit lengthy. Still worth it, just be prepared for a bit of conversation before your food.

Both of us were full, with half a slice of today and a fried egg left on our plates after the meal.

Always friendly, great drinks!

I just wish they (Dutch Bros) would have those cardboard wraps to make it easier to hold without getting so hot.
The food here is amazing! Everything I have tried has been delicious! If you come for breakfast on the weekends be prepared for a wait! It is worth it though! The homemade jam is  wonderful!

We stopped in after searching Yelp for a good breakfast joint while waiting for our RV to be serviced. So glad we tried Moe Joe's. I had half plate of Eggs Benedict and one pancake. The best Eggs Benedict I've ever had! So good! My hubby had the breakfast burrito with ranchero sauce, which is HUGE and equally amazing! A HUGE high five to our kind waitress who came up behind me, covered me and whispered my skirt was tucked in. You saved me some major embarrassment. So thank you!!! Highly recommend for delicious food and awesome service.
Tastes good but always leaves me not feeling that great after I eat it if you know what I mean!

My husband and I went to the BBQ cooking class given every Thursday at 6 pm. We had an amazing time. The staff was knowledgeable about barbecue and smoking. We discussed indirect and direct cooking, cooking with wood chips, cedar plates, etc. At the end, there was enough food for the 20+ people attending the class. We had biscuits, roasted chicken, tri tip, pork, butternut squash, potatoes, etc. all cooked during the class. Best part? Only $5 per person and you get that in a credit for the store. Amazing experience and we will do it again soon!

This is by far our family's favorite Chinese take-out place. We've tried many others in town. Joy Garden gives you the most for your dollar, by far. We have never had anything that we don't like from here. The service is great, too. There is never more than a 15 min wait for food when we eat in or take-out.

New location in Meridian is great.  Make a reservation or you may be turned away.   Food is great I love the Polo Maria.  I see Gino in the kitchen allmost every time I go there.  Most of the staff from the downtown Boise location is there.  I usally get to go orders and have two meals as portions are generous.  The menu is a phone book so lots to choose from.  This is how dinning should be.

We tried Moe Joe's for the first time last week.  There was an ad in one of the circulars that came in the mail and what was appealing was the fact that they did an Early Bird breakfast menu for $6 which is from 7A-10A.  It's a limited menu with around 6 items on it but my husband and I both ordered from it and had bacon, eggs, and a pancake.  My husband ordered the special cranberry and pecan pancake and payed a little extra for it.  My son ordered Huevos Rancheros.  The pancakes were good and crispy on the edges.  Our eggs were scrambled and done just right.  The Huevos Rancheros consisted of a tortilla, pulled pork, black beans, eggs fried, and salsa.  I had a bite and it was really good and my son really enjoyed it. They also serve Dawson Taylor coffee which to my mind is the best.

The only part of this meal that I didn't enjoy was the fact that I had to wear my coat during the meal.  It was a very frigid day, and the restaurant has a bank of windows at the entrance, and no barrier near the door, so whenever anyone came in or out, there was a gust of cold air that came in.  Not very comfortable in a dining environment.  I probably wouldn't go back here until the weather warms up.  

I think however, that this place is a nice addition to the large business park of El Dorado and it's a place that workers could come to for a nice breakfast or lunch.
Their sandwiches were so good. Very fresh and the service was quick and super friendly. The fresh bread they use makes it a perfect sandwich.
Definitely the best Chinese restaurant in the treasure valley.  Everything is cooked fresh when you order.  Awesome dishes.  A must try!!

Family favorite spot for burrito and salad. Location is very convenient (nearby my house), lots of parking, clean restaurant, always busy, very family-oriented. Sweet pork is the best choice; burrito when you are hungry, or small salad when you want to eat light.

I had the privilege of having Jordan doing my hair and she is amazing. I have really difficult hair (grey) and she has so much talent that she was able to deal with my hair. Jordan is so talented that you are lucky to even get in with her.

I love me some Korean food. Not a big variety in Boise. This is as close as it gets to an Americanized version of Korean food. Japchea (clear noodles) is my fav and their lunch combo menu is a good option. Can't give it more than 3 stars because I know how authentic Korean food tastes like. It's spicier and more flavorful than the Americanized version. When Ill get the real deal, I'll give it 5 stars. Until then, I'm very happy with their food as is

I'm the easiest sort of customer, so long as you're honest and capable. I came into Snake River Yamaha with the product (a Yamaha Zuma 50F) that I wanted to purchase already in mind, no convincing needed. All that they needed to do was show me the product that I wanted so that I could finalize my decision. I was told that they would have one on the showroom floor ready for me to assess. When I arrived, they had the wrong model, and wrong year of scooter on the showroom floor. They then proceeded to try and sell me that product.

I left the dealership with the promise that they would order one for me that afternoon (after I paid a $500.00 down payment) and that it would arrive the following Tuesday (I ordered it on a Friday). Tuesday is here, and I've been informed that the scooter won't be available until Thursday at the earliest.

My time spent with this dealership has left me feeling...dirty. As if the sales people are incompetent, and as if they were trying to pull the wool over my eyes for profit. I even had to bring to their attention that they hadn't offered me the promotional "6 months interest free" that's easily visible on their very own website. I gave them two stars solely for the fact that the sales person (Jeremy) mentioned in passing that he might give me a gift card toward the purchase of a helmet or gloves.

I would not do business with them again.
Great place, Good food, Unique options, No MSG and very nice staff! My family and I will definitely be back. Really nice back patio with good shade and environment.

Fantastic all around! Courteous waitress, who is the daughter of the owners/chefs. The food was so delicious and full of flavor. The Nu Flavor Rolls were so yummy and a great way to start the dinner. The gumbo was crazy good, but the cornbread was my favorite. I am a southern girl, so cornbread and I go way back, and that cornbread was awesome. My husband and I are excited to go back and try some of the other things on their menu.
Best Chicken Fried Steak ever - huge portions! Had to package up half of it. Nicely decorated - we went early mid week so no wait for us. Great sevice!
Even owning a automotive repair shop myself, I still do all my tire business here. Top notch management and customer services. If you go anywhere else, your over paying.

Made an appt. to get new tires. Was assured  twice it would only take 45 minutes. Took off work, 1 hour 30 minutes later they tell me I'm next up. Tell your customers the truth. I would have dropped the car off. I made an appt., but they worked on other cars during that time. Very frustrated at Discount Tire.

The sushi was really good and the servers and chefs are really nice, really nice atmosphere, I give it two stars because of the service. It took forever for us to get our drinks, and even longer to get our order in.  The place is really cramped. If you want to actually eat, I suggest sitting at the bar on the left side when you first walk in. Otherwise, you will have to wait for the food to come around to you, by then the boats will be empty, and you don't have a chance of grabbing what you want, the chefs only like to refill the boats on the left. Our order was forgotten three different times. We kept having to ask the waitress where our food was.
My friend and I didn't eat much, because it took so long to get our food, we were tired of waiting, the other customers around us were getting frustrated as well for the same reasons. 
Other than all of that, the waitresses were really sweet, and nice. The chefs were nice. The food was good. I guess you just have to go when they are slow and can actually give you attention. I'll give this place another try..
Service was a bit slow. They have remodeled the store. Felt like burger was smaller than normal. Fries are always good and bottomless. Fun atmosphere. Tvs are on sports channels.
Delicious!  Biscuits and gravy were best we've had in a long time. The Bfast burrito was really good chimichanga style. Will come back again.
Very good. Had the cinnamon waffles. Potatoes were great. Staff friendly. Restrooms clean.

Gino's is a restaurant I would normally turn my nose up at. It is located in a relatively new strip mall and feels very cookie-cutter. It still had a spacious, comfortable atmosphere and looked like it might have a pretty patio, but it was hard to tell from inside. We went with a family party of around 10 people.

Food:
Fairly standard Italian fare. They do need to trim their menu by about a hundred items, there are so many similar offerings it's difficult to decide. The food was good but not spectacular. You are provided with mediocre bread at the table, with dipping oil which is very garlicky and quite good. We asked our server three times for extra bread which never showed up. 

I was quite blown away by their generosity with ingredients. There must have been twenty + shrimp on my pasta, a heaping pile of artichokes and sundried tomatoes, things frequently skimped on. My boyfriend's lasagna came with about an inch deep of melted cheese, and then they offer you even more parmesan on top. It is annoying though that you have to pay extra for a salad when you're paying $25 for a plate of pasta.

Service:
As mentioned above, we had a larger party of ten, so some lapses are totally forgivable. However it was a slow Tuesday night and we felt they could have been a bit more attentive, especially with the bread situation. 
The food did come out quickly. The guests were served in almost backwards order - youngest male to eldest female, which was disconcerting, especially as we had several seniors in our party. The server also misheard my mother's order and then argued with her about it, rather than simply fixing the situation. Argued! None of us were clear on how he heard "eggplant parmigiana" as "ham pizza". So she suffered through a rather blah pizza rather than deal with him anymore.

In all the food was decent, the service was unimpressive, and the location was blah. If you're looking for a convenient cookie cutter restaurant it might work.

I would give five stars for the food but the service was lacking. We were seated promptly with a quickly served appetizer but when our server took our order, she was too rushed and didn't take time to ensure we were communicating. We wanted to substitute fried rice for steamed rice and ended up getting both -- charged for a full order of fried rice. Ordered Fu Yong (best I've ever had) -- server asked what meat (she recited all the options) we wanted; I asked if that was an extra charge and she said no it was included. We ordered shrimp then were charged a dollar. Our bill was $8-10 more than we expected. Could have been avoided if the server had not been so rushed to take our order and asked for clarification of what we were ordering. Also, we ordered honey lemon chicken and received lemon lime chicken. We kept the lemon lime chicken--it was delightful! Again--awesome food -- frustrating service experience.

This is THE go-to place for Chinese food in Meridian!  The food is delicious, the service spot on, and the dining atmosphere is clean and modern.  Oh and you gotta love those crispy, flaky chips and sweet sauce dip that is served when you first arrive!  Sort of like the Chinese version of chips and salsa! :)  

My only suggestion to them is to offer delivery.  I spoke to the manager about getting signed up for GrubHub.com and she took note.  When you visit, be sure to mention it so we can get that good stuff delivered!

Stopped here for lunch and had a salad that my mom had recommended...had their shredded beef salad. They gave me a plate covered by a tortilla then some rice and beans and a generous portion of greens topped with shredded beef, guacamole and a small scoop of salsa and sour cream.  Topped it off with a lime cilantro dressing...was delicious!  Perfect combination of Mexican food and salad...satisfied my craving for both without making me feel heavy and full the way Mexican food often does.  I only tried the salad, but my sister and dad tried two different burritos and both were satisfied with their choices as well.  If you are in the mood for Mexican food but don't want to feel bloated and heavy after eating it, head to Costa Vida and get one of their salads!

The service and atmosphere was good, but the food was marginal.  I ordered the veal parmesan and it was so tough it required a steak knife to cut it, normally I use just a fork.  I suspect the waiter knew it would be tough because he brought me the steak knife without me asking.  My wife ordered seafood raviolis and they were extremely fishy, plus the two shrimp that came with it were rubbery.  The portions were small and the prices were high.  I doubt we will go there again even though they are in walking distance from home.

If I could give 10 stars to this place, I absolutely would - and it's pretty hard to impress me when it comes to vets. 

I am a positive reinforcement dog trainer and the major appeal of this place was their claim of being a "fear free" facility. 

They backed that claim in spades. I walked in and there was none of the normal cacaphony of a regular veterinarian waiting room. They get the animals into exam rooms as soon as possible so as to minimize stress from interactions and possible reactivity with other animals. The lowest pane of glass in each exam room is opaque so although the people can see out, the animals cannot unless they are Newfoundlands, Berners, Great Pyrenees or other ginormous breeds. 

The vet techs there are awesome. Each was incredibly compassionate and gentle. No one was pushy with my dog - to be fair, I've spent a lot of time training her so she's pretty solid at the vet, but even still - they weren't rough at all like I've seen at some other places.
