Careful because if you are not looking for it closely you could easily pass by it and that would be a shame. 

I came at the tail end of their lunch hours but was greeted nonetheless with a warm welcome.  Bob Marley music was at a nice volume and really set the mood for what would be a really nice experience. I mean who doesn't like Marley, right?

I ended up ordering a Korean taco which I know sounds strange for a soul food place. And a shrimp Po Boy sandwich with a salad instead of fries and their house sesame dressing. Topped it off with a sweet tea. 

The Korean taco was really good and even better was the jalapeño sauce that came with it. The meat was flavored just right and if I didn't have a sando coming I could've easily had three more. 
The salad was one of my favorite things traditional but has crunchy fried onions on top and with that house dressing I could've seriously just dunked straight veggies in it, it's that good. 
The sweet tea is very sweet and was missing the traditional lemon wedge on the top to make it truly southern in this humble gal's opinion but no worries ask and you shall receive!  I was brought a couple of wedges on the side. I am sure if I would've added more ice it would've been perfect! 
The Shrimp PO boy sandwich was great and served with a lemon wedge but was missing hot sauce to add as an option when I asked for hot sauce options I was offered tapatio or cholula...what?? Which would be my only real criticism. A soul food place should have either a signature hot sauce or a wall of hot sauces that are typical to the style of cooking. Not to worry I always make the best of what I've got. I had some of the jalapeño sauce left over from my taco and tried it on the sandwich and BOOM!! It was awesome! So with another side of that sauce it transformed my shrimp po boy from good to the bomb!  Yeah I think I've said it before I like my stuff spicy. ;-)

Curtis was an amazing server!! He refilled my drink at the right times, answered questions to the best of his knowledge and checked on my status often.  I will definitely be returning to Shanaz for some more of its soul!! Yes!

Portions are big, the food is always yummy, and the staff are nice. There's always a wait, but it's worth it! The hot chocolate comes with toasted marshmallows on top, and my dad loves their rye bread.

For Mother's Day this year I told my hubby that I wanted my favorite coffee... and a steak breakfast burrito from Los Betos! I'm totally serious. He got me what I asked for and I had an amazing Mother's Day breakfast. 

The steak aka carne asada breakfast burrito is my favorite for breakfast. On normal days that I swing thru the drive through I either get a bean and cheese burrito or their new Idaho Burrito. It's a spin on the California burrito (which is good as well). Meat, cheese, fries/potato, sour cream, guac and salsa goodness. It's the best!  

No place is perfect and I've had an experience here and there that didn't blow me away. Over cooked eggs once, and today I was almost half way thru my burrito before I saw any sour cream and guacamole. It was still a delicious dinner and I'll be back again soon!

BIg bomb arse burritos! I had the carnitas burrito and it was very good. Hey, it's not the cleanest or nicest place (think taco truck in a building)  but decent food at a good price (giant 2 meal burrito $5.25). Also, they are open 24hrs.

Bought a used class A rv from Bish's sight unseen on the internet.  It was exactly how they described it.  The real surprise was how great we where treated.  In addition to having great communication with us via email and phone, they spent an entire day with us showing us how to use the rv, they picked us up at the airport, and the next day when we had questions, they sent a tech out to our campsite to answer them.

There are lots of horror stories about buying rv's online, but Bish's did an excellent job with us and I would bet they treat all their customers as well as they treated us.

My boyfriend and I decided to finally go to the Grimaldi's in Meridian. 3 days ago we ate at the original in Brooklyn and that was probably unfortunate for the sake of this review... But hey, we knew it wouldn't be the same. And the Meridian spot does do what they can to recreate it, but it would have been a lot closer if their team didn't mess up 3 toppings...not 1. But 3. And it was 3 o'clock on a Tuesday...

In Brooklyn, we asked for a large (red sauce) with pepperoni, meatball, garlic, extra sauce and extra basil.

In Meridian, we ordered the exact same, except sausage instead of meatball and added green peppers.

What we got? A large...red sauce... pepperoni, sausage, green pepper....no basil. They comped the basil and all was well. Then we got our bill. We ended up getting charged for...extra mozzarella? No extra sauce? Plus they already forgot the basil?

Okay, we are specific about what we want, but the bottom line is that if they didn't absolutely botch what we asked for, then the 3 stars could have easily been 5. 

We weren't expecting the same exact thing as the Grimaldi's in Brooklyn. In fact, we prepared to be extra courteous in our critiques due to that. But the attention to detail here...made the pretty good pizza alright.
The BEST cornbread in town, the best fried cat fish, gumbo and cheese grits!  Love, love this place 10 stars.  Gumbo is available Friday and Saturdays.  Yummy
Good sandwiches, I get the #9. They also have good veggie sandwiches too, my wife loves those! The sandwiches are done VERY quickly, happy friendly people that work there.

Preeeetty tasty!  I still miss Casanova, but this is pretty good.  Their location and general ambiance, however, would probably bring me here over the old Casanova.  Sat in their enclosed patio, heat lamps overhead kept us warm, if not hot.  Waitress was kind enough to turn one off so we didn't feel like rotisserie chickens the whole time, and temperature felt perfect after the fact.  Ordered a small caesar salad to start (large enough to feed 2-3), white sangria (peachy and delicious!), and a large garden with pepperoni, all good.  Waitress was kind, helpful and accommodating.  Will definitely be back!
I almost hate to say this, as this restaurant is already so busy... but this place is fantastic! Delish! I have had several items on the menu and all have been so good. Never disappointed.

Well worth the wait all the food coming out of the kitchen looked great. The wife and I both had the rotisserie chicken salad with the basil vinaigrette dressing and it was delicious. Decent serving size.

We have a Weim and she has had some issues for years. I've taken her to the vet so many times for the same issue. Dr. Roth was able to help her and not charge me for a fortune for unnnessisary tests. We still did tests but resonable test. He took the time to actually listen and think about what the problem could be! I'm so grateful for his help. Go there see Dr.Roth:)

FOOD:
I am under the impression that they have 2 menus: a menu book with more "Americanized" offerings (for lack of a better word) and a 1-pager with more authentic food with the names written in Chinese. I've been here 2x, was always given both menus, and always ordered from the 1-pager.
I'm a huge spicy food eater and have been missing spicy boiled fish. Lo and behold, this place has it! I enjoyed it very much. I've had their Szechuan spicy chicken, cumin beef, and mapo tofu. All good!
Cut down 1 star because of the limited selection, hopefully they'll expand the 1-pager menu to multiple pages!!!

PLACE/AMBIANCE:
Nice, modern decor. They have booths and regular tables. Seems like they have enough space for larger groups as well. Ample parking spaces.

SERVICE:
The servers were friendly and attentive, but it's nothing to write home about. But I'll personally take great food & average service over the opposite any day!

You will not find any stream-lined, simple food here.  Everything on this menu has been extremely thought out and home made.  You can definitely tell that Shanaz really enjoys, and is extremely good at her cooking.  

First off, I want to say that the staff was very composed, since a half our after it opened, there were only a couple tables left open.  They were nice and courteous, even with the influx of people.  You can definitely tell by how many people were there at that time of day, there was something about this restaurant.

When my family first arrived here, we were surprised at the menu selections.  There were American staples, but with Shanaz's own flair.  Just think hamburgers stuffed with white cheddar, peanut butter sandwiches deep fried in waffle batter, and even fries seasoned with salt and a light touch of creole seasoning.  My 2 year old and my picky 4 year old were extremely happy about the trip.  

Then there is their appetizers.  You have common southern appetizers like fried green tomatoes, then you have Shanaz's own Korean Tacos.  Yes, they aren't southern, and a little small, but the flavor is spectacular.  The meat has an intense Korean flavor balanced perfectly by a Korean slaw that makes the whole experience worth everything.

Finally their main courses are also spectacular.  I suggest going with the whole southern experience and getting the southern flair.  I had the sable butter shrimp, which was full of flavor and perfectly balanced on top of a perfectly fried mashed potato cake with cooked corn stewed in this sweet seasoned sauce that my wife and I couldn't get enough of.  My wife had the jambalaya stuffed pepper which brought  what it stated on a bed of even more jambalaya.  My wife says she was "in bliss".  It was perfectly seasoned, which many people who have tried creole and southern food know it is extremely hard to do. 

Then there was the corn bread.  Just imagine a perfect corn bread, creamy with the slight texture from the course corn meal, slightly sweet, cooked and served in its own cast iron skillet.  It was much better than anything I have made.  My wife said it was the best part, especially dipped in the remaining liquid from the cooked corn.  

Overall, if you are looking for a home-cooked, meal, much different than the staple foods you get around Boise, and especially food with a southern, "Shanaz" twist,  then this is the best place you can go.  

By the way, the whole time I was there (after I ordered), I was drooling over the gumbo from the next table.  I've never seen a more beautifully displayed gumbo with an aroma just as beautiful.  That right there is what is going to bring me back to Shanaz.

By far the best pizza outside of Italy that we have ever tasted! The pizza Margherita is authentic!
The service we had was impressive!  We will make this our pizza place from now on! Tuesday is 1/2 off wine day!

We ate at this restaurant tonight for the first time. The couple we were with have eaten here numerous times & really enjoy it.

We had rez. for 6 PM and were seated promptly. The restaurant was probably 90% full. We were given water & bread within about 5 minutes. Out waiter appeared about 5 minutes later & took our drink orders. Wine by the glass cost between $6-$10. The $6 house Merlot & Chard were worth the money. We each had two glasses.

One of my favorite Italian dishes is Veal Marsala so I usually order it at a new restaurant. Big mistake! The waiter asked if I wanted it "sweet" or "dry". I said sweet. The two veal cheeks were tender but they had been heavily breaded & were not very flavorful. The sauce was a bit too "sweet", clear and lacked flavor. The best Veal Marsala I've had in this area was at Asiago's. I prefer a darker sauce made with a fine Marsala.

My wife's shrimp dish was very good, she said. Prices were about what I expected. The shrimp dish was about $17 & the veal was about $21. 

The owner came by twice to say "Hi" and asked how we were doing, etc.

Service was fine but the food was average. Will probably stick with Asiago's for Italian.

How else can you rate this place but a 5 star!  Awesome concept, with terrific flavors and a great staff.  Not only have I been a customer many times here but I have also held some customer appreciation parties here with 50-80 people showing up within a few hour window and all the staff were super helpful with their samples and making my customers feel super welcome.  Thank you everyone at U-Swirl for being an awesome business and always being super helpful.  Your staff rocks and you are my go to place for a frozen treat.

So excited for Idaho to finally have a self-serve fro-yo shop! One of the biggest things my family missed from Cali. Note to others: the price is by weight so you are in complete control of the cost of your cup. I would like to see more tart flavors but the ones I'd cut seem to be a big hit with the others I see visiting the establishment. Good variety of fruit toppings.

Overall good food...better than most in the Valley.  My staple measure is the potstickers...I had them steamed...and they were kinda mushy and bland.  Looking forward to going back to try some other items and see how they measure up.

The mimosas here are amazing with different flavors to choose from. Customer service is great with friendly staff.  I had the Irish Benedict and husband enjoyed the chicken fried steak; both were pleasing and delicious.

I have posted reviews before regarding the inconsistent experience with my local Red Robin.  This update pertains to their curbside.  I have often found their takeout option to be okay.  Usually my order is correct, though not always, and normally the customer service is fine.  Since I've been using the curbside, I have not had a good experience.  The estimated time is always way off.  So, I end up sitting in the parking lot.  When I call to let them know I've arrived, they usually sound annoyed and often forget about me; forcing me to call multiple times.  The person that usually comes to the car if fine.  My orders are usually correct about fifty percent of the time.  My advice is to go inside to get your order and check it before you leave.
Okay service. Always have to ask again for condiments ordered on the side; they never come out with the food. Great food. Huge differences in service depending on who you get.

This is our family favorite.  They are always upfront about the wait time, instead of some other places that will tell you the delivery will be there in 30 min, only to take two hours.  Pizza is always tasty.  Thanks.

This may be my favorite restaurant. My wife and I have been here on many occasions and we are never disappointed. This is true authentic Italian food. I would recommend a dish but everyone I've had has been great. The atmosphere here is nice and the service is always there when you need them. Nothing negative here. Go try this place.

It is worth the wait. Yes the location is weird and you may have to sit in a little cramped area watching others eat, but still...  it's worth the wait. The food is amazing. That's really it. Get the Irish Benedict, or the Farmhouse. Worth it. Totally worth it.

I came in on a Thursday evening and there was hardly anyone there. That worried me, however my fears were abated once I was served the food. The all you can eat sushi bar was too pricy for me ($24),so I chose a different option. My wife got the beef bulgogi and I got the pork bulgogi, which we shared. Each dish had unique flavors and both were amazing.! The pork was spicy and tasty. The beef had a mild spice but the flavor really popped. 
Brown rice was available a long with fried rice. I found the fried rice incredibly bland and wouldn't recommend it. The rice was a sushi rice which was sticky and unusual, but I like it.

The side dishes were really good too. They had a spiced cucumber which was really good. It took courage for my wife to be willing to try it, but once she did she loved it.

Like with any foreign food, I can't make any statements about whether or not the food was "authentic", but I can tell you it tasted good. The staff was friendly and the atmosphere is nice.

Visit was on December 26th, at noon. 

Food was just okay, and service was poor.

Service: We were asked by two different servers what we wanted to drink, both brought them out at different times. Turns out they're not servers, nor do they clear the table. One guy kept going to the podium to check his phone. Not sure of their titles. 

Food: Complimentary wonton chips and sweet sour was served, which we enjoyed. Hard to screw that up in my opinion. 

Service: I asked both the initial drink takers about a menu item, and they both told me they would ask the waitress. We finally see the waitress who then proceeds to take orders from a three top that was seated long after us, as well as rushed to take a to go order when the phone rang. We know it was a to go order since we were sat next to the podium and could hear. We raised our hand, as if to signal..helllooo..and she then acted shocked that we were ready to order. Neither of the boys must have asked her my question since she never answered. Go figure, the three top was served before us, and I'm sure the to go order was ready before ours as well. 

Food: We ordered the triple double for $26. It includes an appetizer, two soups, and two entrees. I was excited for the price that we'd get to try several items. We got the two spring rolls (forgot to take a pic). Would not order again. Super oily and the insides were all mushy, i didn't even finish my one small roll. We ordered the hot & sour and the egg drop soups. Both were good, but nothing that warranted a trip there for soups. Turns out they were the best items we'd have there! Ordered sesame beef and generals chicken with fried rice and steamed white rice. Both rice bowls were bland, had to add soy sauce. The beef and chicken dishes tasted so similar, color and sesame seeds are what told us the difference. The batter was good, but it was very hard to find the meat in either dishes. We asked for spicy, which there was no spice whatsoever ever! Disappointed. Several of the larger chunks were just batter, which of course was gross when bitten into. When we would find one with meat, honestly, it did taste good. It was very disappointing because looks wise, the food should have been amazing!! 

Overall, if we do go back, we'd order to go so we aren't disappointed in the very poor service. We would also order one dish, and it would be of non-fried/battered food to confirm we are getting meat...

I came here for a company dinner. The service was good, nothing to write about there. The food however, is a different story. I ordered the lobster ravioli. It was cold and tasted bland and frozen. Not what I expected from a $26 entree. I am not a rude person and it wasn't my money, so I resisted the urge to send it back, although it was  tempting. My coworker was not as shy and sent back her steak because it was so bad. Maybe they were having an off night or aren't good at accommodating larger groups. I know I won't return. I mean..it's in a strip mall....
Good food and friendly owners. This has been my go to place when iam not able to cook dinner ;-)

Been here numerous times and have always had good service and good food. Matter a fact all the wait people that have help us have been excellent.  But who's Einstein idea was it to serve popcorn in a basket full of holes?? It leaks out I'll over the table and if you're one of those that puts salt on your popcorn, well there it is all over the table now. I've seen people drizzle a sauce on their popcorn, you want that all over the table too. Seriously, this such a bad idea and the ones getting the crappy end of this deal is gonna be the wait staff trying to clean it up. Go back to the bowls that should never have gone away.
The wings were fair at best and the mixed drinks were poorly made.  If you want great wings this is not the place!

Great breakfast, from the Dawson Taylor Coffee to the bacon-jalapeno fried chicken benedict.  I would travel from Boise to the Eagle/Overland location. This place competes with Goldy's and Café de Paris, my two favorite downtown spots. If you live in Meridian or West Boise, this should be your breakfast spot. Joe Boyd (former owner of Joe Momma's) has another hit on his hands. Great job Joe!

Red Robin has really shrunk the size of their burgers. Paying around 11 or 12 for a burger and I expect a big burger. The last time I was there I thought the size of it was a joke, if they did not have free refills on fries I would have left super hungry.

Pretty great enchiladas y tacos camarones!  Great service from friendly staff.  Quick and easy order and food came out fresh, hot and accurate.  Freshly made tortillas are hella good here... hope it was as good for you as it was for me!

I was scheduled for a haircut last Sunday. As I was driving to my appointment the salon called me and said that my stylist was still with a previous client and couldn't do my hair that day after all and that she would be with that same client until close which was 3 hours after my scheduled time...they asked if I could reschedule for the following weekend and receive 20% off. I thought that seemed fair, even though it was inconvenient for me to have already gotten a babysitter and left the house for my appointment. Today I was supposed to go in for my appointment, 30 min before my scheduled time they called again and told me her previous client was going over time and asked if they could push me back again. I told her I had already rescheduled for the same reason and I did not want to again and she said that they were sorry. That was it. I will not be going back. I don't appreciate being treated like my appointment does not matter.

This is my second time here at the KOA in Boise and pulled up no reservations which my bad on my part but luckily somebody had just canceled .
the owner said hey I remember you  it was several years ago .
I was surprised He remembered giving Me a ride to the Restaurant.
the owner takes a lot of pride in their property and it shows 
it's nice to have a mature tree and a picnic table and even a little bit of grass to rest by after hours on the road.

We are visiting my MIL and while I am usually leery of ordering BBQ outside of the states known for their outstanding "Q" they wanted to go here. For the most part was pleasantly surprised. We were seated promptly and drink orders taken. I loved my Dave's rum punched with grilled pineapple, my MIL's martini was just the way she likes them, dirty with extra olives. We ordered the trash can and after a bit of a wait it was delivered. The greats were the corn muffins, straight out of the oven, also the ribs, chicken, slaw and beans. The ribs were meaty and well cooked with still a little bite to them. The chicken well seasoned, moist and flavorful. The slaw, which I am normally not a fan of was really good with a nice kick to it. The beans were worthy of note as well. The ok's were the fries and corn, the fries while cooked well were to salty and I do love salt but this was too much, and the corn was past it's prime. The not so great was the brisket it was dry and didn't look fresh sliced, a little gray looking to boot.
The array of sauces was impressive and I tried them all, not surprising I guess was I liked the Texas version best, the Carolina was good as well as the sweet and tangy.

This was a fun place lots to look at, attentive staff, and how many other places serve you off a trash can lid. All in all very good!

This is a first for me with any Discount Tire. Referring to the location on Eagle in Meridian only... They're service is terrible. We sat ignored.. not unseen. Just ignored. Apparently they have all the business they want, and any new business is just too much of a burden.
Great breakfast and friendly customer service!! Their stuffed hash browns and sour dough toast are AMAZINGGG!! Definitely recommend for your morning meal

Great beer choices and the staff is friendly and helpful. If you Like beer download the digital pour app and check out the great selection. Cool big round bar with plenty of TV's. I've only eaten a few times and it's been good. It's locally owned and operated and they care about service

Comfort food at it's best, we had about 10 different dishes from pork to shrimp, all very tasty some with a kick!. Now they have a alcohol license and you can enjoy a beer with your food. There is a bit of grease smell in the air, they probably need to work on the ventilation a little.

Fantastic place.  Very professional and extremely forth coming with all information.  
is the 2nd time I've been here and each time I walked out feeling like I got a deal.  The manager is gold.

1st time:  I had to buy tires for a company truck and they didn't have the exact tire I needed in the local inventory.  However, they offered me a set of used tires that would work just fine, plenty of tread, and sold them for tiny fraction of what I was prepared to spend.  

2nd time:  I needed a nail removed from my right rear tire.  It was a free service and the techs spend some time with me discussing all the crazy things they've pulled out of tires.  Very entertaining.  I made sure I tipped the tech doing all the work.

It seems most of their menu items are frozen and then thawed to be served to customers. I doubt anything was fresh except the salad items. Just not very impressive fare. The customer service was good, but the food was not worth returning for.

It's not great sushi, but it's delicious interesting cheap sushi with variety and the entertainment of wondering what will float up next on the little sushi boat. Also some fun, unique rolls. 

Service is friendly. If you think they're unprofessional, it's because you're a formal person and they are very informal. You need to relax. 

Deep fried peanut butter and jelly sandwich is delicious!

Asian beef taco tasted good, but if you think this is a proper Korean bulgogi taco, you are a hick. 

Don't be too offended. I am a hick also.

Oh wait, I just realized their Asian beef taco isn't supposed to be a Korean bulgogi taco. It's more Hawaiian style--sweet and tangy.
Amazing little breakfast and brunch spot! Great menu, good coffee and sweet servers. Try the Idaho Nachos!!

Customer service in this location has gone down hill unfortunately. Love the Nampa branch but the manager on duty tonight (Sarah) is not who I would want as the face of my restaurant. Waitress was fine but definitely new which also caused problems.

I'm going to try and be fair with this review, but I didn't enjoy this place at all.  The staff was friendly but that couldn't make up for the quality of food. My party had a shredded beef burrito, an order of nachos and a shrimp bowl. Everything was sub par. The food is made to order so the customer chooses what goes on each item. The burrito was served just a tad above luke warm. The shrimp bowl was nearly the consistency of a soup and not very appetizing, and the nachos were soggy after some very watery salsa was poured all over them by the girls preparing the order. Nearly all of the food was discarded in the trash. We didn't like that the meals were served in those aluminum foil bowls and the utensils were flimsy plastic. With so many placed to choose from on Eagle Road, I'm doubting I'll ever be back to give them another shot.

So awesome. Came in late and they charged us for 30 mins but then ended up keeping shop open late for and extra 1.5 hours. The front had a lighted area to play it wasn't as fun as the dark, but gave you a good chance get use to the game.

I didn't play with an upgraded gun, and that worked fine. The free guns shoot one disc ammo at a time.  The court had castles made out of cardboard that you hid around. It would be nice in the future if they would upgrade to something you could climb up on. 

It was also a little hard to find. 

All in all I was impressed, and had a lot more fun then I thought I would.
Great tasty food, attentive staff,  decently priced.  We've been telling friends and family to add it to their eating out routine.

Delicious hash!! Servings are super generous and we took half home to enjoy again. Service was prompt and staff keep moving all the time. As with many busy restaurants, the noise level was high. We had to wait about 5 minutes on a late Monday morning (after 10 am).

Went a week or so after opening. Nice atmosphere. Nice to have some more options in this area. Took a little time to be seated. Wait staff was very friendly. Salmon was good. We enjoyed the shrimp app as well. Are there some kinks that need to be worked out? Yes - new place, new processes. Give it time - good menu and friendly people. Will be back.
Delicious food and great service.  Highly recommend this place when you want a nice splurge

This was our first time trying this place. We are visiting from Oregon. We needed a great breakfast/brunch place that would cure the next day headaches lol. This place did NOT disappoint. The food, the atmosphere, the service was amazing. I got the country friend steak breakfast and my husband got the loaded hash-browns. This place knows how to make a fantastic homemade chicken fried steak. It was so filling! I HIGHLY recommend y'all trying this place!!! You will not be disappointed!

Ginos was ok, I wish I could give it 2.5 stars. They are trying too hard to be an elegant Italian dining experience. Calling the sauce ragu is ridiculous, especially since it was barely edible. Thick, pasty flavorless sauce that was almost inedible. If you make a good quality homemade sauce you don't have to call it ragu. Italian food is rustic comfort food that reminds you of home and no home calls it ragu or makes it like that. Also, the prices are ridiculously high. This is coming from a guy that is visiting from NY/NJ. These were midtown Manhattan prices in Idaho. I never ate an Italian dinner more expensive than I did last night. Not to be all negative the fried calamari was excellent and cooked just right. The problem was the sauce had no business having that nice calamari dipped in it. I had the chicken parm as my main course and it was a beautiful piece of chicken cooked perfectly. The mozz tasted and looked like a high quality mozz. The sauce (ragu lol) made it barely edible. The side of penne I couldn't eat because of the sauce. Deserts were excellent and service was good but a little rushed at the end. If the owner wants, I will gladly come to his kitchen and help him make a nice Sunday sauce like we do back home.

Ordered a children's pepperoni pizza and an "adult" margherita pizza. The margherita was clearly (accidentally I assume) made on children's dough. (I posted a picture for you to see yourself.) Was given a lame excuse about the  cook not stretching the dough enough. We proposed paying for two children's pizzas, but the manager threw a fit and took the whole thing off and literally stomped off. Disagreements will happen, but way to turn an awkward situation into us never returning. We even planned to get some tiramisu, but never mind. The manager should be the level-headed one.

Change your hours.
Drove here 20 minutes out of my way for breakfast and got here at 2:05 and told their hours are wrong.

Awful beyond belief! Everything was fried, and so greasy. I put a shrimp on the napkin, and the napkin was soaked in 2.5 seconds. Like I really want to put that in my body. I know Chinese food (when it actually is Chinese food) may not be the healthiest, but this went way beyond that. It was $40.00 of ahem food, that we were to wimpy to not pay, and the dogs ate it and farted for a week. Never will we go back there. The staff could tell we didn't like it, as we didn't touch it, but they were like deer in headlights and did nothing and said nothing. YUCK!!!!! I should have taken the fact that we were the only customers as an omen, well lesson learned.

Food, service and wine list were all good. The tables are small and crowded together. Be sure to have a reservation and encourage Gino to put a website with menu and pricing online.  Would spend money here again.

Food was incredible. Menu is huge, and unique, and affordable. My only complaint is that the restaurant is like an amphitheater for noise, so instead of a quiet breakfast I was able to enjoy the amplified voice of several obnoxious children.
I love when a place has multiple eggs benedict options and I had never tried it with corned beef. A great breakfast with large portions and nice service!

We have been searching for a replacement for our favorite Chinese restaurant that we moved away from. We finally found it here at Red Pavilion! So so yummy! And very moderately priced. And the waitress was quick, which is always a bonus. No complaints at all!!

Sigh, I have been to Gino's soo many times. even when he was still in downtown Boise. I have had good meals, and so-so meals. Problem is never a GREAT meal.
Went back tonight and ....meh.
Service: Very good. Our server was very attentive, and friendly.

Atmosphere: The usual Italian themed place. Very comfortable, but noisy... We had a hard time hearing our own conversation.

Food: Sigh. I usually stick to the traditional offerings. Meat with red sauce. I have had the osso bucco , and lamb shank many times, and really enjoyed it. This time I ventured out and tried the seafood raviolis. Pretty bland, left me wishing I stuck with the standards.
My girl had the veal, and peppers. The veal was overcooked, and we had to ask for a steak knife to cut it with.
We did order a nice Primativo wine (bottle), and it was a very good value ($30.00). We enjoyed it very much.
We will go back at some point, but we will try other options as well.
Mediocre food at best. The cashier didn't say a single word to me, even after my food was ready. She just put it on the counter and walked away.

As close to perfect as a breakfast joint can come. First they have great coffee rich and flavorful not weak like most. I had the CFS and eggs and it was delicious and a good job on the gravy. My only problem is that I need a nap!

Just left after a busy Sunday brunch....well worth the wait! The host was friendly and was hustling to get tables sat as quickly as he could. Our server was great, fast, efficient and very pleasant. The food was delicious, great flavors in the hash. We've never had jalapeños in pancakes....amazing! Happy to have tried and enjoyed something new! Thank you for a great breakfast! Much appreciated.

Quality food, friendly service and comfortable vibe.  In the firmament of Treasure Valley Chinese food restaurants this is a star.  In Chinese culture the color red represents luck, happiness and joy.  I hope all are true for the nice folks who run Red Pavilion. 

THEY'VE PICKED A LANE:  I love that they've picked a lane and drive in it.  Many local Asian food restaurants combine Chinese and Thai or Thai and Sushi or Vietnamese and Japanese cuisines or multiples of those on the same menu to end up with mediocrity.  It is hard enough to do a great job on one Asian cuisine.  Here they focus on and do a good job preparing Chinese food with some dishes for diners who enjoy standard Chinese - American food and some for diners familiar with Chinese fare offered in old world restaurants in larger cities.

MENUS:  Large, multi page laminated menu has many items from appetizers through entrees and with descriptions and photos that are typical of Mandarin restaurants focused on American diner preferences.  If you ask for their special menu, or Chinese menu as they sometimes call it, they'll bring you a single page typed menu with a couple of dozen items listed in both Chinese characters and English text.  That is our 'go to' menu.  The servers are happy to ask the cooks in the kitchen about ingredients if they didn't know them in response to special menu questions.   For example, "What are the ingredients in the pickled potatoes?"  But that is to come...

FOOD:  Hot and sour soup is my guilty pleasure to try on first visit to any Chinese food restaurant.  The one here was good for consistency and chock full of the right ingredients including black wood ear mushrooms, even if I'd add in a bit more sour.  The wok cooked items included we tried included five spice pork with tofu and vegetables and also the pickled potato dish.  No kidding for the latter.  It was a stir fry combination of julienne potatoes, pickled (daikon) radish and infintisimally small shred of bok choy.  New to us and delicious.   If there is a weak spot, we found the noodle dishes, in particular those we've ordered off the special Chinese menu and called out as Sichuan style,  tend to be both bland and too oily.  We avoid noodles in any form here.

Portions are generous for all dishes.

WHAT I'D CHANGE:   if I could wave a magic wand in the kitchen, I'd have them use less oil in all their stir fry dishes.  Still, my husband and I appreciate the dishes aren't swimming in sauce as is the case at many Chinese food restaurants serving American diners. 

VALUE:  Menu prices range from as little as $2.50 for a bowl of soup to a high of as much as $14 for an entree with most items coming in around $10.  Typical for us of two cups of soup or a starter and two entrees plus comes to about $28.00 before tax and we have enough take away for another meal at home.  There are combo lunch deals and family dinner deals.

VIBE:  Light, bright, great overhead lighting, a few pieces of interesting art on the walls, elevator-listening style music sung by Chinese language artists and lots of red in the decor.  

ACCESSIBILITY:  Accessible parking in lot (2 spaces).  Level in the door.  All one one floor.  Seating is standard height and a combination of booths and tables.  Didn't check the loo.

OUTDOOR SEATING:  All the way at the back of the restaurant I noted through a glass door there were a few metal tables and chairs with umbrellas overhead. 

.
Terrible . Slow service , boats hardly ever dime around . Sushi is low grade . Same thing as a year ago . Gave them a second chance . DONE
Busy on a Friday night.   Good food, good service,  clean restaurant.   Good times!  I recommend checking it out.

Wish I could give this place more stars. Have been supporting Idaho pizza for years and they do have great food, but we will no longer be going here because they can't quote a delivery time under 2 hours...EVER. No matter the day of the week or time of day (we've tried it all to continue to give this place a chance), it's still a ridiculous amount of time. Pizza is good, but it's also convenient due to its delivery option and this place totally drops the ball on it. Hire more delivery staff, because you're losing business.

I've been wanting to try this place forrreeevvvverrrrrr. So glad I finally did! 

It feels upscale casual. I love the feel of the black and white art, and the checkered table cloths. So great. 

I took my husband and our two boys here (8 & 6) on a Sunday afternoon. We were promptly seated and our waiter came right away. He was a friendly guy who made us feel right at home. We ordered the Four Cheese pizza (small) and a make your own (small).

Holy Hannah, these "smalls" are the size of a regular medium AT LEAST. I couldn't believe how big they were. We def. had leftovers but I am not complaining! The pizzas come out quick, the four cheese was amazing. I can't wait to try more toppings and some of the salads next time we are here. A new favorite for us in The Village!
Good calzone. Friendly place. Cool neighborhood joint for lunch. Will have to check out the dinner scene.
Absolute worst of the insurance companies out there. Just prepare to pay for everything you need out of pocket.

We were here recently because of a craving for barbecued ribs.  We tried both the St. Louis and babybacks which were both tender and flavorful and not too spicy.  The sides of coleslaw, macaroni, and potato salad were also good.  One person in our party ordered the chopped pork which I sampled and I would probably order that when I come back here again.  The side dishes of coleslaw, macaroni and cheese, and potato salad also were very good.  Our server was very pleasant and helpful as well and very efficient.  We decided to share a piece of pecan pie and key lime pie but the manager informed us that both pies did not turn out well and  we were offered complimentary desserts of bread pudding and a brownie sundae.  We weren't disappointed--they were both delicious!

We come here every week for a fair-priced, quality breakfast. The frittatas are delicious, as is the ranchero sauce. People may not love the prices but this is not a chain restaurant, everything is from scratch!! Joe is even looking at gluten free options.

Very good Italian food! There is nothing better than a steaming hot bowl of Chicken Fettuccine Alfredo! The pasta was perfectly cooked, and the sauce was hot and creamy! Service was outstanding! My cup was never empty! And I was asked by different people if I was enjoying my meal, and if I needed anything. It was a little pricey for my liking. But overall it was a good experience and good food.

Boo. We arrive there Saturday afternoon at 4 we were seated. We were immediately told we're shutting down our ovens for cleaning so we don't want to rush you but you need to order right now. Too bad you don't have menus yet too bad you haven't even got to sit down but again don't mean to rush you but you need to order now or leave so we left. Not to return. What a ridiculous way to run a restaurant especially in a place like the village. You don't have enough ovens so you can cook pizza's while you clean another oven. Surprised you're even in business.

We always received great service for lunch and dinner at red Pavilion! Their potstickers are good, their soup is better, and there traditional mongolian spices and food is excellent. They treat you very well and don't push you out if you want to stay longer.
If you do a pick up order triple check that they get your order right before you drive down there.  They messed up my order several times and I stopped going because of the poor service.

We are from east coast for good or bad and have not been happy with any Chinese food places in Idaho. Sorry. Panda Express seemed be best option and then add soy sauce.  The Red Pavilion was HOME RUN.  Had hot s d sour soup that need little more hot spice that was available table side. Calamari appetizer kicked ass. Every other dish at table fantastic.  Portions of entree all large.  Side rice was excellent and portions only needed be larger to come home cause no one finished there entrees.   Just fantastic everything.  Definitely the place to go.  Kicked PF Chang butt.
Service was good, too expensive for what you get as far as pasta goes. Charged me for extra bread and didn't tell me that it was gonna cost extra.

My husband and I have been here several times and had a good meal.  Last night however was not one of those.  I usually love their bread, but the one delivered to our table was very undercooked and doughy.  We ordered the prawns for an appetizer.  First, for $14 I expect more than 4 prawns, but there was so much raw garlic in them you could hardly taste anything else.  They took our favorite dish the Abrusie off the menu, so we ordered the bolognese pasta and requested the penne pasta since it's easier to eat than spaghetti.  Neither of ours came with the penne.  The waitress assured me it would be a quick fix.  My husband kept his and was half way done eating before mine came back. Our waitress was nice, but totally disorganized and frazzled.  Wasted a good amount of money on a poor experience.  I would have complained while we were there, but my husband really wanted to come here, so I let it go.  We will not be coming back.

Wow this place is great!  Fast service, super hot food.  Some of the best Chinese I've had.  Super happy to have found this place.  We will be back.  

My wife had been reading great things about this place and they weren't wrong.

Amazing food, nice atmosphere, can't go wrong.

This is easily the best kept secret in Meridian. I have loves these chefs since they opened their doors in Boise. The new Meridian restaurant lives up to Fujiyama Boise's reputation. Fresh fish beautifully prepared and expertly rolled. My wife and I have the opportunity to eat sushi around the world, and I would put Fujiyama at the top of the list. I've even had them cater client events.

Been there once only but was very please by the friendly service and warmth of the waitress.
We were seated right away and ordered the shu mai (4 pieces) very good.
We both  had sushi, both very good. 

This place also does takeout which I could definitely enjoy in the future.

This review is only for the take out. 
Don't do it unless you like soggy fries and a dried up buyer.

So this is the sister company of the one up in Mccall! I really enjoyed my experience here and wish I could belly up for more! Everything that came of the kitchen smelled delicious. I enjoyed the shrimp and scallop dish. I wouldn't mind trying the mandarin chicken and red tofu dish next time I come. I wish this spot was a little closer to downtown.

We ate breakfast here twice while in Meridian. The food was great both times. Hubby had a stuffed burrito which was HUGH. The second time he had corned beef skillet which was wonderful. I went with the jalapeño frittata wow was that good. Also tried the jalapeño pancakes the next time. Yep I like jalapeños. It was complimented with a berry sauce that was a perfect merry between the two items. It had cream cheese between the pancakes. If you are a light eater order a small stack. Did not know that but now I know for when we return. 

The atmosphere was nice and the staff was great. We had a wonderful girl who waited on us but I can't remember her name. Should have written it down. 

Very clean, out of the way place. You won't be disappointed.

My mom wanted Italian for dinner and in our area that means pizza.  We are happy to make the drive.  The food was excellent.  Our server was very attentive and very personable.  Our only complaint was our plates were taken literally seconds after we put down our forks and one point we were not ready for them to be removed.  We will be back, as I stated the food was excellent. Fyi get dessert the dark chocolate torte was a masterpiece.

We have been in Boise at the Marriott for 4 days and happened upon this place our first morning. Everything was delicious, and the servers were friendly. The biscuits with marionberry are amazing. I probably gained 3 pounds because I had a giant biscuit each day. The MoJoe potatoes were good but we both preferred the hash browns. The eggs -- poached, scrambled, and omelette were all delicious. I highly recommend MoeJoe's!
Love U-Swirl. The staff is always friendly when we go in and the yogurt is delicious. They always have the toppings stocked and the fruit is fresh. Plus there's military discount! :)
For some reason the service has gotten so bad over the last few months. They're so slow and our waiters have been bad. It's sad cuz we have loved this place.

We noticed that their sign on the door said they open at 5pm. It was 4:51 and the door was unlocked so we went in. Before we could walk in the chef rudely said ''we don't open untill 5''. Really? We couldn't wait inside for 9 minutes? Horrible customer service in my opinion. We ended up going someplace else and won't be back.

Sad to say but this visit was disappointing.  The past visits have yielded great food.
My primavera with chicken was extremely bland.  The pasta was good well but was also not dressed.  Just plain pasta.  The chicken was tough as tough can get.  
The other dish we got was butternutt squash ravioli.  The brown butter sauce tasted burnt.
The best item we had was the table bread with dipping oil.

We love Costa Vida!!! We been coming to this location since they've opened! We came here today for lunch. My daughters shared a Large Sweet Pork Salad and I had their daily special, which is Sweet Pork Enchilada w/drink! Everything was good! Love their refillable Horchata! Sure, their lettuce was not in the perfect condition since we spotted a few brown pieces in our food, but it happens, especially during this time of the year. Despite that, I still give Costa Vida five stars ! That's how much I love Costa Vida! Till next time!
Great breakfast- a lot of food.  Took enough home for another meal.  Friendly staff.  Crowded even on a Wednesday but we didn't have to wait to be seated

The 4 stars is a bit misleading but an accurate average, as we have been here twice. Once was just my wife and I for a late breakfast, and then we brought our family there when everyone was out for a family event. Our first visit was a solid 5, and the second a low 3- so hence the 4.

First visit our server was Sam. Nice younger guy, super friendly. There was a bit of confusion at first as he and a lady were both taking drink orders and offering to take food orders etc, but eventually Sam was the only one and he did great. Breakfast was great. My wife got the lemon poppy seed pancakes and they nicely agreed to put the glaze on the side (good option: the glaze is great but sweet, and it would have been too much poured over them. Plus, we had 2 of the 3 to take home because they are HUGE and the glaze on the side meant they weren't soggy or anything!). My omelet was delicious (avocado, cheese and broccoli) and also huge. The female server had suggested (without hesitation lol) the potatoes vs the hasbrowns when asked, and she was dead on: they were awesome! The only thing I didn't enjoy was the side of sausage: they were basically small burger patties with sausage seasonings. Very odd texture, giant, and dry. Other than that everything was awesome. 

We left very pleased, full, and looking forward to bringing our guests in the following week. 

Tip: This is a VERY small little place, with a small patio. It's cute, comfortable and not great for big groups. We had 8 on our second visit (weekday), and they won't seat you until your entire party is present (understandable-- just an FYI). 

We were seated with a young woman server, who 1) I don't think liked groups and very much didn't like kids (we had our two sons with us) and 2) Didn't seem to actually listen to any request most of us made, even something as simple as an additional kid's menu and crayons so BOTH kids had one. I asked 4 times and finally gave up.

Waters were constantly empty, the food took almost 30 minutes, and almost all of us were missing something or had an extra something or something was wrong. The server was so unhelpful and unfriendly we didn't even bother discussing most of it, and just tried to eat and leave. That said, the food was very good and I think most of the group enjoyed their meals. Sadly, most of us commented on the poor service when we left vs the quality of the food.

We did see the server we had previous and it appeared he was hosting. it would have been better had they swapped those two I think! 

We will go back and hope to be in a different section next time, as the food was good, a solid value and the other people all seemed very nice! Go early to avoid the crowd and pay attention the hours because they close after lunch! Speaking of lunch, they have an avocado sandwich I can't wait to try!

Delicious food. Way too pricey for the small amount of food you get tho. We ordered a large container of their Mongolian beef and a large one of beef chow mein & it barely fed 2 adults and 1 child.  Their rice was EXTREMELY dry as well.... I wouldn't recommend getting that.

Wonderful service! Quickly becoming one of our favorite sushi places. Huge selection  and very fresh fish.
On our last visit the hubby had their teriyaki chicken. Very good! For a chicken breast it wasn't the least bit dry. If you are a salmon lover, the salmon sushi dinner is great! Lots of salmon sushi and a tiger roll for under $20
This location has never been busy on our visits so we've gotten fast and attentive wait staff.
Very reasonably price for the quality of fish.
Check this place out for good Japanese food and sushi.

We wanted to try all the wings!!! The menu options were vast and we will have to return to try them. The sauces were great and the appetizer was large and delicious. The beer selection included a lot of local beers on draft and was expansive. The waitress let me sample three because I just couldn't chose, she was upbeat and fun. The kids menu included the regular kids type food but with a few surprise items like chicken Alfredo that was quite delicious.

We returned here for breakfast after first eating here 2 years ago. We were here this time looking for a retirement home. 

As good as we remembered. Prepare to wait if it is a Saturday.
Oh my goodness! The service is awful. Took over an hour to get served. Then finally had to go find someone to get our ticket. So so sad.
One of the best breakfast places I've tried across the country.  Great griddle items, potatoes, and side meats.  Need to find a reason to be back in Boise to eat this again!

This is the cLosest I've had to east coast pizza since I've moved here. The sauce is delicious. Very tomatoey (if that's a word) the dough is great also. They are a little pricey: I paid $9 for a small pizza And they charged and extra $4 for one topping and $2 for a little heavier sauce. But i will definitely come here again :) i haven't had anything like it at all in the area. I also heard Tuesday's are half off wine.
No joke, this guys just throw UNCOOKED bacon into their breakfast burritos. It happened three times before I stopped going there.
Great place for everyone! Best sweet pork salad ever! Kids love their quesadillas. The only thing that I would say is negative is there isn't enough locations!
Great BBQ. Friendly and effective staff.  Enjoyed the Ribs.   Loved it for a chain restaurant. The choices in sauces were a great addition.  Look forward to going back.

I have eaten Taco Johns for many years and even in other states like Wyoming and Utah. They have changed some nowadays, but they still carry the basic items that I love like the taco bravo and super burrito; also, the potato olès are always good. My in-laws owned a Mexican Restaurant and a Taco Johns franchise for about 15 years before they retired. My husband worked at his parent's restaurant while he went to school. He can even tell you how to make all the salsas!:)) He was so happy when he found out that we were going to have a Taco Johns close to where we live. Previously, getting to the closest location took a drive to Mountain Home. For dinner tonight we had the six pack and a pound; which contains 6 tacos and a pound of potatoes olès! You can have either soft or hard shell tacos or, like us, both. We love Taco Johns Super Hot Sauce! I like to dip my olès in a mix of ketchup & super hot sauce! We came @6:45 when it wasn't too busy, and it took them about 10 minutes to get our order ready...Not too bad. There are things they could definitely improve, like the state of the dining room. More than half of the tables were dirty when we were there. Also, when we were going to take some sauce from the bar, almost all of them were empty. I had to ask them to fill it up. Other than that, keep up the good work! We'll be back!

Before I went to the village had a dinner already. Just because the pizza place was so crowded I decided to try them how they are. I ordered a 12" personal cheese pizza to go it was good when I had it, but I had to wait 2 X15 minutes. The girl took the order said fifteen minutes after 18 minutes I went she said we forgot to make it come back another fifteen minutes it will be ready. I never had pizza without topping, but didn't add any topping. The toppings are a little pricy $2.00-$4.00 based on what you add on a 12" pizza.

Boise/Meridian knows how to make breakfast. I've never seen a city with so many great breakfast spots. Goody's is still my favorite but if you live and want to stay in Meridian I'd say this is the best breakfast over the rest.

Breakfast buffet at J B's Restaurant..this is really good.

Buffet has everything you could possible want, pancake, french toast, eggs, bacon, sausage, biscuit and gravy, fruit, juice, and the list goes on.

Waitresses was great looking 20 something year olds, friendly, helpful, and on top of their great service here.

Prices are moderate, and the restaurant was full on Sunday morning.

I have an update on the pizza- 

Pizza is a no here

I ordered an extra sauce pizza. However when I arrived I was given a pizza with hardly any sauce.  When I politely asked if it could be redone, I caught a lot of glances and smirking between the hostess and the guys behind the counter making the pizza. First let me emphasize that the hostess asked the guys how they made my pizza and I heard them say with extra cheese. I was standing right there. When she told them I ordered it with extra sauce, they backtracked. The guy caught an attitude and said he would redo it but still put the same amount of sauce. I don't pay for attitude. I have a right to get what I ordered. I hope the manager can teach his take out side to display the same amount of professionalism and courteousness as the dining area. 

Dining: is a yes!

The very best food I've had in the area- hands down. They have a great ambience, great service and delicious food. Their bread is super good- has garlic and herbs baked into the bread, and their dipping sauce goes so well with it: garlic, olive oil, and pepper flakes for a kick.  My favorite meal here is the lamb shank.  It tickles your palette in all the right ways. There's so much goodness about the dish- basil, garlic, San Marzano tomatoes and gnocchi. Let me tell you how I never even knew I liked gnocchi until I experienced this creation at Gino's. They are like light velvety pillows. I'm not even a big pasta girl and I adore these. The dish is slow braised, tender and moist meat. I wouldn't change or add a thing to it. It's about $30, but you are given a Generous portion. Easily 2.5 meals. The service here is great- they don't come every 5 seconds, but also don't disappear. They have mastered the right amount of contact and top it off with delicious and fresh tasting food.

This is our go to restaurant for everything Italian. Food is always superb, service prompt and courteous and Gino usually circulates around the restaurant to see that everything is perfect, and it was as usual.

I went there for a birthday lunch with three other friends. We ordered some sodas and two medium pizzas with a few toppings on each. The bill came to $76 because of the added charges of the toppings. Each topping was two dollars, and chicken was five dollars for each pizza even though it was only on half of each pizza. The price of an iced tea was $4.75. And the best part is that it's not even great pizza. I will never go there again.

We just had our first visit and had a very positive experience. Mark Fineman DVM is very knowledgeable and I was impressed with his speedy diagnosis'. His assistant Sarah was very helpful and friendly. He patiently answered all questions and provided us with options concerning our budget. I feel confident that we have made an excellent choice.

Had lunch recently at Rudy's on Overland. The place was fantastic. Great food, great service, highly recommend it. 
However, since I live in Star, I just found Rudy's on McMillan. Very nice atmosphere but food was considerably poor. Had fish & chips (tots) and a salad. Fish batter was cheap and very greasy, tots were equally greasy. The salad was a typical "bag" salad b/c all the pieces were the same size. Cut from a machine. The cut edges were turning brown and not real crispy. I didn't finish the salad.
I can't believe the difference between the two restaurants, but the Overland location seems to be better managed for food quality.
Loved the interior,  good was great. Just had the tri-tip tacos and some shrimp. Wine of course was fabulous!!! Great place

Great food options for vegans and meat eaters alike. Great healthy options and great taste. Love this place. They need more staff, but the ones they have are friendly and courteous. Would definitely recommend to anyone wanting to eat healthier.

When I arrived I wasn't sure if it was seat yourself or wait to be seated. I was taken to a table, made my order and my appetizer arrived. I had no eating utensils and had to ask for it and a short time later I was brought a fork....no napkin or other utensils.....just a fork. 

The food was great and had great flavor it's just the service wasn't up to par and made the experience mediocre.
Fantastic, that's all I can say!  Best breakfast place in town hands down!  Food is amazing, staff is superb. Renovation looks great!

This is one of our go-to dining destinations. The food always hits the spot. We used to always order the sweet pork salad but found we get more of what we like by ordering the sweet pork burrito with the small portion of salad on the side. The staff is always friendly. The manager, Tim Murray, often greets the guests.

Absolutely the worst customer service and delivery time in the valley. Consistently 30+ mins late. If you don't mind waiting for extremely long periods of time with no resolution with an ambivalent waitstaff, this is your spot. Awful!!!

Our experience here was consistently terrible. Started with the hostess losing our name. As a result, a 15 minute wait became a 45 minute wait. I asked the hostess if they had a gluten free menu. She said no. When our waiter came to the table, he gave us an iPad for doing allergen sorts. The food took another 40 minutes. It was bland at best. This is the se one time we have had a bad experience here in Meridian. We are not coming back. We have been going to RRs for 30 years. This is not up to par.

My experience was as bad as one could have in a salon. I have been getting my hair done professionally for 13 years and have never been this unhappy. Staff had very little knowledge about the techniques they pride themselves in offering. I made a very feasible color request given my current hair color which was bayalage, I left just completely blonde. No contrast, far from any bayalage. Then they offered to get me in next day with someone else to correct, then at that appt I explained everything that had happened to this hair stylist and VERY specifically told her exactly what i wanted and what I was not happy with. She again did not listen and seemed to be very inexperienced. I left that time with a brown crown around the top of my head with a line and the rest still all blonde. On top of that all of the other hairstylists that would walk by would snicker, give me looks and talk amongst each other. I was so humiliated I couldn't wait to get out of there. The most unprofessional experience I've ever had. I'll never walk back in there again. But that's not all, I was then severely apologized to and told I would be getting a call in the next couple of days to refund my money, I have yet to receive that call. Which I waited for before writing my review. I would post the pics so you can see how awful it looks but don't see a place here for that. Let's just say my hair looked 100x better before I ever went there. 

Save yourself the humiliation and the cost and go somewhere where you will get your monies worth and be treated with true professionalism.

We are big fans of the Discount Tire company because of their quality service, great prices, and well-trained staff. This location is no exception.
We discovered a worn spot on our tire and knew we had to replace two of the back tires. We called Discount Tire. The person who answered the phone was very professional and gave us an accurate quote. They had to lowest price on the tires we wanted and we got an appointment the following day.
We arrived to find a very busy lobby. We were checked-in promptly and they took our car in right on time, as scheduled.  The whole process took less than 30 minute and we were on our way. They bagged the old tire and recycled the other one for us. You cannot get better service than that. I wish they would train other companies on how to treat customers!

Very disappointing how far service has plummeted at Gino's. Called for reservations recently (they still haven't joined OpenTable or other online reservation apps/services). No one picked up, so I left a detailed message requesting a reservation for later that day. Never received a call back, so I elected to drop by and check on availability. Hostess stand was staffed by 4 teenagers. Told them that no one was answering the phone and they curtly replied, 'sorry.' Asked them about availability that evening and the hostess seemed bewildered and asked one of the waitresses to survey the restaurant. There were at least 4 empty tables in plain view without anyone else waiting in line. The waitress returned and listed at least another four empty tables and the hostess looked up and bluntly stated, 'sorry, we don't have any availability.' I thanked her for her effusive hospitality and walked out. Hope the food hasn't suffered a similar precipitous decline.

Let me just start by saying YUM! We had excellent service, the wine was perfect and most of all the food was very good. Gino wad in the dining room checking to make sure all was well. I love that an owner/chef is concerned about his customers enough to walk around and see how everyone is doing.

My husband and me have been staying away from Red Robin a bit since our last experience (at the Parkcenter location in Boise) was less than stellar.  We feel that changes Red Robin has made to 'keep up' with the more upscale burger joints (Five Guys/Smash Burger etc) took away from some of what made them our favorite sit down burger place.  My husband had a free birthday burger available to him though, so we took a chance at the Eagle Road location.   Since we were only the second customers through the door of the day, being greeted and seated was no problem.  We were seated in a booth just behind the passway aisle between the bar and the main restaurant.  In retrospect this was kind of annoying.. HOWEVER we failed to speak up when the hostess asked if the spot was okay, so the onus was on US. 
Gone are the table tents that used to tout the current 'special' burger (right now some ginormous thing with brisket on it to go with the new "Hercules" movie) Gone are the large glossy tri-fold plastic menus (replaced by smaller, spiral bound booklets).  Also gone are the funky little cardboard coasters for your beverage.  STILL there however, an assortment of intriguing appetizers, beverages, burgers, sandwiches, salads, entrees and desserts.  As others have mentioned, the prices have indeed gone up.  You have to be very careful when looking at the burgers if you are having to watch your pennies.. I wound up with an 'artisan' burger (the black and bleu,.. noms) that was $14 compared to others as low as $7.99. 
As we reviewed the menu I saw the hostess coming our way with a family of four.  Parents and two little ones probably no older than 2 and 4.  Despite the entire restaurant being open season, they were seated directly behind us.   I promise, I understand that servers have their set 'areas' and that keeping patrons in the areas with assigned servers is status quo, but I still fail to see why at least ONE booth couldn't have been left as a buffer.   To their credit however, the parents did a wonderful job of keeping the noise level down, there were no kicks to the back of our booth and no little hands sought to try advanced knot tying with my hair (which HAS happened to me in other places).  
Hubby chose the crispy chicken sandwich, asking it be placed in a basket (they've done away with the red plastic baskets in favor of what we think are some horrific plates) that his sandwich be wrapped (they don't do that anymore either unless you ask) and cut in half.  He also asked for ranch to dip his fries in.  I ordered the  Black and Bleu burger and fries. (On Ciabatta bread served open face, the burger is topped with sauteed mushrooms, grilled onions and crumbled bleu cheese, a 'knife and forker' delight!).   He was drinking the tropical green tea (a bit to sweet for my taste) I went with  diet Dr. Pepper.  
Our order arrived, prepared exactly as we asked it to be.  The food was hot and tasty.  Our server was a bit slow on drink refills (again odd, as there were very few people in the restaurant).  When the manager came around to see how we were doing his arms were laden with notebooks and a box of Krispy Kreme donuts, which I thought was not only unprofessional but left us feeling like we'd interrupted his day).   We lingered a bit over beverage refills and a 2nd order of fries then left.  Oh and apparently they've done away with the free birthday dessert.  But at almost 50 my husband and me are okay with that. 
Suffice it to say this was a much better Red Robin experience than our last forray in Boise.  We'll likely go back to this location again, for MY birthday in October.

Took a road trip through Boise. Going south we hit Goldy's Breakfast Bistro (3 Stars) however on the way back home we hit Moe Joes Breakfast Eatery. Wow, 5 star rating for sure. The food was amazing, atmosphere was bright and clean. Not overly loud inside but still full of happy people. 

Loved it! 

Eggs Benedict and Cinnamon Roll French Toast were divine.

I'm going to have to give this place mixed reviews. It definitely has its pluses and its negatives.  To begin with we came in the door and were told that we would have to wait. As we waited I looked around and noticed that three quarters of the restaurant seats were empty. I became more concerned when more people came in and they are being told that would be a 20 minute wait.    We were finally seated after about 15 minutes but we're not given menus.  After 10 minutes I went and got them myself.  I looked at the buffet and as other reviews noted it was not worth the money.  The waitress came and took our 2 orders and left.  My order of bulgogi came and was very tasty yet my wife's order of spicy pork came 20 min later.  Her meal was very nice.  After her food came we never saw our waitress again except as she helped others.  Our drinks were never filled and I had to go and find another waitress to get my check.   

It should be noted that you should be careful if using a card because more than once I saw a waitress take a check and leave them on the hostess stand near the front door unattended.

3 stars just because I enjoyed the food!

I would give a Two-star rating based mainly on hygienic aspects. My room had a sticky spill across most of the desk/table area, two of the "clean" bath towels had other people's hair stuck in them(pretty sure one of the towels had hair from the nether regions in it). Thankfully I had one clean towel in the bunch. Upon settling into bed, I felt something tickling my feet. There was also long hairs near the foot of my bed. White sheets...dark hair...how do you miss that?  I would not recommend or stay again, just based on housekeeping mishaps. Pretty disappointed.

I had been going to Camping World until Bish moved in.  WHAT A DIFFERENCE!  I cannot go  back to CW again.  Customer Service is better.  Their outfitters are better.  They really listened to what we were looking for and put us in the perfect RV for us.  The sales cycle seemed a bit long, but we walked away very satisfied.
Our outfitter was Brandon and he was amazing.  He not only knew what he was talking about but he took time to build a relationship.

My husband and I have been fans of Red Robin for awhile.  Most of the time we dined at the Meridian location on Eagle Road.  We've also been to the Milwaukee location in Boise.  We've always enjoyed good customer service, hospitality, prompt service and well-prepared food.

Today was another story. We were in the area so we went to the Red Robin location on Milwaukee.  As we approached the entrance, a young man opened the door.  There was no smile on his face and he made no verbal contact with us.  As we arrived at the reception desk, it was momentarily vacant.  A young woman came to us and again, with no greeting or smile asked us if we wanted to be seated in the lounge or the restaurant area.   We didn't know what the "lounge" was since it had been a long time since we'd dined here, so we elected to go to the "restaurant" area.  She showed us to a table, handed us menus, and left.  This was around 12:30 and of course it was busy,  but we weren't offered a beverage and no one came to our table.  I also noticed that there was a computer monitor on the table, similar to what is found at Chile's where patrons can elect to order their own food rather than having the benefit of a personal server.  I guess that is the experience here, and if so I find that very off putting.

Needless to say, we left without ordering food and went somewhere else to have lunch.  I'm disappointed that Red Robin has resorted to such impersonal, sterile type service.  We won't be back.

I really hate to be writing a review like this but it is what it is. I have been going to Red Robin since my kids were at home. A little over 26 years and today I had the worst service I have ever had their. To being with I want to state that I believe the reason was because it was just my wife and I and we ordered to of the small tavern burgers and water.  Not allot to make a tip on so we were what seemed to me summarily dismissed by the waitress. I won't say her name but I would suggest you avoid the one with (very long blond over bleached hair).  
I ask for a small basket of fries to nibble on before the meal was served.  They were actually served about 3 seconds ahead of the meal by a bus boy and they were barely warm, had not been seasoned and to be blunt rather disgusting. The waitress happened by I said these are cold she said let me get you some fresh ones.  WE NEVER SAW HER AGAIN UNTIL IT WAS TIME TO GIVE US THE BILL.  Our water was never refilled even though waitresses in our area walked back and forth with water for their customers 3 times.
Out waitress Ja...... ooops seemed more consumed with the LARGE PARTY on the other side of the room (larger party bigger tip) she spend the majority of her time over there waiting on them hand an foot. It did not take a rocket scientist to figure out that we just didn't $$$ count.
The promised fries never came (not that I wanted them after the meal was over) and our water was never refilled, she didn't even attempt to expand the bill by offering us desert. By the time the bill came all I wanted to do was leave.   I had to wrestle with my wife over the tip. 15% was 2:21 and he most certainly did not deserve that. All she did was write down the order, she did absolutely nothing else. Had I been there by myself I would not have tipped her at all.  
I love Red Robin and I will be back but this was not one of their better days, and it was not because of the product, it was because of very poor service by a single $$$ minded employee. If she is ever my waitress again I will request someone else. 
DEFFINATLY NOT THE NORM FOR RED ROBIN.

What an awesome job Great Floors did installing my new carpet. It's just fabulous. Michael, the sales rep was terrific, answered all my questions as well as sharing some good advice for the pad. I've just finished a redo in my home and it's spectacular.

Spectacular place for very authentic Mandarin cuisine. After living in Seattle for a few years this was a real treat to find. Portions are perfect, flavor is terrific and prices are more than reasonable.

This used to be my favorite go to restaurant. Last night's visit was disappointing at best. Our waiter was more like a robotic drone than anything. My food was greasy and the chicken tasted strange. The sangria was missing fruit. So,  if the service, food and beverages stink . . . for the same high prices . . . will not be returning. THEY ARE NOT CLOSED.

I have three words: sweet pork tacos. I kid you not, you will have happy food dreams about them for days after you try them. I have never had a negative experience at Costa Vida, the staff is friendly, conscientious, and quick. This is a great place to go if you need to eat gluten-free, just mention when you order and they will change gloves and make sure nothing with wheat touches your food.

I normally frequent the Boise location but decided to give this location a try since I was in the area. I'll get to the point of my review right off the bat. You are missing out if you live in Meridian and do not have this on your regular lunch outing rotation! 

For lunch today I got the chicken katsu bento box. Each lunch bento box is ~$8 and includes: Salad, Soup, 2 spring rolls, a California roll, your choice of protein with a sauce and rice. Honestly, you could spend that same amount of money on pizza or a Big Mac meal, but come on, for the price you can get a ton of authentic Japanese food, no comparison here!! 

Do yourself a favor and check this place out for lunch (dinner is really good too, but have only had dinner at the Boise location). I promise that you will add this to your rotation!

Absolutely EXCELLENT!! This is by far the best breakfast spot in the Boise area.  Move over Goldys!!
I had the corned beef hash and side of pancakes. AMAZING! Corned beef was seasoned and cook perfectly, the diced potatoes had an amazing seasoning and they were crispy but soft in the inside. Topped it off with 2 over easy eggs and it was the best I have ever had! 

The pancakes were phenomenal .  Crispy around the edges and super moist. Not over sweet and light and airy. 

Well done!

Better than your Taco Bells of the world. And a serviceable late-night option if you work late or need something in your stomach to fend off the booze (as I work late and this location is on my way home, I make the occasional trip here if I'm starving). But otherwise if I'm pining for Mexican food, this place is never a destination. 

The prices are relatively cheap and the portions are good even when you think the price might be a little high ($2.25 for a taco, but you get a pretty good chunk of meat for it). But you have to consider that what you're being given in those portions is cheap as well. The meat here just isn't very good. The asada had been most reliable for me, but late at night it tends to be sitting around around for awhile already cooked. That's when I tend to choose lengua because I know they'll need to cook it on the spot. I can get much better lengua around here, but at least they offer it at this location. I don't know about the Nampa locations, but the one on Fairview stopped serving lengua. Buche is also served here. Kinda odd to me that the Meridian location would be the one to serve up the funkier meats (for that reason plus the relative cleanliness here, I give them an extra star).

For a place like this, the salsa bar is pretty good. There's always an abundance of limes, radishes, and those marinated carrots mixed in with jalapenos. Chips cost extra though.

I've encountered some landmines along the way. I decided to make a burrito a burrito mojado (wet burrito) one day, but their enchilada sauce tasted cheap like it came straight out of a can. I won't be doing that again. Nor will I be getting a taco salad. The ultra thin fried tortilla shell couldn't hold the ingredients too well, and the whole thing became a soggy mess fairly quickly. Other reviews have complained about getting more potato than egg in their breakfast burrito, and I'd have to agree. I barely saw or tasted any egg in mine.
