Adria was a great server, in the midst of the mother's day rush she was positive, and helpful.

My daughter is always scared of the dentist. She was getting 2 tooth extracted before we get braces. I was so nervous for her cause I know she was nervous. The staff and doctors here are absolutely the best!!!! I can't say enough. I wish I was a kid so I could come here!!

I grew up in SE Idaho and Jakers was the gold star of fine dining for young Michelle and her young standards. I remember going here to celebrate special occasions with my parents, like birthdays or a job promotion. I particularly remember my obsession with their scones (because #BreadLife). When I moved to Boise for college, I remember feeling excited that Jakers was here! But as I became accustomed to true local, fine dining, I realized that Jakers is held back by its "local chain" status. 

There is a decent variety of price options at Jakers. You can get a $13 burger that is alright or a $50 seafood dinner that is alright. They do have a lovely lunch buffet that I really do enjoy. Their soups are fantastic (particularly the Lobster Bisque- huge pieces of real lobster swim in an oh so creamy soup) and the salad bar is fresh and diverse. I have never had a bad dish at Jakers...but I've never had an incredible dish either. They are held back by their large kitchen, filled with line chefs and a corporate menu. For example, a $15 burger should certainly be cooked to perfection. My medium burger was served well done. A $25 plate of trout should be plated beautifully with a stellar sauce. Mine was lacking sauce and pizazz. I will say, the housemade croutons are delicious (#BreadLife).

The waitstaff and bar staff have been friendly and efficient. The layout reminds me a lot of an Outback. Very little imagination or personality. The bar area is quite crowded and definitely not ADA compliant. There is a small ramp up to one of the seating areas, but there should be available seating for friends who need to stay on the ground floor. 

No matter the time of day, Jakers is busy. It is many other people's favorite place and it might be yours too. But the problems that often plague chain restaurants are evident here. If you are going to spend over $30 on a meal, you might find more WOW elsewhere.

Love this place. Been here 4 times this year, not bad given we moved to Idaho Falls a few months ago.

It's been 3 years since my last review, felt it was time to refresh it.

Still feel this place is wonderful, and it is nice to have been here this year given not going much of anywhere in 2020. Everything I reported in 2018 is pretty much still true, and we always have a great experience here. We've recently gotten more into their sandwiches (Reubens) vs. steaks, but recommend both.

We are not dessert people - at all, but their bread pudding is the best we've ever had. But unless you still have a large appetite, a half order is enough for TWO people. Enjoy!

Came into Kahootz at 9pm on a Saturday Night. We were welcomed by a wonderful young lady, and a gentlemen at the bar, while being promptly sat. We were greeted with a great smile and some great opinions on the food. We consulted for awhile talking about the menu. I ordered the Steak Sandwich. My two friends got the French Dip w/ Fries and the Ribeye w/ Potatoes, Asparagus and a Baguette. Starting with the Steak Sandwich, it was very well put together, but lacked in taste. The Ribeye (not $26 worthy) was a mediocre steak that would be served at Denny's with Steak & Eggs. The potatoes were over-seasoned and cold. Although, the Asparagus was not too shabby, mediocre at best. The French Dip was very well put together but the fries were cold, and almost something you would get at Burger King. 

I would definitely not call Kahootz a Steakhouse. Rather, Kahootz: Steak Trailer Park

Great experience for my first visit & consultation. Friendly staff and the doctor was so good in explaining all my options. He really took the time to listen and was very thorough in his questioning. So glad I went and looking forward to see how I can alleviate some pain.

Dr. Williams is amazingly talented and really did a great job helping me with some intense issues I had with a tooth that was almost beyond repair. (I think any other dentist would have pulled it) He took took the time to meticulously repair and prep it for a new bridge. The previous bridge was 15 years old and had failed. I'm terrified of going to the dentist, but he made me feel comfortable. 

I really appreciated that he was up to date on the latest tech and techniques and willing to spend the time to do things correctly. I've had some nightmare experiences in the past with other Dentists, so it's a huge relief to finally have a dentist that I trust.

Anyway, thank you Dr. Williams.

Manager Michelle was sitting 2 booths down from us yelling at 2 employees about getting a door dash order incorrect. Apparently they missed an order of fries. We did not appreciate having to listen to this conversation during our dinner, she should have taken it in the back room. While yelling at them she was not wearing her face mask. Then manager Michelle began asking everyone how their up sales were going , then she began coaching them. Inappropriate and unappreciated!! If she was a going to continue to be the manager she needs some training. Needless to say we will not return to this Chili's

College game day and these idiots can't get a too 10 matchup on the TV but on the bright side we have 10 TVs on yesterday's re-run, as soon as this place went corporate it has gotten worse and worse.  And I've been sitting here for 20 mins writing this review and not one has asked if I need a drink.  What a s show.

This place took a rescue dog from a bad situation and tried to auction it off. There was no vetting process to ensure the dog was going to a safe home, it would simply go to the highest bidder. Although this technically isn't illegal, this is very inhumane. Dogs are a big responsibility especially working breeds and auctioning off a rescue dog to the highest bidder without at all ensuring it's going to a loving safe home is horrific. I can't imagine how a training company could ever find this ethical or do something like this. I would never recommend this company to anyone based on how low they stooped here. After a few people pointed out how horrible this was they simply took down the posts to hide it like it never happened. I have screenshots of their posts but I can't seem to upload them here(if you look on my Google review you can see them) I just wanted to post this here so everyone has an opportunity to see what this company tries to get away with so they have all the facts before making a decision on a training facility.

Animals are not auction items, they require love, care and responsible owners who are ready. Adoption processes should never be side stepped because every animal especially a rescue deserves a loving home and a fighting chance.

If I could give zero stars I would. I went here to get two burgers and onion rings because they normally are amazing and as someone who has been here a dozen or more times just in the past few months I can say normally they are amazing. The girls who helped me at the window were sweet but the manager was an absolute joke. I called because our burgers were burnt and the onion rings we couldn't even eat because of how salty they were. After being a dick about the fact that we had eaten most of the burgers so he couldn't do anything about it and saying he was being nice and offering replacement onion rings after being an ass I just about lost it. He said he's been a manger for 2 years. As a manager myself I would've been fired if I were him for taking to me like that. Won't be coming back and won't support a business that treats customers the way I got treated.

We were really pleasantly surprised when we ate  here for lunch. We haven't been here six months, but we have not found any good Chinese food in the treasure Valley. Yes we're from California, and yes, we are spoiled when it comes to Chinese food. Sorry treasure valley, we love you, but good Asian food is hard to find here. We both ordered the curry chicken. It was outstanding. Lots of nice chopped up vegetables and a very light but flavorful sauce. We've had other entrées since then,  not quite as good but still good. Egg roll is excellent also. Hot and sour soup is very good.  Highly recommend.
We first tried the location in McCall and really liked it. We had a party of 12 and they were able to seat us quickly. The food is good and came out quickly. It was a good experience!

As much as I used to love Firehouse, lately their customer service has been pretty bad. I don't know if they have new employees or just don't care or what but they have messed up 3 times in a row in the past month or so. I've only had issues at this specific location. They don't listen in the drive thru it seems like and when I clarify and they confirm my order yet they dont give me something I specifically asked for or will add something I asked to not include. They continue to put Mayo on my sandwich, ask me 3-4x what kind of bread I want, never give me a total at the screen, and then give me either regular coke or Dr Pepper when I ask for Diet Coke and repeat myself multiple times. I asked for a cookie one of times I went last and they tell me to "choose at the window" and when they mentioned oatmeal I chose that. What did they do? They put a chocolate chip in the bag instead. The last time I tried my soda to make sure it was diet And it wasn't the girl rolled my eyes when I asked for a replacement. It's been shocking to me and I'm a huge fan of Firehouse. I can go on and on about the stupid little mistakes they have been making and I don't know why I continue to go there expecting a different outcome. I'm not one to complain and haven't even wanted make the effort to call and ask for some type of comp but actually hope they get it together and hire people who give a damn and take pride in their work. Sorry Meridian Firehouse but I know you can do better.

MOST IMPORTANTLY- AMAZING BURGERS!!! 
Best burger I've ever had.... 
They forgot our fries in our first order and they made it overly right by not charging us for the next meal. Which is  way more than expected. I appreciate their staff and service super friendly.

Very difficult to reach by phone.  The first time I just waited on hold forever and finally gave up.  I called as soon as they opened up the next day and the kid on the phone sounded very unprofessional and didn't really seem to know what he was doing.  Hopefully, he took down the information and my equipment will be picked up tomorrow.  I hope I never have to use them again!

Fabulous place. We loved the salsa. My husband had the spicy shrimp on the starter menu and I ordered the tortilla soup. Both had great flavor and we would order them again. I had the street tacos which were really good. Husband had the braised Carnitas. We really enjoyed everything we had. 

Wait staff took good care of us. Kept drinks full and very friendly. We were able to sit upstairs and watch the game on the TV which was great. We happened to be downtown but struggled to find parking. Decided to try Village location even though it's not rated as highly. That being said, I couldn't find anything wrong with our visit to warrant a bad review. Would definitely recommend!

I sent an email through their website expecting a call back. They never called me back not a "positive " experience.  I ended up calling them this morning and a girl in a childlike voice answering the phone offered a group consultation.  I requested a private consultation to find out the next avail appointment is not for 3 weeks. I will be looking elsewhere.

My wife and I go here all the time. We usually get the seasalt parmesan flatbread as a starter ,which is very tasty, split a pizza and enjoy a couple of ice cold beers on tap. The food is always great! The only reason I give 4/5 stars is because the service is hit or miss. It seems like every other visit the service isn't up to par. But either way the atmosphere and food makes up for the uncertainty of quality service!
They've gotten my order wrong literally every time I've gone there but the food I've gotten has always tasted good so ‍

Thus place is my new go to for Chinese food in North Meridian.  Sure the orange walls in the place are a little to bright for my taste but I am not there to judge the paint.

The place is obviously family owned and they all work here.  If you have a problem with the waitress having a baby strapped to her back don't visit. If you like very good food at very good prices and large portions, this is your place.  Fast service has been the theme everytime.  

Been working our way through the menu and here are some thoughts:
General Tso's Chicken-  big plate of yummy chicken but wish it had veggies. 
Iron Deluxe Sizzler-  wow!  One of the best dishes I've had at a Chinese restaurant.  Think Chinese fajitas with shrimp, beef, scallops, chicken and all the veggies.
Hunan Beef-  yummy, full of flavor and not that spicy.
Egg Flower Soup:  very good.  

I would seriously recommend this restaurant for its food, it is a beacon of hope above the average Chinese restaurants

Wow. just wow. Daniel was phenomenal! 
to this day i have never had such personal service at a restaurant. being the first time visiting this restaurant, I could tell they wanted to earn our business Not just for today, but for years to come! 
whenever I'm looking for a good evening out, I will definitely remember land ocean.

Always good food and drinks. It's a fun place to just hang out with friends over drinks and appetizers or to grab a full meal. They have a Bavarian pretzel appetizer that is so good and their burgers rock.

I cannot say enough good things about Blaze pizza! It is so yummy and fast!!! You get your own personal pizza and you get to choose your toppings. Their Caesar salad is pretty decent also. I would say customer service is really great here. They are 'fast fired' like they say. Price wise is pretty good too, $7 for your own pizza and to personalize it. My husband and I call it the chipotle of pizza because of the personalizing and the quickness. I recommend getting the pesto sauce drizzled on at the end!

We came in for a late lunch last week after driving in from a 4 day road trip. We were seated immediately, but the service was a bit slow, and my order was taken incorrectly, which meant my entire family was almost finished eating by the time they delivered the correct salad. Despite this error, the food was tasty and while the service wasn't exceptional, correcting the error quickly saved the meal. Special thanks to the employee who wasn't our server but made sure that she took care of us the rest of the time!
Good food. Good drinks and huge beer selection.  More food than you could eat in a lifetime. But a chain so if you are into that...go!

What a great find. We loved the food and the owner was so nice and helpful.  I like my food with a little heat and this place delivered, it was yummy and made my eyes water, loved it. A family owns the business and I like to support local business's.  We will be back.

Hooray, finally a Ramen Shop that comes close to being authentic. 

The menu is large enough to cover the Ramen gambit with some Asian stir-fry dishes. Since we only had Ramen bowls for our first visit, I am going to limit my review to those dishes. We had 2 different Ramen bowls: The tonkatsu chasiu ramen and the tantanmen ramen bowl. Both had clean tasting miso broth with distinctly different tastes, as they should. This was not an asian restaurant where they seem to use the same sauce/gravy on all the dishes. Kudos here.

We did look over the appetizers and would have the spicy wontons and the potstickers, but the crab rangoons are pretty gweilowish.

Surprisingly, the broth did not seem to overload my system with salt from soy sauce. Kudos, again.

We will be back again and I might try one of their stirfry dishes. BTW, the place is clean and was busy for an early Monday dinner hour. The food came promptly though. 

Good slurping Asian Noodle place.

Seriously liking this place. We arrived minutes before happy hour ended. Good happy hour menu. The third or fourth?? restaurant at this location and so far my fave. Love the dim lighting and industrial vibe although you combine that with 40+ vision and a small print menu and you can't see the menu but I guess that's what your phone light is for. 

We had the Steak Tip Dip Sandwich which was very good but so saucy and juicy that you need to eat it immediately or it gets all soggy and messy. I kept detecting goat cheese (which I'm not a fan of) but it's not an ingredient used in this sandwich so I'm not sure what I was tasting. The parmesan fries were very good and crispy.

Our server was polite and efficient.

We'll definitely be back to try something different.

This was incredible! If you're looking for a lunch spot, this is a great choice. You get a good amount of food for a good price. I was super impressed with both the pizza  and salad I got. Ingredients taste fresh. I was super impressed.

How does it take 45 minutes to cook a pizza?
Got there 5 minutes past the pick up time just to be safe and still waited 20 minutes.

After an evening of Tennis, my husband and I just wanted a bite to eat without cooking. We decided on Kahootz. We were immediately seated which normally they are very busy. Our server greeted us and was very prompt. I ordered the ribeye and hubby got a shrimp dish. Both were very tasty. The atmosphere was chill. We will be going again.
After contacting management, Holli offered a gift card that never showed up, I have sent a follow up email regarding the gift card with no replies.

We love going to this place. The "Early Dine" specials are awesome. We often sit at the bar, have a cocktail and dinner. It is our "go to" place. My husband loves the Crispy Chicken Salad with the honey lime dressing, my favorite is the 6oz Sirloin with two sides. Their Caesar dressing is also very delicious!
Oh man!  We slipped in just in time for happy hour and Martin served us up so well. Food and beverages were amazing!

Good is so inconsistent that we have stopped going.  We have been there 4 times and for the price and the inconsistency it's definitely not worth it.  We rather go to Crave or Coynes for less money and better quality food and service.

Went to a long lost hot spot.   It was easier when we could arrive on bicycles, enjoy beers on tap , and eat outside.  Tonight's visit , post COVID found all of us with new protocols.  The wait was an hour - we ordered wine and waited in the heated waiting area.  The staff was more than helpful - safety a priority.  We sat at the bar and enjoyed our usual favorites.   Mine is the French Dip with awesome fries - my husband selected the pasta with meatballs.  Remember.  It's worth the wait.  .

When I have to make a trek out to the wilds of the Autobahn, er, Eagle Road, Pueblo Lindo is one of my first choices when looking for sustenance. Plenty of chain restaurants and fast food joints flank the road, but Pueblo Lindo has the charm and service only found at smaller, local eateries. 

The decor is rustic Mexican and charming. Staff are attentive without being disruptive. I love that they leave a carafe of water at the table. 

I've only been here during lunch. Their chips are fresh and perfectly salted. The salsa is piquant and stands out from the typical Mexican restaurant salsa schtick. I'd like to see some beans along with the chips, but that could be due to my American palate. 

I've had the Pueblo Lindo enchilada and the burrito. They are similar, but the enchilada sauce has a mole-ish base; the taste of peanut is distinct. The meat is always tender and the food is steaming hot. 

Next time you're in the Meridian area, give this place a shot. It's tucked away from the fray, and very worth a visit.

I was in town for work and had an opportunity to stop into Donut & Dog and wow is it a fun place! Love the aesthic of the shop and the staff were all super duper friendly. I ordered a 4 pack of fun donuts to go, they were all so beautiful I almost didn't want to eat them! The Vanilla Glazed and Maple Bacon were my favorites, love that amazing brioche dough. My cuban coffee was fantastic as well.. I wish I lived locally because I would come back for a donut, dog and a beer sometime... Next time I am in Eagle I will be stopping back in for sure!

Found Kahootz on Yelp while at an event in Boise.  The 30 minute wait was well worth it! I had the Prime Rib which was cooked to perfection and my husband had the filet.  Both were superb! Crime Brûlée' for desert.  The waitstaff was fantastic.  Would definitely return if ever in the area again!!!

Had the worst gel manicure ever!!! The shape wasn't what I requested, my nails were visibly slanted and prior to her putting on the color I told her and she said she'd fix it after the gel polish. She left a huge gap between my nail color and cuticle. When I addressed my nails still not being straight she said they were I showed her and she insisted they were. The sides are rough. While I was getting my nails done another lady came in to have them fix her nails that they did yesterday. I told the lady they do a horrible job and this will be my first and last time and she said hers as well. Do Not Go Here!!!

Losing confidence in Yardhouse .
A couple of weeks I received a cup of iced tea with lipstick stains all over it .
The manager discounted our food and gave us a free dessert . Which I thought was awesome .
We came back tonight and the over all the experience was ok .
I ordered a Cesar salad with salmon for my Mother in law for Togo and when we arrived home she open the bag and all that was in the bag was garlic fries which we did not order.
I called the restaurant and the hostess try to play it off like we forgot a bag which we didn't because we were given the wrong bag.
I asked to speak to a manager and he credited me back the salad but didn't try to make up for the failed customer service .
I'm not in a hurry to go back to this location .
I want to mention names but I'll refrain at this time .

InsideOut has a mission to help trafficked victims off the streets of Idaho.  If that's not enough reason to give them a 5 star review, then perhaps this will be...They conduct a professional salon made-up of talented stylists who truly care about their clients.  I am grateful to have found this salon.  It has been a true blessing to meet Dawn and get to know her staff!

I've always wanted tattoos and as soon as I turned 18 I booked an appointment with Kingsley. He designed a beautiful butterfly piece to go on the back of my arm. He was extremely flexible with scheduling. When I got to the shop, Kingsley was very kind and talked to me the entire time he was working on my piece. I couldn't be more happy! I will never go anywhere else for future tattoos.
Great food and staff is extremely nice and friendly. Only stopped for lunch as were passing through town but would definitely come back here again!
I would give them a 5 star rating if they weren't so over priced.  Great service, great products, just a bit to expensive.

So I absolutely have to give Jakers bar staff, 5 stars. We have only been there for Happy Hour, albeit many times, and have always had impeccable service. Their bartenders are on it, cooks and servers too. Grace is our favorite. We don't eat big, so HH apps are all we get. Which leads me to the Steak Bites...omg...melt in your mouth...and $3 off during HH. I literally get these every time, although husband tries other things, all good, according to him. It's busy, yet still a relaxing vibe due to the ambiance. We love Jakers, and hope you do too.
They had a friendly staff and excellent service, I usually don't write reviews but I took the time to do so because the service was that good. Food was also great.

Well I did it again! Inhaled my food before taking photos- sorry! U would have seen perfectly cooked sausage, pulled pork & brisket. Two hush puppies that we're yummy yummy yummy! And a refreshing side of creamy-yet-light coleslaw. I ordered via DoorDash, so I didn't get a dine in experience- so I appreciated the nicely packed meal & the choice of two sauces. The meats all seemed high quality & very fresh- a definite recommend!

Wish it was better. Really wanted to like this local spot. Tried lunch when they first opened. Not very good. Wanted to give them a second chance, after they were open a while. Went to dinner in October. Hot weather. Flies everywhere. Landing on us. Landing on our food. Seemed like thousands of flies. Staff ignored the flies. All the tables were smacking and waving the flies away. Fool not good second time. Bad experience all around. We went with another couple. Next time we planned dinner out with this same couple, they said "Not Homestead"!

First off, our waitress was awesome and the food was great, but we waited for a seat for an hour. The man that greeted us at the door originally said the wait would be 20-30. My family waited for 30 minutes before we realized that there was PLENTY of tables that were cleaned and were ready to seat people. So I asked the man at the front why we couldn't sit down, and he said they were working on it. About 20 minutes later, I overheard the man talking to his boss, saying that we had requested a booth, which we had specifically said we DID NOT want a booth as it could not fit our family, then a family that had came in 30 minutes AFTER us got seated at a table with 6 seats. I asked why they were being seated before us, and the man said again, that they were working on it. I haven't been to chili's in a LONG time, and maybe that kind of service is normal at chili's now, but I was VERY dissatisfied.

At 9:00 this morning there were ZERO cashiers available. Only option was self checkout. When I get a discount for doing someone else's job, I'll use self checkout. I know employees are hard to find and keep. If you can't staff the store, don't open. Have yet to see a manager man a register. Not a good image to present to your customers.

We came here for the first time with my Fiancé & was greeted by a gentleman named Patrick who was very polite. In less then a few minutes we were seated & introduced to our waiter Kyle. Kyle is amazing & definitely made our experience so much better with his humor & personality! The food is amazing & the restaurant itself is so upscale, which makes it perfect for special occasions or a date night! Everything we ordered was literally perfect! This is our new date night spot for sure!

I ordered takeout on May 18th.  I picked up my order and was pleased to see coronavirus protocol being observed.  However when I got home, I discovered my order was short items.  This in spite of the checklist attached to my order that it had been checked for accuracy. I called Buffalo Wild Wings and the manager said I was welcome to come back and pick up the shorted items.  That didn't work for me as the order I picked up would be cold by the time I spent my gas and time to make up for their mistake.  Then the manager said he would send me a gift certificate to make up for the problem and that he would put it in the mail right away.  Well, a month has gone by, and no gift certificate.  I will no longer trust Buffalo Wild Wings and will get my wings elsewhere.

So glad that they are open. Still have to wear mask still you get a table. Atmosphere was wonderful. Tyrus our server was great and very personable. Food was great. I had a grilled chicken rice bowl. It was just right amount of food and SUPER yummy!!

I went to a new patient appointment this week but I didn't make it past the waiting room. The screen in the lobby was playing chiropractic 'facts'. I stood there waiting for the receptionist and read, slide after slide, as they down played the safety and effectiveness of vaccines, as they highlighted harms while ignoring benefits, and finally, as they suggested chiorpractic care as a cure and preventer of the flu and other diseases.

The slides referenced the Splanish flu of 1918. Upon personal research I could not find a single study that confirmed chiropractic is a suitable treatment or preventer of the cute.

When I got to the counter I canceled my appointment. I don't support medical providers who spread vaccine skepticism.

Ten years ago I was hospitalized for pneumonia that was a result of the flu. Last year, my husband's college friend died of the flu, leaving a young family behind. Telling people chiropractic care is a suitable alternative to vaccines is dangerous. As such, I will not be using this chiropractor.

Having heard good things about Jakers we decided to start our New Years eve with them. We made a reservation and looked forward to a nice steak dinner that would not materialize. Upon being seated, the waiter was quick to direct us to the buffet. Apparently, heir buffet is an event that is offered only a few evenings each year. There was a limited menu alternative, but the waiter's praise for the buffet convinced us to forego the anticipated steaks. Poor decision. We realized later that by going the buffet route, our waiter reduced his role to clearing a couple of plates and checking on our beverages. His effort at both tasks was weak. The buffet too was disappointing. No specific item is worth mentioning.  We may try them again for a true steak dinner. But it will take some time for this poor experience to fade from memory.

i'm going to be honest- donuts are top 3 favorite dessert for me. it goes ice cream, cookies, donuts. I absolutely adore them. being keto is not easy, and I can tell you if i'm going to cheat on my diet it's going to be with one of those 3 things- or rice. LOL. I live for rice.

anyway, the ultimate best donut on earth for me is krispy kreme. the hot plain glazed and the chocolate glazed are just the best thing ever. I love this location and I have to say we frequent it. maybe once or twice a month. they are always fast, friendly, and it's consistent. I have never had one single poor experience here in all my years.

thank you for existing, beautiful krispy kreme. you are amazing.
Tasty! Hot good food, just what I was looking for with a ramen place. Good prices and nice atmosphere

Despite all the negative reviews this restaurant seems to generate my husband and I decided to give try one Friday evening. We've recently bought a new house in an area that no one seems to want to deliver pizza to, so huge thanks to Chicago Connection for being the only pizza company we've found to do so to date. 

The order process was simple, and the delivery arrived just in time. We ordered a medium Double Deluxe Pepperoni (two layers of pepperoni over and under extra mozzarella cheese, $19.95) and single cheese bread (garlic bread with melted mozzarella served with marinara sauce, $3.95). I'm not very used to deep-dish style pizza, so it was A-okay for us. I mean, you can't really go wrong with pizza. But it didn't blow my mind away. There was an excellent amount of cheese however not enough pepperoni for my liking, so then it was overwhelmingly cheesy. I ended up slapping some of my own pepperoni and it did the job! The cheese bread was alright as well.

Overall this was a subpar experience. I will order again only because (1) no one else orders out to me and (2) I'm a huge believer in second chances. Maybe I just ordered the wrong things? If anyone has any suggestions or favorite menu items please let me know. I would love to update this to a 5 star review! :)

Pretty tasty and love the beer selection. I would probably get happy hour here but feel less inclined to return for dinner.  I ordered the grilled cheese and tomato bisque but found myself still hungry afterwards. Service was unbelievable though. A member of our party was cold so our waiter moved a heater over to us immediately.

My friends and I frequently go to Yard house for dinner/late night drinks. The servers are always very kind and willing to help in any way they can to make your experience better. Additionally, the food is incredible! If you're ever visiting or looking for a great spot, Yard House is the place to go!

I just ordered out there and first off the young boy could not care less to take his headphones out of his ears or even say welcome. I ordered a poke bowl and it was very below a average. They don't make it in front of you, so the portion sizes are extremely small and I even ordered a medium. The rice had either been sitting out a long time or was underdone because it was very hard. They also left the stems on the cilantro so you have to break them off yourself or enjoy crunching on cilantro stems with your food. I always go to paddles up poke and now I know why.

I just wanted to express my disappointment via public review even though we have already spoken to the manager. I came in (4/22/21) with two of my friends to Texas Roadhouse and left very shortly after, due to the blatant immaturity of the hostess 'Alexis' alongside the rest of the girls at the host desk. All three of us watched her point fingers at us and whisper to her coworkers and laugh OUT LOUD and it happened more than once in the very short time that we stood there. We did nothing wrong and for a group of girls who don't even know how to fill in their eyebrows correctly or fix the bumped ends on their hair to be so blatantly rude and inconsiderate to their guests be seems to be a morality issue on their part. We left completely humiliated and embarrassed, confused and very uncomfortable and we never even got seated. All three of us have worked as servers and bartenders and have moved on to bigger and better careers since then, but we would never dream of treating customers how they did to us, which was BEYOND unprofessional. We went to Winger's instead where we were met with genuine smiles, compliments and friendliness, and we were sure to tip VERY generously (25% on a $120 check.) for their EXCELLENT service. If they're going to talk about the people who are literally paying their bills then maybe walk away and don't do it right in front of them. I truly hope they learn how to treat people, especially complete strangers with respect. Never coming back.

My friend and I were looking for a new place to get our nails done and came across this place. She was just getting a polish change and I got a fresh full set of acrylics, usually I get fun designs and glitter and all that but this time I only did one solid color and I still paid more than what I would have if I got 3 designs. I'm so shocked and they don't even reach to my cuticles and don't look very natural sitting on my nail bed. Also one thing is I can understand some Vietnamese and they were clearly talking about my friend and I while we were having a conversation. I'm disgusted by this place and their employees. Needless to say I will never come back and will go out of my way to tell my friends not to come here.

The staff are half and half - sometimes nice sometimes rude. Got one that gave me an obvious look of disapproval when I spent a pretty penny without a coupon. Then I've had a couple who were fine, nice people. Neither here nor there.

My major issue with Hobby Lobby is their limited yarn selection. 1-2 rows of yarn selections (and very few 36" circular needles). 

Granted, they have TONS of silk flowers. They came to mind first when I needed some silk flowers, but they ended up not having enough shades of the green I wanted.

If you don't care too much about service and you need some options for crafts, this is an acceptable place to look. But if you want yarn, don't waste your time.

Have always loved this place since the days when we had to drive from Eagle to Bown Crossing. Love love love their European style pizzas. Perfect! We've had a few lunches lately where the waitstaff seemed more interested in visiting with each other and hanging out chatting at the bar than keeping their customers' drinks filled. Twice now we've had to flag them down to either get refills or pay the bill. That's my only complaint. Otherwise great food.

Wow. This place blew me away. From the service, to the decor, to the food...amazing! My table of 4 all ordered different dishes & we all loved our food. Everything was perfectly seasoned, cooked & presented perfectly, & tasted delicious. After eating my food I understood why there was a 35 minute wait for a table. We will be back again & again. The only downfall is this place is a bit pricey but definitely well worth it.

All they want is your money, They will give you an estimate and then the estimate will be 30% off. When you call them up they will blame your Insurance and not care for the long standing customer. If you are okay with your budget being screwed up every single time in this economy feel free to associate with them.
Very disappointing experience, Twice
My daughter drove over there tonight to get us dinner and she was told, "sometimes we close early".  Neither one of us will be going back.

What can I say, I really love Blaze Pizza! I have been out of the country for a while and the first place I wanted to eat when I came back was Blaze pizza. It might be my favorite pizza place in the Boise metropolitan area. I love Blaze because you can always get what you want and the service is helpful, non-judgmental and friendly. Pizzas here are so affordable and proportional to the cost. I was able to utilize a two for one promotion (get the app!) and as a result, my significant other and I were able to have a filling dinner and two lunches. I also love the blood orange drink that they have here, it is a must try! If it is too sugary, if there is such a thing, you can always water it down some and go back for more.

Heard about Land Ocean so went and tried to out. 
The lobster tail and steak were very good. 
The only hesitation to dining here for most people will be that they only serve beer and wine at this time.  Atmosphere is quite nice

Great food! Smoked wings, burgers, brisket all good. Onion rings are my favorite side.  Servers and staff are good people, friendly and courteous.  The Holiday dinner was excellent! I could eat the creamed corn everyday. As you can probably tell I frequent this place alot! Definitely recommend!

We love visiting for lunch and enjoying the leftovers the next day.  Each time in we have tried something new and each time have been so happy with what we've gotten. I'm super fussy (much to my husbands chagrin) and would never turn down lunch or dinner here.

Worst customer service known to man kind! I repeat if you want sushi, refrain from this place!! Just don't go here. Don't recommend at all. I ordered a poke bowl, did not get what I asked for, when I asked for a refund. Manager refused and called me a liar and said I ordered the wrong thing. Which I double, triple check everything. On top of that the salmon and tuna tasted 10 days old. And still refused to get me my refund. Like I said go somewhere else. Not worth it. To make matters worse, the manager started yelling at me telling me I was wrong and he was right.

The fact that this place even exists, makes me sick to my stomach!

Today's pet store highlight is Puppyland in Meridian, Idaho. 

Puppyland sources all of their puppies from a large  USDA broker/dealer called JAKS Puppies Inc located in Iowa. JAKS pulls from hundreds of puppy mills and sells them to pet stores in 20 states. 

When pet stores use a broker, it makes it nearly impossible for consumers to do their research prior to purchase as pet stores in ID are not required to disclose the breeder information. 

Sadly, consumers have purchased sick puppies and reached out to us for help or have wanted to know the true origin of their puppy. This has allowed us to connect JAKS and Puppyland to the following breeders. 

Indiana
-Lucas & Rhoda Miller: does not appear to be USDA licensed. 
-Francis & Margaret Wagler: 36 adult breeding dogs.

Iowa
-Mike Decker: 105 adult breeding dogs. 

Minnesota
-AJs Angels: 758 adult breeding dogs.

Missouri
-Gary Simmons: 54 adult breeding dogs. 
-Lester Troyer: 76 adult breeding dogs. 

Wisconsin 
-John Lambright: 33 adult breeding dogs. (has not been USDA inspected in over 2 years) 

Along with sourcing from very large puppy mills, Puppyland has a clause in their contract that states they will void all health guarantees should a customer post publicly any comments or reviews of any negative nature and that any payments, fees, or reimbursements that have been paid by Puppyland regarding health warranty will be due back immediately. 

https://bailingoutbenji.com/buyer-beware-jaks-puppies/
#researchbeforeyoubuy #endpuppymill

"Dance 10.  Looks 3."  Song title from Broadway hit "A Chorus Line" describing a dancer could be applied to Crave! after their second audition for delivery and food respectively.  (See earlier review for details about the business.)  They continue to be best at the delivery part - on time, well packaged, arrives hot and cold as appropriate for the dish - and the delivery drivers are the best - professional, friendly, helpful with questions.  It is Crave Delivery's food part that needs attention to get things right - both for the descriptions on the app listing to be complete and for the food to be prepared correctly.  While our first experience with Crave! left us eager for encore, the second pass made us think we'll wait a bit to see if the owners can better arrange for kitchen supervision.

Food specifics follow.  Some is good news.  But the bad news much outweighed the good this time and for a $52 order - before tax, delivery fee and tip for driver which put it over $70, we expect more professionally prepared food.  This is not about being a finicky consumer.   Crave Delivery was launched purposefully during covid19 days to leverage the fact that people are ordering take away not dining in.  Their business model is to prepare food according to specifications of the 'big name' restaurants who sponsor each dish on the menus.  Getting it right needs some work. And a problem they really need to fix for this order from app model, their dish descriptions are incomplete with ellipses (...) leading nowhere and/or with descriptions that don't match the food delivered. 

*  A dish that highlights the problems with the incomplete descriptions is Panzanella Salad ($13 from ESR - Seattle based Ethan Stowell's 'at home' Italian themed eats).  The app listed heirloom tomatoes, toasted croutons and red wine vin...  Let's assume vinaigrette for the last.  But what it did not say was this was prepared in "deconstructed" style with the heirloom tomatoes cut into big chunks - like quarters.  That's fine but not what we expected based on classic panzanella preparation and had they been more descriptive we could have been more prepared.  Sadly, those heirloom tomatoes were icy cold, as if refrigerated for a long time and so they were spongy and flavorless as is the case if you refrigerate fresh tomatoes.   We did not eat them.  Also the croutons scattered about were deep fried and oily not toasted.   We could not eat them.  The (few) chunks of mozzarella di bufola were good though, so was the scatter of fresh marjoram leaves, slivered red onions and green and black olive halves.  The vinaigrette was awful - as if they had used red wine and not red wine vinegar to whisk into oil.  Panzanella is one of our fav dishes and this was a big miss.

*Crab Cakes ($14 sponsored by Elliot's Oyster House in Seattle) were our fav of this delivery. Two good plump crab-rich cakes, a tasty fresh corn 'relish' alongside (but too little for two cakes) but alas the (small portion) potato salad didn't quite fit the description (another ... issue) and was really overdressed.  But we would order these again.

*Rigatoni with spicy Italian sausage ($10 for small plate portion and from ESR) arrived with perfectly cooked for al dente rigatoni and kudos to them as that is hard enough for eateries to get right to service at table let alone for delivery.  The arrabiata style spicy sauce was good and the pasta was dressed just right too.  But while the flavors in the sausage were on-point, it was as if they had made the sausage into a patty, pan fried it then cut it up in four chunks.  Neither sauteed pieces of sausage nor links sliced into pieces as might be expected with this pasta but more like a sausage patty shape one might get on a breakfast sandwich then cut up.  Enough wrong for us that we wouldn't order this dish again.  (Keeping in mind that in my Italian husband's culinary view some things are sacrilege.  Your opinion may vary.  As they say.) 

*Cacio e Pepe ($15 also ESR) translates cheese and pepper and is a dish that has only 3 ingredients; spaghetti or linguini pasta, grated pecorino or parmesan cheese and cracked black pepper.  Steps are few too; hot pasta water is used to sort of emulsify the cheese into a light sauce then cracked black pepper is added and tossed with the pasta until each strand has silky coat.  A simple dish that is simply delicious when done right.  Alas, while the linguine arrived perfectly cooked - kudos to them - but looking nude atop a very little liquid in the bottom of container that may have been the water emulsfied cheese but flavors were not as expected when we 'dug down' to find it and toss it with the dry pasta and there was literally not one spec of cracked pepper.  Fortunately we could add fresh cracked black pepper at home.  But for the entire dish, since this is supposed to represent ESR Home's preparation my husband said "ESR would be appalled."

The food and service was meh. The portions were small and flavor was not there. Unfortunately there aren't many Chinese restaurants near the Wahooz water park, but we we ended up spending more here than if we were to pay for the over priced food at the water park. Water had no ice, and it was a hot day today. Needless to say, I won't be back.
Hot Dog Cold 11:30 am is when I bought my dog.  $5 for a cold dog not going to fly with me.  And if you do no like sage be careful... there is lots of sage on dog.

Looking for a great new place to visit for breakfast/brunch/lunch? This is the place! Located in the old Souper Salad location at Eagle and Ustick, this is a real gem! I had the Fisherman omelet, hubby had the Idahoan. My omelet had a salmon filet, tender spinach, green onion and tomato, bathed in homemade hollandaise sauce. Yummmm!!! Salmon was perfectly cooked! Hubby's Idahoan was steak, onions, mushrooms and peppers, adorned with plenty of cheese. Service was awesome, iced tea freshly brewed. Everyone that we saw in the restaurant was dining happily on some wonderful breakfast meal. Go, I understand that Saturday and Sunday's are premium wait times, but go!!! Skip Le Peep and go here! You won't be sorry!

We went today on New Year's Eve & honestly I wish I could give a hundred stars! Or at least hug the young lady (guessing owner) who battled obscene amounts of to-go orders, a full restaurant, irate impatient customers,  door dash drivers who honestly I pray dont make this business decide against door dash,  & handled all of it with kindness & heart & a smile upon her face! I would have just locked the door & said "Get Out!"! I saw a side of Idaho I didn't like tonight! But! I saw a restaurant owner that took that old adage "the customer is always right" & never once faltered! We will go back on a less busy evening! Just because of this young lady!
If we could turn away from people acting unkind & impatient we got to see probably most of the owners family helping out.. Including this sweet toddler wanting to help her grandmother clear tables. Even this little baby was like "I help! It okay!" . The food was good & had good flavor. Wish there was a family dinner option but we honestly didnt want to ask too many questions. We even said we would go to cut her stress but she was like "it okay..". Honestly the food could have been awful (it wasnt) but the customer service and the lady I believe was the owner just made me want to come back! You do not see customer service like that anymore! It's sad but it's the truth! The way this young woman handled 10+ people,  the phone, to go orders and the restaurant was like watching a beautiful ballet. They took orders right up until closing! And my jaw drops shes going to do it all again tomorrow! I need a vacation & I was just watching! Nothing was spicy... Ice Tea was real brewed (another rare find)... Food was flavorful and plentiful! It's a small space so we were food watching other tables & they ours. We got to chat with some of the nicer customers and it really felt like on a regular night this would be like a family dinner experience. I enjoy that! I can see how popular they are & hope a bigger place might be in their future! I've been looking for years for that mom & pop Chinese experience since my place on 11th downtown closed. In Idaho Chinese food kinda is a crap shoot but this was a pleasant find. Wish I had tried it sooner! I hope this young lady if shes not the owner gets a raise! And if she is the owner I hope someone gives her a hug! Not everyone tonight was unkind but just too many were! Please help give this great business more kindness and go try a fun new spot for lunch or supper

I took the family here this time.  We tried other dishes:. Chicken with broccoli, General Tsao's chicken (aka Orange Chicken), wonton soup war, Pork Chow mein (which I ordered last time I was here).

I have to say, the dishes were delicious.  Especially the War Wonton Soup and General Tsao's chicken, which we asked for non spicy.  It is very fresh, thin crispy battered, very flavorful chicken.

Service was still attentive as my first visit.  It is a bit far from where we live, but since it is a "family approved" restaurant.  We sure will be back.

Got the ramen + appetizer combo. Highly recommend the tantanmen. The broth was perfect - light, creamy, and perfect amount of spice. The milk tea boba was also a good way to top off our meal. Will be back to try other items on the menu.

Where do I begin?  We had a dinner reservation but thought we wanted to get a cocktail early in the bar, so met a great waiter, Dan.  He was vivacious and made us feel right at home .... helped us make the right decisions ... ... great drinks!  Then they came right on time to seat us .... then we met our waiter, Law .... great guy!  He took care of every need and again, made us feel right at home.  Happy dude!!  Two of us had never eaten at this restaurant ... one had and was pleased is why they thought we needed to try it.  After another cocktail then I noticed the table behind us being cleaned off ..... and, to my surprise it was the owner.  When is the last time you quietly saw an owner help to make the restaurant run more efficient?  I can't remember when!  I ponder THIS is one reason this restaurant runs so well ... the owner cares and is there to watch and help when needed.  Two people had the small Prime Rib with baked potatoes .... GREAT!  One had the coconut shrimp with baked potato with cheese sauce.  YUM.  Oh, and BTW ... the coconut shrimp were better than the old Murphy's on Broadway or the old Angell's downtown!!  All our meals were excellent!  We were very pleased with everything.  Scones were delish!  Our favorite was being so well taken care of by Dan and Law .... great servers!  Thanks Jake for your continued dedication to serving your customers!  We'll be back!

I hate leaving unkind reviews.. but... my mom ordered the Taco salad with Picadillo beef.  You needed a magnifying glass to find any meat. When mentioned to waitress her comment "that's just how they make them here, whe I order a taco salad with chicken, it's hard to find any"
not good coming from waitress.  And nothing was done about it. Also hubby had the chicken buritto and it was really lite on the chicken. Now I had the veggie Chili relleno and it was awesome. Moral of this story, they don't give out much meat, but veggie dishes are great

Yummy! Our friends suggested we meet here for dinner and we are so glad to have a new "go to" Mexican place. The service was outstanding-for our party of 8 our young server was amazing. Our food came out a little slow but she made sure we knew they were working on it, when we placed our drink order she let us know our drinks would be made and served by another server due to her age. She made things easy for our kids and kept everyone's drinks filled. She was personable, happy and professional. And the food was delicious!!! What a great new find, can't wait to introduce more friends to this place.

Had it delivered via door dash. Ramen was great! Togo set up was really nice. We will be back to try some other things

I just found my new favorite restaurant.   We had the French Dip sandwich and the wedge salad.  They literally tasted like I made them myself.  Not over done, just perfect.  
Ellie was our sever and she is great!  Nice lady!! Friendly, courteous, and she knows the menu. I can't wait to come back and try some desert.  This place is sooooo goood!!

Land Ocean (2 locations in NoCal) has ventured into Treasure Valley (Ustick and Eagle, in the Trader Joe's shopping center), and we headed over after church for brunch to test drive the place. Still in the soft opening stage (doors opened 11/26) it's a tender time for any new restaurant and the parking lot reflected that. We really enjoyed our meal there, so I hope this review helps fill that lot up a bit. 1st, the interior ~ love the vibe, warm tones with white, 2 level booth/banquette seating, bar central in the room. Not overtly large, supper club'ish ambiance. Not to be confused with prissy or pretentious - neither the vibe or menu project that. Proper professional employee etiquette, from reception to serving staff, I like that. Complimentary mini blueberry muffins; we added bottomless mimosas ~ a good way to start. We ordered the Ahi Poke Taco appetizer bc we're suckers for Ahi and Taco in the same title. They were delicious. Hubs had the Italian Sausage and Bacon Skillet, which he pronounced yummy. He's a GF kinda guy so passed on the gravy; but I can attest to its texture and balance of flavors being just right. I ordered Crab Cake Benedict, daring choice for a first date with the kitchen.  Crab cakes were generous and properly presented. My tastes lean toward a bit more seasoning, but the mango hollandaise was unique and worked well with the crab. Kitchen struggled a bit with a medium poach on my eggs, but I allow that they are still getting their land legs back there and I'll try this dish again. Breakfast potatoes were perfect texture, seasoned properly and we did them justice. We finished Brunch with an Apple Crisp - not that we were still hungry - the kitchen has a great feel for providing without portion overkill - but it's a fave and needed to be sampled. Arriving with standard vanilla ice cream scoop, the balance of sweet and spice was good, not spectacular, and even apple slices in prep will improve the finished texture at presentation. Final note: I'd like to see the kitchen provide some GF prep options because a lot of folks require that: but based on our overall experience I'm going to give Land Ocean a solid 4 stars; not bad straight out of the chute. Definitely worth a visit and now is the time while there isn't a line out the door, because I think Land Ocean will develop a fan club. Footnote: some funky filter on my phone camera has these pix a little 'warm', lol! Look past it, please

I have been driving by this location on Fairview and kept wanting to try after looking at their menu. I was ordering curbside pickup, and even though I live close, I was aware that the food would not be as good as it would have been hd i dined in. 
I ordered 6 wings, with BBQ sauce 
BBQ Pork Tacos
"Sliced" Brisket Sandwich with More Heat, less sweet Sauce
Potato Salad
Fries
Fried Pickles

Food was ready by the time indicated, so far so good...
When I got home i started unpacking the food and we dove right in.
My wife was having the BBQ tacos, fries and fried pickles. The tacos are two small pork tacos on corn tortillas. I did not try these, however after eating one, she offered the other to me and indicated it wasnt good. She ate 3 fried pickles, and left all the rest, because again, they were not good. The fries, were, well fries, and once not piping hot, always fall into the disappointment category.
I started off with a couple of wings. I enjoyed the sauce, and the wings themselves were prepared well. This was the last enjoyable moment, I'll ever have from RandR, as I excitedly moved onto my brisket sandwich. First thing I npticed, was these are cubes of brisket, with a high amount of fat, very little meat. As I was putting the two pieces of bun together, I noticed that my brisket was also dry like the Sahara, and I feverishly looked for bbq sauce in the bag... there was none. No BBQ sauce, more heat, or otherwise, on your BBQ meal is pretty disheartening. 
I decided to call RandR and explain what happened. This was when i was told, that the BBQ sauce is free, so its not like I was charged for it, and that there was nothing that they could do... I let her know that I would include that in my reviews. She told me I could speak to a manager, and I told her if there is no way to remedy this, then I'm not willing to waste my time and get more angry for nothing to happen. She thought it was a good time to hang up on me. I was not swearing, or raising my voice, but apparently they are told it's okay to hang up on their customers, and tell them, too bad so sad, excuses for their shortcomings. This is of course my first and last visit to R and R, and will use the relationships my 20 years in the valley have gained, to spread the word. Very disappointed, in food, and appalled at the level of service. 

If you are looking for poor to mediocre BBQ, with horrible service, and possible no BBQ sauce on your BBQ meal, this is your place. If you enjoy high quality BBQ and high level of service, I would try any of their competitors, there are plenty out here.

I don't want to sound like a snob, but I live in Los Angeles and have a huge variety of restaurants and cuisines to choose from.  Mongo's Grill was amazing.  I was in Idaho for family business (a funeral) and my family took me there when I first arrived.  I had no idea what to expect, but it was incredible.  You have a huge - really humungous variety of ingredients to choose from and then you have it grilled and served to you fresh.  You can do anything.  I'm a big fan of Korean BBQ and it sort of reminded me of that experience except that they do all of the cooking so you don't have to deal with the smelly clothes (a big plus for me) and the options are wonderfully over-the-top.  It does take a while to get used to how to choose your sauce/oil options, but after a couple of tries, you get to learn (I'm a pretty great chef and foodie) what combos will work for your own taste.  I think many people focus on the noodle/meat options, but there's pasta, mac-n-cheese, taco, wrap and burrito options as well, and a fullly stocked salad bar.  The entire staff is courteous and friendly, remembers you (I went in again during a 4 day trip - it was that good) and the service is great.  I go to Boise often for family stuff and this was a true surprise and delight.  If I lived there, I could see how I could get addicted to it.  The prices are extremely reasonable (super cheap for LA or big city standards) and if you go for the unlimited (all-you-can-eat), you can't go wrong.  I wish they had this in the Los Angeles area because I think it would make a fortune.  Sure, I wasn't around when the place first opened, and perhaps they ironed out some issues that any new restaurant has to deal with, but I was truly impressed and I'm a bit of an LA foodie-snob.

I'm glad we found this place! They seriously know how to make a tasty steak with perfect grill marks!  We've visited this location 4 times and the Nampa location, once.  We always receive friendly service and seating at the bar top is fast.  I like my NY steak rare and it always comes out that way.  Even the General Manager stops by to say hi and asks how things are.  I've had a couple different sides, veggies, chili (this is a good one with cheese and red onions) & steak fries but ultimately my favs are, the baked potato smothered with butter and sour cream and mashed potatoes with white gravy, like the stuff you put on biscuits!! Yum!!  Anyway, my husband has also had the cheeseburger and he swears by the kabob plate.  Try them out if you want quality steak at a darn good price!

I've never tried this place before looked really good was surprised SO GOOD!!! I'm pretty picky so that means a lot coming from me but that's just based off what I ordered. Only reason I Gave a 4 star is when I got there girl working didn't seem welcoming.

My husband I went in for an after dinner drink. Ordered an Irish Coffee. Worst Irish coffee ever. Luke warm coffee and whiskey. That's it. Irish coffee is made with coffee (hot) brown sugar and whipped cream and Irish whiskey. A little training needs to be done here.

Been wanting to try this
Place for awhile because of the huge mimosas!! Finally got that opportunity today. Drinks were good, food was good. Servers could be friendlier especially since you have to wait awhile tell someone even acknowledges you. When we finally got our actual waiter he was friendly but the 3 girls were not. went there for happy hour first time there ordered beer and chicken nachos beer was cold, nachos were hot but had no taste asked for salsa they do not serve salsa never heard of nachos with out salsa it is like serving prime rib with out horse radish  its not done Will go back again but no nachos will try there pizza.

Really a fun place to go on Sundays and Monday nights to eat watch the football games. (When there were NFL games, that is.)  They have a diverse menu, something for everyone. I usually get one of their many yummy salads (chicken, apple, walnut is a good one!) and a personal size pizza (Bianco magnifico is delicious!).  They offer gluten free crust, which is pretty tasty. Their kids pizza is so fun! They bring the pizza dough and toppings to the table and let your child make their pizza. My son loved that! Nice atmosphere and fun patio to eat at in the warmer months.
Great service, attentive staff and a very comfortable waiting area. What else do you need!

Much meh. Meat was dry and lacked much smoke. Portions were ok. Roll was basically a kings Hawaiian roll. Slaw was pretty dry and was just mayo and cabbage, not much bite. Nachos were pretty decent and came with a ton of cheese. Would go back for nachos only.

Had lunch here yesterday and it was pretty good. The bento boxes were surprisingly large but they also contained a lot of rice. I ordered the unagi which had good flavor but also had a jelly-like skin that was difficult to remove with chop sticks. 

Staff was pleasant, restrooms were clean, prices good. Not many people here at noon on Saturday though,  even with a large offering of lunch specials.

This restaurant is considered quite good by people on the Nextdoor app.  I gave it a go, hoping to find a good local sushi place.  It has some things going for it, like the location, adequate parking, a gas station next door...  the hostess was really nice.  She helped explain the menu as it was my first time there.

I picked out 3 rolls; a tuna roll, a salmon roll and a soft shelled crab roll all on the classic side of the menu.  They were less expensive then the fancier side.  Fewer pieces per roll as well.  I was pretty disappointed with the food.  First was the smell.  Fresh fish should have much of a smell at all.  This did.  The tuna should have melted in the mouth.  It didn't.  In fact none of the 3 had much flavor at all.  I was especially disappointed in the soft shelled crab.  There was some slimy orange stuff smeared across the entire length of the roll, the crab had very little flavor... and where were the claws?  They should have been part of the roll.  So disappointing.  I won't be back to this one.  On to the next sushi place!  I really hope I can find a truly great sushi place in the Treasure Valley.  I visited Portland a year ago and had sushi so fresh it tasted like the chef plucked it from the sea, rolled it in rice and served it up.  Wow!  I miss that!

By the way, this is a one star restaurant that got an extra star because of the hostess.  That's it.

First time we have been to this Chili's restaurant and when we walked in, it was clean, not too loud.  We sat down and we're greeted by the manager, Tori and he went above and beyond for my boyfriend and I.  Very personable.  He recommended some appetizers and fajita plate which was delicious!!! First experience with Crave Delivery - they opened June 1 - was good enough for food and great enough for delivery  to look forward to trying again. But there are impediments in ordering app and processes we hope they fix. 

WHAT THEY DO:  Delivery of dishes selected by customers from app-only accessed online menu of options from nationally known "name" restaurants as prepared by Crave Delivery kitchen employees in their "ghost kitchen" and delivered to Meridian, Eagle and Boise by drivers who work directly for Crave. This is not a 3rd party delivery app, like Grubhub, this is vertically integrated business of food prep and delivery.

Right now there are four "name" restaurants in the mix for dishes to order and the menu includes about half a dozen choices from each one:

*Betelnut (SF Asian Fusion eatery that closed 2015)
*ESW@home (Seattle roots)
*Elliott's Oyster House (Seattle roots)
*Crawford Cookshop (Raleigh roots)  

Crave Delivery plans to add 8 or more restaurants to their line up later in the year after their big facility - that will include 14 or so kitchens - is built in Meridian.  (Target completion Fall 2020.)  But now their "ghost kitchen" is in a repurposed former fast casual food eatery in Meridian given Covid19 issues introduced opportunity to launch their business several months earlier than the Fall 2020 time originally planned.

NAME CONFUSION:  Crave Delivery - owned in part by owners of The Tavern @ Eagle Crossing in Meridian - has no connection to CRAVE the restaurant soon to open in Eagle by Lucky Fin (Boise and Meridian) owner.  Since Crave Delivery also calls itself Crave! in marketing materials, naming confusion is possible.  But so you know - different businesses.

DELIVERY:  For the three legged stool of order process - food quality - delivery I'll work backwards for delivery first as it was 5 stars worthy.  On time, as warm as can be expected given the distance from origin kitchen to our front door, neatly packaged in containers inside sturdy bags and the cold dessert was in a separate bag from the hot items.  The best part was the young guy driver (in Crave shirt and cap) was a great 'ambassador' for the service.  Adorned in mask - as was my hubby when he greeted the driver at door given the ordering app had no way to request contact free delivery nor a way to add driver tip we wanted to provide - he was friendly, professional and clearly proud of being a part of Crave Delivery. Delightful guy. 

FOOD:  We chose four options from Betelnut menu.  Flavor in these dishes was better than we've had from most Asian food restaurants in Boise and a big hooray that they were not over sauced.  (A flaw with most Asian dishes prepared for American audiences.)  The firecracker chicken lacked heat punch (in spite of lots of dried hot red peppers in the pretty mix) of Betelnut's firecracker shrimp (on which I'm thinking this was modeled) but we enjoyed tender chicken, abundant fresh minced ginger and just right rice.  We also appreciated what we could taste and see as quality ingredients.  The pork for vinegar glazed spareribs was from Carlton Farms in Oregon and perfectly cut and the baby bok choy packed with them was delicious. Every item in the order was neatly presented inside their individual containers.  The dessert was the weak link for us.  Fun packaging in canning jar and with mint sprig and edible flowers on top, the key lime had separated from the coconut mousse and pooled the bottom of the jar.  Desserts are made by local Boise Pie Company.  Maybe our Sunday order was filled with dessert prepared on Friday. 

ORDERING APP / PROCESS IS CLUNKY:  Hope they are working on this.

*Posted menus contain inadequate description of items.  Intro line for some items has ellipses (...) that when clicked offer no further information.

*Impossible to get questions answered in a timely way.  "Please call us..." inquiry went to voicemail after several minutes on hold with no callback.  (Does X contain gluten?  Are anchovies in Y on side or mixed in?) "Please email us..." inquiry took almost 48 hours to receive answer.  Too late if one needed to know to place an order then. (Were I ordering from a local eatery to pick up or from one that does it's own delivery I could either glean information from online menus or by a quick call to the restaurant.)

*No where in the order process to request contact-free delivery.  Nor does order process contain way to add gratuity for driver onto the bill which is paid, of course, by credit card at time of order.  

PRICES:  Meal that could have fed  2 - 3 people was $62 food (see below) + $16 in combo of fees & tax to equal $78 (before $25 "first order discount").  

*Kurobuta pork filled dumplings $9
*Wok garlic green beans $8
*Red vinegar glaze pork spareribs w/bok choy $18
*Firecracker chicken w/rice $17
*Coconut key lime mousse  $10
If you want to find a place for good BBQ ribs this isn't the place ,even tho that's what they are known for. I went to this place because I was craving for ribs and they didn't have any.

Great service.  Ramen noodles are good. I prefer less cooked.  So far best ramen In Boise area.  Gyoza are really authentic.  Also their other entrées although not Japanese they are really good.  Grand kids loved the orange chicken.

I have to say. This tastes like home. I grew up taking the metro to little Tokyo in Los Angeles and I missed the flavors I'd encounter on a daily. I won't say this is the best ramen I've ever had. I will say that the quality of ingredients is noticeable, the flavors are clean and the portions are spot on. I hate paying for tiny ass portions. I'm a big girl. lol. We got the beef broccoli, fried beef rice, and tonkatsu ramen. Oh and crab Rangoon. It was fried well and didn't leave a greasy residue or soak up the oil while it was being fried. Staff is friendly and super clean environment. I will be back!
I highly recommend this restaurant.  Very good food. We will certainly be back! The staff was helpful and very friendly.

This place did not disappoint!  Everything was cooked to perfection and the wait staff was great too. The layout of the restaurant is really interesting and modern. When they get their liquor license, it's gonna be packed.

So this place! Ugh. I'm sure some saw me check into a pet store and were like TF?? 
Some of you know that my lil man, Frankie boy passed away almost 4 months ago. (Very weird as soon as I mentioned his name here, the song I tried to get him to dance with me to when we went to the mountains together...the song started as soon as I typed his name. Y'all would laugh at "our song" lol 
He's always with me)
Losing him was one of the worst things to EVER happen to me. 
I miss having a little guy in my life. I've looked at several breeders online and whatnot over the past few months. And that's what y'all should do if you EVER even think for ONE SECOND about going into a pet store.
For so many reasons! One being and the most important , the health of a pup from an actual breeder is always guaranteed. Another, pet store pups always come from puppymills . PuppyLand swears theirs don't. I'm like 34, 43, 38, 35 years old (LOL) and in all my years...EVERY pet store I've gone into has always sworn "we promise our pups only come from registered and experienced breeders"

The pups were healthy. I didn't recognize any that were coughing. One pup and I hate saying this about any dog because dogs mean more to me than most things lol. 
This pup was listed as purebred Golden and it was soooo NOT a purebred. It was a funky looking little pup.
Very friendly, because she was looking like a result of her mom hooking up with one of her sons and this little girl was the result. 
Their little areas were somewhat clean. You could smell the sh*t in almost all of them tho.
The thing they do is just throw some more shredded paper on top of whatever is in there.
The way they handled the pups too I saw and was thinking...umm, that's a tiny puppy! Show him/her some respect. Don't just drop it back in his/her little playpen.

I've had friends who have gotten puppies from here and have yet to have ONE of those friends say "no health problems"
So many awful stories from folks who have bought from here. Do I blame them? Absolutely not, they didn't know any better. So many people don't realize the gamble you take if/when you get a pup from a "fancy puppy mill" that's how I see SOME pet shops.

I raised golden retrievers for years. Even before then I knew the horrors of pet stores and where 98% of these dogs come from and the awful conditions they come from. If a buyer came to me and told me they looked at a golden in a pet store I'd be like OMG WHYYYY!!! And they answered with "I didn't know pet stores were like this"
I always told them to ALWAYS research these stores before and to never buy from one. Sure some may get a pup with zero health issues, but again, it's a gamble. 
Lady got a pup from Puppyland and she has a rare brain disability. The dog can't walk right and will be like this her entire life. Puppyland pretended to care and last time I talk to this lady I asked if they fixed the problem, offered to pay vet bills, anything!? And she said the messaged her once and that was it. They never offered to refund the $, no offer to help with the unbelievable vet bills, nothing. 

Puppyland is sketch as hell! Even when you go to their Facebook page and even if you comment something nice, they immediately delete your comments.

So with breeding history, if you see this review ALWAYS  contact a breeder first and ONLY! if you're wanting a purebred dog. 
Going to a pet store is too risky. Plus they charge 2-3k more than most breeders depending on the breed.
I'd hope this day in age, most would know how bad pet stores are, but sadly they don't. Again, I don't blame them.
Did I like my visit here? Of course I did. I miss my little man SO MUCH! But I know better. I also know these precious kids need love too. So it's painful to write a review like this when they need love too and if you buy from here or any pet store, that's your business. 
These kids were soooo sweet and so needing love. They were so excited to see anyone stop by to see them. They were literally dying for some love and when I'd walk away, they'd cry and cry.
If Puppyland gave their health guarantees and actually honored them, the review would be much better not only from me, but from anyone who has actually gotten a puppy from them and if their guarantees about the puppies coming from reputable breeders were legit and they GAVE PROOF OF THAT! (Which they don't! No pedigree, nothing) then people wouldn't be contacting lawyers to get this place shut down. 

Puppyland, one thing, train your staff to be a little more friendly and less militant....and not just with the pups, with the customers as well. Tell them to put their phones down too and actually act like they like their jobs.

2 stars was for the pups. They deserve more but more stars would make this pet store look better than it deserves.

Cheers!

I definitely recommend this restaurant by The Village.

After many years of living in Meridian, I finally tried this place.  The burger was good, but not the best I've ever had.  The onion rings were very tasty.  My daughter just ordered an ice cream cone and I don't know if this is their standard cone, but HOLY MOLY...I kid you not when I tell you that the ice cream on this cone was at least 12" high!!  So high that they gave us a large cup to dump the ice cream in if she chose (which she did because who can eat that much ice cream fast enough before it melts or at all?)  I'm telling you a family of 4 could have shared this ice cream cone!  
Anyway, I thought it was a tad bit spendy for just a hamburger combo meal and an ice cream cone.  But to top it off, the gal at the window asked me if I would like to leave a tip.  Nope!!  If you are looking for a tip in a drive thru fast food joint, leave a tip jar outside.  They put people on the spot when asking for a tip at a drive thru burger joint and most people don't want to be embarrassed by saying no, but I said no.  Only because first, I thought the meal was expensive in and of itself and second, I don't like to be asked if I want to leave a tip.  If I tip at a drive thru fast food joint, it's because someone did an amazing job and went above and beyond.  Not because they did a job they are being paid to do and handed me a bag of food.  
Will I go back?  Most definitely, but not too often.

Came into Kahootz at 9pm on a Saturday Night. We were welcomed by a wonderful young lady, and a gentlemen at the bar, while being promptly sat. We were greeted with a great smile and some great opinions on the food. We consulted for awhile talking about the menu. I ordered the Steak Sandwich. My two friends got the Sunstone Brew IPA, the French Dip w/ Fries and the Ribeye w/ Potatoes, Asparagus and a Baguette. Starting with the beer, which was brewed with champagne, almost tasting like a less carbonated, dryer Budweiser. The. Steak Sandwich, it was very well put together, but lacked in taste. The Ribeye (not $26 worthy) was a mediocre steak that would be served at Denny's with Steak & Eggs. The potatoes were over-seasoned and cold. Although, the Asparagus was not too shabby, mediocre at best. The French Dip was very well put together but the fries were cold, stale and almost something you would get at Burger King. 

I would definitely not call Kahootz a Steakhouse. Rather, Kahootz: Steak Trailer Park

Great place. Went there with my wife and had no idea of what to expect. What we found was a place that has the best service I have experienced in years and a menu with around 150 items. Anytime I see a menu this vast I worry about getting cookie cutter mediocre food but this was not the case. The food was great, the service was great, and I will be back many times in the future!

I only rated this a one star so i could post a review otherwise I would have given it zero stars... If you are looking to get a Lowe's card DON'T DO IT, I have made all my payments every month for the length I've had my card and i logged on tonight as i do every time this time of the month only to find out they have canceled my card and are now wanting my balance paid in full... this is a very shady company and i do NOT recommend them... Ill be taking my business elsewhere AND spreading the word to everyone i know about my experience with Lowe's....
