By far the best decision I have ever made! I've been drawing my eyebrows on for years and am beyond excited that I chose to do this! Anna did an AMAZING job and I would recommend that everyone go to The Brow Club for anything they are looking to get done! I can't stop smiling! MY EYEBROWS ARE GORGEOUS!  two thumbs way up!

Was in the treasure valley from out of state and this place to me was a must try. I was not disappointed food was excellent staff was friendly and easy on the eyes. Would love to return in the future if I am ever in Idaho.

Best family-style Basque fare in the Treasure Valley. Come hungry, and order with on open mind.

Basque food is not for vegetarians or finicky eaters.

Love the lamb chops and BEST rice pudding for dessert, family recipes, and authentic Basque atmosphere. This is a great place for foodies, out-of-towners, and locals curious for a taste of this region's rich Basque culture!

¡Salud!

I have bought full sets of furniture multiple times through here and haven't ever had issues. This time around, I'm unimpressed. We ordered a bed set back in December and were told it would take 1-2 months to come in. It's now almost been 4 months and they told us sometime in April? Don't lie to your customers! Be honest with them. Especially during these times.

Came here on a busy night. It took over two hours to get our food with no explanation until the end that it was a fundraiser night. The fries were cold when we got them. The waitress apologized at the end, but up until that point said nothing except for the occasional your food will be here soon. If they knew it was a two hour wait for food, someone should have explained that up front.

Great spot! Service was on point, pizza was phenomenal, and the best mozzarella sticks I've ever had! I definitely recommend the "Ex Girlfriend" pizza, and of course the mozzarella sticks... Lol. 

The atmosphere is great too. Clean, and inviting.

Fantastic food made quickly, even during these challenging times. This is now my go-to for sushi and other excellent Asian cuisine. Highly recommended and they deliver right to your door through Uber Eats!

Is it just me or do you feel like employees should wash their hands after using the restroom?  Need I say more?  This was observed in the Lowe's in Meridian Idaho. 
Customer service was hard to get help Tool World.  Customer service guy had no idea how to answer our question. Item was priced at a "new lower" price, ring up at the regular price.
This place is so good, the food is awesome and I love that they have a gluten free option !! The staff is so nice and friendly!! Also love that they have grilled options for the chicken !!

I ordered the Philly cheesesteak, and somehow this two-bite wonder was $15? Also on Uber eats it says it comes with curly fries, which obviously did not come with it. Already small and  came with not a lot inside the roll. Had to order a pizza after I ate this $15 snack.

I was surprised how well this place is put together.  I loved the fact that you can pick your seats ahead of time.  I also enjoyed the Bistro upstairs and the menu.  

The staff at the Cinema were knowledgeable and helpful.  I had inquired about the VIP section and the employee gave me 2 free tickets to come back. 

I will definite be back!

Unsanitary and unsafe. Swarm of flies in the lobby alone, I estimate 40-50 (pictured is only one part of the ceiling, the entire ceiling was like this. They are hard to see in the photo without zooming in). So disgusting, I was waiting 10 minutes (only one there so it shouldn't take that long) with these gross things landing all over me before I left without the order so gross. Stay away my goodness so gross. Don't believe me? Literally step into the lobby ugh

This movie theater is so nice & the decor almost makes you feel as if you've stepped into a theater from the faraway past. The staff is always so kind too!

I only have one small con that isn't even a big deal, but it's that the popcorn comes in paper bags, which can be noisy & more prone to spills - but that's such a small problem to have!

I enjoyed my dollar chicken sandwich/value fry today, but I was really caught off guard with the staff. It was maybe 12pm, so I can understand if it may have been busy in the drive thru that was holding up the crew. My fiancé and I were going to eat inside. As nice as one guy was to bring my fries to me later on in my meal, I was really put off by the energy behind the counter from the same said Guy. As we were waiting in line to order, this guy (I'm guessing he could have been a manager, name tag only had his name and no position) was fuming and running around barking for the others to hurry up. I heard/saw him yell out "G** Dammit" in the back side past the fryers. I let the Lord's name slip sometimes, even with a cuss word accidentally, and I know I shouldn't expect a fast food joint to be totally professional and exquisite because that's not realistic... But belittling and cussing at your coworkers in front of customers is embarrassing for all of us who witness it and kinda shameful. I awkwardly looked at my fiancé like I desperately wanted to leave the situation. I hate conflict. We still got our food. It was still yummy!... But seriously, ease up on your coworkers.

No STARS!!
Mattress Firm is the worst of the worst!! We bought a new bed in January 2017 and it has a huge sink hole already. Their warranty says it is normal wear. The Mattress Firm Store dropped out of the whole issue after 60 days.  What a weak jacked up CORPORATION! Never ever buy from them!!
Would like feed back from my photos...?

Thai in name and while serving Thai food options in the main, this is one of the many Treasure Valley Thai restaurants that also squeeze Chinese and Vietnamese items onto their menu.  Service is friendly and sometimes, as in our most recent visit, even splendidly so but better organized at some times than others.  Knowing that going in to set patience expectations in advance may make the dining experience more enjoyable.

Owners are the same who own Pad Thai House in Boise and while we have had really poor experience for food and service and facility there, we have had good ones here for the same.  During the 2014 - 2015 years we ate here scores of times but it fell off our radar after that until recently given the discovery of better Thai food elsewhere in the Boise area.  I note the review I posted back then is missing, although the photos posted with it survive.  Having recently reacquainted ourselves with Thai Basil, it seemed worthwhile to review it again.  Falling between 3 and 4 stars based on umpteen visits were it not for the fact they denied access to the bathroom for two women in our recent dining party, we might have rounded up. 
 
VIBE:   Located in one of Meridian's woeful strip malls, the interior is welcoming with Asian décor, including a fish tank at the door, faux bamboo plant accents, dark red walls and interesting lights.  There are comfy seating options at all standard height tables with chairs.  And here I add "yahoo" while noting 70% of Zagat surveyed diners said in the 2018 released summary that they were "so over" high stool seating and yet so many Treasure Valley eateries rely on them.  Hooray too that there is for the most part ample space between tables to not feel as if one is in a sardine can, as is the case in many other local eateries.  And we appreciate every time we've dined here, even at full house, noise is contained at a level that makes conversation possible.

MENU & FOOD: This is a pretty safe bet for anyone across ages and experience with Asian food, from people whose frame of reference is Americanized Chinese food Sweet and Sour dishes or egg rolls...they have 'em...to people who want a bowl of spicy Thai Green Curry or the stand by dishes like Pad Thai.  There are better options in Boise for Thai food (Thai Cuisine as the leader and Siam Orchid as worthy contender) but this will do for good eats if you know what to order. We like to stay in the Thai lane, but also appreciate the Chinese lacquered duck served here.  Hard to find that cut up with bones in it delight.  Nearly all their Thai dishes are things we'd happily order again.

There are specials at lunch time, if that's your thing, for under $9 or you can order off of the standard menu then too.  Menu prices run about $6 to $20ish.

SERVICE:  Our most recent visit included people across three generations, some of whom knew nothing about Thai food and little about Chinese food.  The server was a model of grace for explanation and assistance.  Well done.  At peak times, like lunch hour rush, the only couple of cooks in the relatively small kitchen can lag behind and being prepared for delays then is a good idea.

ACCESSIBILITY:  It is more than disappointing, it is actually illegal, that they have put barriers in the way of equal access to the women's loo by people who use wheelchairs and walkers.  The ADA has been law since 1990 and this restaurant launched around 2014.  They should know better.  They need to remove the chairs stored in the hall outside the ladies' loo door that make the entry too narrow and also remove the piece of changing table furniture in the loo itself.  It is not optional to provide equal access to bathrooms for all people.  It is Civil Rights law. This is the business owner's failure.  The structure of the building is right.  Impediments  added by the restaurant owner are in the way.

PARKING:  Private lot parking is a big advantage here.  But the ADA parking is not laid out for either design nor for the minimum numbers required by both law and Idaho building code.  This is the strip mall owner's failure not the restaurant owner's.

HOURS:  Open Lunch and Dinner but NOT straight through.  Note they are closed from 3:00 - 5:00.  This seems pretty common practice for smaller, owner operated ethnic restaurants as it gives time for "family meal"' and for the kitchen to refresh for dinner service.
What a find. We love Thai food and this one is great. Had the Tom kha soup , Penang curry and sea food fried rice. All excellent.

this property management company is horrible. do not apply through them! they do not do business by the rules.  they screw up and then do not stand behind their word.  they take your money and then lie about things and blame it on the owner of the properties.  its not a property management they dont do things right.  i have so much i want to say but im going to leave it at just stay away! they are a very shady company and should go out of business.

On a warm day, my husband, our little girl and I decided to stop by Culver's to get some frozen custard. 

Because the drive through line seemed a bit long, I decided to go inside to order while my husband and our little girl sat at a table outside. The employee who helped me wasn't the nicest but oh well (since I am from California, we don't have a Culver's and I have only been to Culver's twice ever so I'm not the most familiar with their frozen custard flavors). She seemed annoyed when me when I was looking over the menu trying to see what I wanted to order, even though there was no one behind me... Honestly, I probably took less than 5 minutes to make my decision. Some people are just bitter... 

But anyway, I ended up purchasing: 

Vanilla Frozen Custard + Waffle Cone- After I ordered my item, I was given a number. I found a booth and sat because I wasn't sure if the employee who brings me my frozen custard would know to find me outside. About 5 minutes after I ordered, my order was brought out to me and then I went outside to join my husband and our little girl. I was surprised to see chocolate syrup on the frozen custard, when I was not asked nor had I requested to have any (I picked vanilla because I thought it would be okay to share with our little girl since she loves eating frozen custard and ice cream too. She is definitely a foodie too. When I have ordered frozen custard from another Culver's location before, it was not served with chocolate syrup). The employee who brought me my order was very friendly. Anyways the frozen custard was good. Just the perfect texture, creamy and just perfect for the warm day we visited. A good portion to share with another or 2 (including a cute little dog). If only there was a Culver's closer to me. 
---------------------- 
$3.06 after tax

Service really could have been friendlier at the register. But I won't let that spoil my frozen treat. 

Plenty of parking. Would come back to try some of the other food offerings here if I lived closer.

It was okay. I had a beef enchilada, asada taco, and a Chile relleno. The Chile rellano was good, but the beef enchilada and asada taco were just okay. The beans were also good, but the rice was under cooked, and the salsa lacked spice. Probably won't order again, but would be willing to give another shot if meeting with friends.

A great deluxe cookie shop right in the Village. It's just like the one in downtown Boise but with better parking and better prices. Each cookie runs about $3 a pop as of December 2019 but they are worth it! These cookies aren't like your standard cookies that leave you wanting another. These cookies are huge! Every time I stop by, I split one with my wife because they would be an entire meal to me alone and I'm a fully grown man. They aren't just about quantity though, these cookies are delicious! They have your standard chocolate chip and other cookies on rotation. My favorite was the one with Reese's Pieces in them. It was a peanut buttery, chocolatey moment of pleasure and I would recommend it to anyone who asks. Come give them a try!

I need to do quite a bit of printing and cutting and shipping for work and I've always had a great experience at this FedEx. The employees have been really helpful too. One time, there was only one poor young lady working on a Sunday and she got slammed with 4 customers but she was hustling! 

My prints are usually done the same day that I submit them online. They have a giant paper cutter there that I like to use when I need to do a lot of slicing too.

When I need to ship something, they help me find the best option and always give me  a receipt! 

One thing I would say is that there seems to be no rhyme or reason to when they will be busy. Weekdays can be dead or super busy, weekends are slammed or slow. Who knows!?

This restaurant is just plain fun!  We choose the Teppanyaki room for a dinner of 7.  Our chief was Harry.  Harry was fun, funny and very entertaining.  He is by far one of my favorites.  He kept the 3 kids  laughing and they enjoyed every minute of Harry's cooking show.  The food was tasty!  Unfortunately my food was prepared in the kitchen due to my Gluten allergy but was yummy nonetheless.  I appreciate their honesty that they could not prepare my meal without gluten.  

The host came to us at the end to see how our dining experience was.  It was great!  This place is consistently good.  We'll be back!
Having lived in Japan for many years, I was a bit skeptical, but I was very pleasantly surprised with Izumi!  The service was very good, and the sushi was really tasty.  I would definitely go again!

Love the atmosphere, food and jalapeño margaritas. Each time we have gone, the owner comes around and checks in with the tables.  This is definitely a family restaurant.  We have had several different meals and they have all been very good!  Staff is very attentive.  This is our favorite Mexican restaurant in the area.

Helpful and friendly people work here...  however there was a guy helping someone with one package on the weigh machine.  He was there the entire time!  Why was it taking soooooo long?  Both of the guys were helping someone but at least the other guy had a customer with more than one package.  Neither looked up from staring at their computer screens endlessly to acknowledge me for patiently waiting while holding on to my increasingly heavier package.  Finally a third gentleman came up to help me.  I was out of their in less than a minute when he didn't have to just stand there and stare at a computer screen.  I.T. come help these folks out!  They're headed for an eye strain workers comp case!!!!

If you want amazing brows, go to the BROW CLUB!! The staff and owner are so professional , great customer service , the inside is so calming and pretty.. I won't  go anywhere els but here, I highly recommend them. They offer brows and other beauty services as well.. The owner Anna is the best..
The staff is very friendly, the bread was good, the food was mediocre, red lobster food with extremely high prices

I had great expectations after locals talked up Epis. In summary, it was mediocre and overpriced.  We ordered the Chorizo appetizer, which was OK, not spectacular. The bread, the bean soup and the salad (iceberg lettuce with a single tomato) could have come from a high school cafeteria. Really, how hard is it to provide  good bread and an interesting salad?  The mains were pretty decent.  I had halibut, which was served in a boat of butter, but was hot, flakey and flavorful..  my sons had the cod filet, which was moist and enjoyable, and the lamb chops, which were cooked properly (pink center, seared on the outside with a little salt).  We shared the green apple bread pudding dessert, which was over smothered in whipped cream.  The meal for three, without wine, was $170, which would be fine if the apps and sides were as good as the mains.  The ambience was "aunt millie's parlor".  The service was prompt and cheerful.

Since moving to Boise we have eaten at Beef 'O Brady's 5-6 times, and of those experiences 4 of them have been terrible. The staff is typically friendly but we always seem to have issues with the food. My boyfriend is from Florida and has always had awesome experiences and loves their food at the locations there, so he was super excited to see there was a location in Boise. We keep hoping our experiences will get better but they never do. On one occasion we ordered our daughter chicken nuggets and they came out RAW in the middle, we let our waitress know and she had the kitchen recook our order, they came out raw again, at this point we were just ready to go, the waitress was nice and helpful. The next time we came in we ordered and I took a bit of my rice to find that it was moldy, seriously it was disgusting. When I told the waitress she looked at me like I was lying... she took my plate back to the kitchen and returned shortly to apologize and say that she smelled the rice and it was in fact moldy. Tonight we ordered wings to be delivered through UberEats, we had requested the wings to be extra wet. We get the wings and there is literally no sauce on the wings. We called to let them know and they did offer solutions but we didn't feel like leaving the house, which isn't their fault at all obviously. 

They have offered to help solve all of our issues, which is appreciated, it just seems every time we come in there's a problem. Unfortunately we probably won't be giving them another try.

Came to Izumi on a weeknight with a large group. They have a very nice, private event/party room for larger groups that seats up to 40. 

There were 17 in our group and so we filled roughly half of their private party room. I arrived early to ensure our table would be all set to receive our group and they already had the room completely ready for us! 

I ordered their Blue Hawaiian cocktail, which was pure blue swirling tropical indulgence. My dining companion and I ordered four different sorts of rolls to share. Their fish is wonderfully fresh and every roll we tried, we enjoyed. 

The hibachi chefs were entertaining and generous with the sake (for realsies...whoa.)! After our meal, several in our party tried sake bombs and for the under 21 crowd, they offered sprite with apple juice bombs. I thought that was a very sweet offering.

The ambiance is top notch. The outside doesn't do much to hint at the sleek, modern interior. The dining area is lovely and the bar is situated as a sort of tempting centerpiece. 

The service throughout the meal was spot on. Our server was able to keep track of all the orders and separate checks well, which is always nice!

Overall, a great meal in a lovely setting.

Get to it!

Had a terrific dinner last night with my wife and mother. Everyone gets what they want at Sizzler and the prices are very reasonable. The Salad Bar is by far the best around. Lots of fresh options for your salad. I especially enjoyed the roasted sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts. You don't normally find options like these as well as quinoa and edamame. I had the Baby Back ribs as my entree. They were delicious and fall off the bone tender. As good as you will get anywhere. My wife and mother added the side of Colossal Shrimp to their salad bars so it was a perfect fit for everyone. Highly recommended!

We have been to jump time in Meridian and Boise on a few prior occasions. Yesterday after being cooped up at home all day with a fussy baby my 8 year old and I set out with baby in tow to go to jump time meridian. We paid admission at 9:14 p.m. it seems ridiculously expensive at $10.50 per hour. I would have been fine with this rate if we were not treated like second class citizens the entire time we were there. They closed the foam pit at 9:40 so they can clean. after aaking if it was going to be closed for the rest of the night, I was told that it would "maybe" be opened up again and that it was really up to the Tramp Guard. I was told to ask the Tramp Guard about it  just to continue getting completely blown off , vague answers, and told to ask other employees about it. My child was very disappointed because she did not even get to set foot in the foam pit area despite me having paid full price admission.
Here's what really gets me, it was abundantly clear they were dead set on getting out of there no later than a nanosecond past 11 o'clock which is there closing time. After closing down the foam pit they continued their cleaning duties, asking me to move out of their way two different times. An employee was dust mopping the floor gaining closer and closer proximity to myself and my 11 month old walking infant. When he reached my baby with his dust mop he just looked at my baby and then looked at me like "get your kid out of my way". I swooped my baby up very quickly; If I hadn't been so quick it was clear the employee would have swept on top of my baby's hands!!! They mopped a section without restricting access to it which made my 8 year old daughter have walk barefoot on a wet, chemical covered floor. Prior to my daughter stepping on the wet floor, she asked the employee who was mopping if she could go where he had mopped so she could look for her socks. He told her to proceed with caution because it was slippery. He didn't pay any mind to the fact that she was barefoot and that it's a huge OSHA violation to allow a barefoot child/person to walk on a wet floor. 
THIS PLACE SHOULD BE SHUT DOWN.
There was no manager on duty, the employees were selfish, rude, and unprofessional except for one young man. Unfortunately though, he was not proactive in communicating to any of his coworkers regarding the reopening of the foam pit. I mentioned the fact that I was very unhappy about it closing early having paid full price. If the employees were half decent, had received proper training, or perhaps if there was a manager on duty, this part of our problem at Jumptime Meridian could have been resolved very easily by simply offering to extend our time allotment. It is clear that it's their way or the highway, and they will gladly accept your money at the full price rate too. Oh, and customers are a mere inconvenience. 
Jumptime Meridian, be prepared for a BBB complaint demanding all of my money back and a call to OSHA.

I've been coming here for years. It used to be sooo on point but then the staff all went to nampa( nampa location is so good!)
Meridian location is falling apart. It's not clean anymore. They reuse the papers in the baskets every day. They don't clean the case anymore. They touch the money and pay pad with their gloves hand then make the food. I've had a girl come out of the bathroom from cleaning and didn't change her glove until I said something.
It takes 25 mins on average for two bagels. Half the time they don't get the order right. They open at 630 but never have any bagels ready. 
This morning I came in at 645. Nothing was ready but she had a jar of eggs blended and sitting on the counter. I came back at 9am to get food for my staff and she still had the eggs sitting out. That's cause for illness! No more than 2 hrs and even that's too much!
Please get them some help at this location!! Please! I love your company and your food but dear god please get better staff that actually care... like the staff in nampa and Boise!

I'll eat the hell out of a bagel. That's what I do.-- Jade Puget

I agree with, Jade... I'll eat the hell out of a bagel, too, especially all the yummy things that Sarah's does with them! 15th person to review Sarah's Bagel Cafe on Meridian Rd near Franklin in Meridian. Easy on and off I-84. This is my 433rd review. 

Um, yes, please!  Last week I ordered a breakfast sandwich with sausage, egg, and cheese on a croissant. Today I got a roast beef on a Asiago Cheese bagel and it was super good. Fresh quality ingredients. They sell more than bagels-- you can get croissants, blended drinks, cookies and more.

They have lots of different bagels and toppings. I keep going in for a bagel and cream cheese and have ended up with a yummy sandwich each tim
e. I recommend! 

They have day old bagels and croissants for sale by the bag on a shelf in the corner. 

The person working, Long, was super friendly and makes suggestions for his customers. Nice guy! 

Enjoy!

Culvers reminds me of another fast food/ice cream shop I used to frequent, only better.

This location is very clean and the staff super friendly. The line was a bit long, but moved quickly. 

The food is tasty. It's fried fast food, so the bar is set pretty low, but the bites here are yummy without being greasy. The cheese curds are super delicious. 

The cold treats are very good. My kiddos love the concrete mixers and husband enjoys the shakes.   

The price point is fantastic as well.  Worth a stop in!

The food was good. We had the fajitas and the meat was the best I'd ever had. The condiments were a little scant.  The service was sub par and it the reason I'm rating them with two stars.  The waiter brought me a margarita after I ordered a dirty martini with vodka.  We asked for a TV channel to be changed. After waiting a long time we asked another waitress to do it. Then our waiter finally piped in and got the job done.  My husband and I ordered wings and fajitas to share.  The waiter did not bring an extra plate for either order. My husband used the lid of the tortilla container.  He did not once ask if we wanted another drink.  We were still finishing our one drink and he wanted to bring a check. We told him we were not ready to leave.  He still did not ask us if we wanted another drink and then brought us the check anyway. We were enjoying the atmosphere and would of probably ordered a several more drinks.  There was hardly anyone in there and it was before 8 pm on a Saturday.

Been here years ago and the food is still solid. I got the beef ribs again and they were even better this time. House salad was to have come out first but instead showed up with main which kind of rushed things. But all-in-all a very good experience.

One of the more screwed up systems to buy tickets in person. The need to prepick seats slows the whole Cluster F.  process down

The ONE electronic kiosk was also overwhelmed. Couldn't have two? And I'll be dammed to pay a 37% Fandango surcharge to do it on line. 

Won't be using this mode of movie viewing or this theater. Certainly makes TV streaming more attractive and cheaper to boot.

Stayed here for a night, I'm going to be honest I can't give too much detail as we were hardly in the hotel. It is very conveniently located to some excellent shops and restaurants, and like I said, we did not eat here as a quick 10 minute drive brings you to the village in meridian with lots of choices. 
The rooms were clean and the beds comfy, what more can you ask for? Check in was simple, when we needed some extra toiletries they arrived within minutes.

Just got into town and decided to try this place because I could walk from the hotel. I should have driven somewhere. 
Walked in and it was a typical sports bar. Sat myself and waited for a waitress. Took only a few minutes. 
My problem with the joint was the food. Tacos were tasty but the presentation lacked. They were thrown on the tray and were open faced. Next to them were the chips and salsa. Coulda gotten better chips and salsa at 7-Eleven. Pace sauce and store bought chips. Not what I was hoping for.

Our experience with this company, and the guys who came and moved our big furniture (Josh? and Gavin) was top notch. They were both efficient (barely stopped moving) and courteous. They wrapped our furniture and asked all the necessary questions, and answered all our questions. Very professional. We were moving from our rental home to our new home 3 minutes away. We only needed them to move the big furniture. Start to finish (they even disassembled our bed and put it back together) it took them about 2.5 hours. I would 100% hire them again and I will be recommending them other friends and family in the TV. In fact, in my search to find movers, it was almost impossible to find anyone who had openings in August on the days (we had about 4 days in different weeks we could have moved) we had available. VCM had availability and were very upfront with prices and timing etc. I had also called another big name mover in the Valley. They said it was going to take them 8 hours to move our stuff and that they would charge us 15 minutes twice for them to take their truck to our house and from our house back to their warehouse.... and we were in the same Boise zip code! Ridiculous. I told them that it didn't even take them 4 full hours to move all our stuff in and out of our home when we moved from out of state 6 months ago! So... long story short, don't call around... Call Valley Custom Moving FIRST!! Oh and call WEEKS ahead of time in the summer otherwise you might be in a bind. The only reason I am docking one star is because they said they were going to move us in the afternoon. That worked perfectly for us on that day. But 10:30 AM I got a call that they had finished their first job of the day early and were heading over. This caused me a lot of stress since we were not prepared for their arrival and I had planned that entire morning to get everything ready for them by 1 or 2 pm which was our original quote. Things worked out in the end, but it was very stressful for me, so I thought you guys would appreciate that feedback. And again, thank you VCM! We will 100% hire you again!

Do not use this company if you have nice furniture. We contracted them for a move on a large house and we're completely honest about the size and complexity of the move. They sent out two guys To move a 7600 square-foot house about 6 miles away. One guy was completely new and one guy was unable to carry heavy objects my husband had to move many of the things along with them they stacked and laid things in the driveway without proper wrapping and my large pottery barn leather sectional was scratched on every corner, my Ethan Allen table scratched on legs and my high end dresser had huge scratches on the top, as well as furniture left with dirty prints. Another guy was sent out mid move but this never should have happened or been booked with out properly skilled employees. The move took over 11 hours because they were so poor at this. Furious about this we called the owner. Josh, who is a nice guy came over and looked at it apologized and let us know that he had already discounted the moving job because we did not pay for the third guy. That was neither here nor there because the third guy should have always have been sent due to the size of the house and they should have quoted us for that instead of having the first two incompetent guys in charge of the move. I showed him the damage and he gave me a Furniture Repair place to come out. They were able to repair most of it to my satisfaction but my dresser still was terrible. When I asked the Furniture Repair company to contact the mover and get permission to do a refinish job on it they refused and said they had already paid out their maximum. This is not true as some companies have to replace items that are damaged and in this case this dresser is a couple of thousand dollars. He made it about the fact that he was losing money on the job but as I see it as a business owner it is his responsibility to ensure customer satisfaction and that his employees can deliver what he advertises. That did not happen here, and it was totally avoidable in my opinion. I think I was being very reasonable in asking him to pay-the $1000 to refinish the dresser regardless of what the move cost since  it happened because of his employees. I would not recommend using this company if you have higher-end-items; should they be damaged there is the  strong risk that they will not pay for them.

These are genuinely nice guys who go out of their way to take good care of customers. I was just in there again this morning, having a pretty bad day, and dealing with a flat tire I didn't have time for. 

Let me just say, these guys went above and beyond, solved my problem, let me vent my frustrations, (unrelated to them) and I walked out of there with a smile on my face. They made a real difference. What tire store does that? Who takes time to sit down and listen to their customers any more? 

You won't get this kind of personal service at the big box stores or national chains. These are neighbors and friends. This is what a tire store should be. Highly recommended!

My friends and I wanted to try the Meridian Bodovino laocation, We had dinner at Grimaldi's (which is excellent !!), and headed over to Bodovino for some wine.
As we entered there was no direction, or person to tell us to seat ourselves, or wait. We looked around, no one to direct us, so we found a table and sat down.
Again, we were not sure if now we needed to go to the bar to get our drink order in, or if someone would wait on us. I went to the bar, and bartender said she would come over. She dropped off a couple of menus, with no instruction, or conversation.
we all picked out our selection (glass), and waited. Finally drinks were ordered. Then 2 of the wines we selected were empty on the auto dispenser (Which was weird that that was the only way for them to get our selections...It is a wine bar right? So after a lengthy wait we got our wine. The pours were very small, and the wine was really cold (we were drinking red). For $12.00 a glass for a pretty common Sonoma County Cab, I'm not impressed. 
So fair to say, we won't be back.

Just left this restaurant after having a beer and grabbing some wings to go. Some guy commented when I asked for extra ranch, "How about some extra celery, you know it actually takes more calories to digest than what it delivers".

So I thought, whatever, just another douche that interjects their opinion when they don't even know the person they're talking to. Turns out that douche was a bartender / server that was eating at the bar, on break I guess.

So when he delivered my to go box he pointed out the oversized ranch he  provided and said, "Is that big enough for ya"? 

So I looked at him with my WTF eyes and his apology was "Sorry for giving you so much shit buddy".

I will never go back and whoever the hiring manager is needs to do a better job. I'm in town practically every month and have been a loyal patron. This employee has cost you my business. 

BTW, Audrey is amazing and the main reason I've been such a good customer. I'll miss our conversations young lady.
Tough call between El Rey & El Chaco for best tacos... The carnitas are ridiculously delicious

Ok I like the manager/owner here. He's very nice and one of the ladies was nice,  but the young girl who helped me today copped an attitude with me that was completely unnecessary! I'm sensitive to spices and pepper and I asked if the pico had jalepenos and she said yes. I asked if I could just have some plain tomatoes and she basically said no this is what we have. I politely told her I could not have peppers and in the past they gave me plain tomatoes. She smirked and huffed and went to the back. She came back with a double load of tomatoes and dumped it in my bowl with attitude as if to say,  "you want tomatoes, I'll give you tomatoes! Take that! " What she didn't know is that she gave me just the right amount of tomatoes! The food was good and there was no meat dropped in my veggie bowl this time! We did hang around for a long time visiting with our daughter and they did not seem to mind us being there so long. I recommend going here.

Worst experience of my life. I ordered a quesadilla for my son with chicken, cheese, sour cream and corn salsa. I literally has nothing in it. Not one even one piece of chicken which I was charged extra for it. When I called to complain about my order I encountered a rude employee Jesus who basically told me he didn't care that it wasn't right and wasn't going to do anything or apologize and told me if I spoke with his manager he wasn't going to do anything for me either. I wouldn't go to this store because clearly they don't care about food quality or putting out a good product. Choose somewhere else where you are valued as a customer.

My wife and I had to try this place after seeing it on Diners Drives ins and Dives. I had  burger. My wife had Chicken alfredo. The burger I had was just about the worst I have ever had. Totally lacking flavor. I had some of my wife's Chicken Alfredo. It was ok at best. its a fun place, but really? I did not get what all the fuss was about on DDD. The walls of the place and all written on by people saying it was the best food ever. If they do have the best food ever, we sure didn't get any of it. I know any restaurant can have a bad day. But its like that old expression. You never get a 2nd chance to make a good 1st impression. We won't be going back.

The Karlfeldt Center has helped our entire family, in just a few short months, more than years and years of other clinics combined. Dr. Karlfeldt is incredibly kind and patient with our son with special needs and offered us real hope. This is one of the few clinics my son can walk into and not melt down. He thinks Dr. Karlfeldt is one of his best friends. :-) Please check out the website, ask lots of questions and see if it's a good fit for you and your family.
This place is yummy!! I was pleasantly surprised at how flavorful the steak quesadilla is! Its my favorite! The mixed drinks are really good too!

I was in Boise area on business last week, and decided to get some Indian food.  I was perhaps feeling a bit homesick.  I came to Spice Indian Cuisine, and found it to be a small, but nice place.  It was quiet that day when I came.

I ordered one thing for dinner.  I ordered the Lamb Palak.  This is basically lamb curry with spinach (greens).  It was served with white rice.  The food was quite good.  I actually found it to be a bit interesting, as it was served to me with a metal plate, rather then the standard ceramic.  Nothing bad, just a bit different (in India it is more common to see metal plates).  In any case, the lamb palak was good.  It tasted the way any good curry like that should taste.  The lamb was cooked well, and was definitely not chewy.  It had just the right amount of heat (spice).  

I wish this place well.  Perhaps, when I come through on business again in Boise area, I may come back here.  I travel through Boise enough on business.

Worst customer service. Owner never reached out after my email review following what was to be a "day at the spa" as a gift from my husband. They were rude, never offered me any amenities while offering them to others right in front of me, messed up the scheduling of my services and then didn't apologize for the mix ups. I left after the massage and "pedicure".

The lounge seats were so comfy!!!  We
Sure miss the second floor cocktail patio!  It was so fun to enjoy a cocktail and watch the people while waiting for a movie.
Great spot for some classic BBQ. Portion sizes are huge! Highly recommend the onion rings as a starter!

We had dinner tonight at Goodwood Restaurant on Eagle Road in Meridian.  After taking a bite of my entree, I realized the salmon I ordered was extremely undercooked.  I told the waiter about it and he brought a small plate to our table and asked me to place the piece of salmon on it so it could be returned to the kitchen to be recooked on the grill. I expressed my concern about the safety of placing a piece of food that had been partially eaten back on the grill.  He sarcastically replied that the grill was 300 degrees.  He then reluctantly offered to have a new piece of fish prepared.  

The manager came over to the table and explained that any undercooked, half-eaten food returned to the kitchen was placed in a separate pan.  The waiter was apparently unaware of this important information.  

In about 10-15 minutes, after I was done with the rest of my dinner, a piece of salmon that was completely OVERDONE was delivered to our table.  I left it there.  At the very least, the restaurant should have offered to deduct that horrible meal from our check.  This will be the last time we visit Goodwood!

Undercooked salmon - yuck!

We are from out of town visiting and looking for somewhere to entertain our kids for a while. This place was great! Super clean and hand sanitizing stations everywhere. Our kids could run from one end to the other and We could see them everywhere. The staff was super friendly and helpful too!

Let me start by saying that I love The Village, and everything that it has to offer our community and The Village Cinema has been our theater of choice since opening here.  
This week my husband and had 2 movie dates (a special treat for me... of course for him he just wanted to catch up on some movies he was wanting to see, HAHA!)  On average, my family and I go to the movies 1-2 times a month and I finally decided it is time to share my thoughts and feelings about the Cinema.  I so so so wanted to give five stars but its just not possible in my opinion.  If these conditions change I can always do an update to my review.  
Let's start with the positives... 
1)  The staff is ALWAYS smiling and friendly.  I have never experienced bad customer service, an upset staff member, or an employee who hasn't been willing to go the extra mile... A+++ for that! 
3) COFFEE BAR!!!  Limited choices but I think EVERY theater should have a coffee bar!!! 
2)  The environment is stunning and fun.  Not an overabundance of movie theater posters but just enough for people to notice what movie they may like to see next.  And there is a little arcade to help pass the time while waiting for your showtime.  
3) The option to have child free viewing in the VIP section, with comfortable seating and service before the show (must arrive early for the service), is OUTSTANDING!!!  They have a pretty full menu that is from the Backstage Bistro (not covered on this review but is AMAZING!) and adult beverages which makes the experience that much more fun!  
P.S. They even open VIP to kids sometimes when showing kids movies (minus the alcohol of course). 
4) The prices are great.  Even with all the added experiences, the great environment, and the oh so plush comfy seats, the prices have remained reasonable.  
Now with my not so good notes... You will be happy to know that these are actually outweighed by the positives, but they are important to me.  
1)  The women's bathroom is repulsive.  I mean... ABSOLUTELY REPULSIVE!  Over the last 6-12 months the women's bathroom has been extremely neglected.  I kick myself every time for not running next door to the Yard House when I need to use the restroom.     
Examples: 
a) The stalls are falling apart, several of the locks are broken and have been manipulated at best to extend the life of them.  
b) The stalls and toilets are filthy.  I would like to say after multiple uses I can see how dirty these can get, but when I go in to the first showing of the day I would expect to see it much cleaner.  I won't go into detail of the unsanitary conditions I have seen these bathrooms in, but I will say that it has always been so bad (over this last 12 months or so) that they may need to hire a full time janitor to do nothing but maintain the restrooms all day long.  To add to that, many of the toilets do not flush well and people don't necessarily wait to make sure its done its job.  
c)  Many of the sinks are not working, the paper towel dispensers are out of order, you are lucky if you get soap, and as the day goes on, the garbage is falling out of the trash cans.  
I love the comfy new seating in the theaters, but then I ask myself is it ONLY about comfort when watching the movie?  I want to be able to walk out of the bathroom not thinking about what possible disease I could have contracted.  To not feel dirty and gross and want to wipe every part of me with alcohol wipes.  And what lady hasn't just finally resorted to wiping their hands on their pants after washing because the line for the hand dryer is too long to endure (as it is the only means to dry off at the moment)?
2) Lastly and no longer on the bathroom rampage, I recommend not ordering the buckets of popcorn when in the VIP seating.  The popcorn is served in buckets, with free refills, which is perfect... except they have no popcorn machine upstairs so the buckets are pre-filled and sitting on a shelf upstairs.  By the time the customer gets their popcorn it is cold and stale.  If you like your popcorn like that, by all means go for it, it is super convenient.  But if you want a less stale, warm popcorn, I would recommend you pick that up in the downstairs lobby before heading up to VIP. 
All in all... Still my favorite theater in town.  I recommend going, if for nothing more than the experience.  The prices are good, even the snack prices are reasonable and the seats are comfortable.  Just remember the ladies bathroom downstairs is sub-par.  My husband does report that the men's bathroom is "fine" and I have obviously not used it.  For disclosure purposes... he works in an underground mine and they use honey buckets 90% of the time, so anything has got to be better than that.  Enjoy the movie!

Not really sure how this is considered good BBQ. I feel sorry for the people who pay for this and are satisfied. I wouldn't waste my time with this place. The pulled pork was so damn dry and pulled too thin. Just don't.

Not the best nor the worst dessert experience.   
We had two "concretes" - their thick shake like dessert.   One made with vanilla was very runny/thin.  Neither one was mixed to the bottom.  
Staff was friendly.

As a new patient, they made everything so easy. I was able to get an appointment the following day of calling. The establishment is very nice, friendly staff, and ordering contacts was extremely easy.
The food is so good and the atmosphere here is great.   Very friendly wait staff.  Short wait times too.

First time trying this place. I'm definitely a burger critic and this place passed the test. Will be back. I got the mushroom Swiss with bacon and ketchup. It was bomb. Much better than I was expecting. Also they serve a bunch of craft beers. Soooo goood. The "girl stout" mint cookie beer was amazing.

Just about the best fries and best onion rings I've had, and the burger was pretty dang close too. Service was incredibly friendly as well. Only thing I wasn't head over heels for was the chocolate shake, which tasted like it was made from vanilla with Hershey's syrup (which I'm never a fan of). This place is much better than anything around when it comes to burgers (Habit, Smash, Boise Fry Co., etc) and I highly recommend it.

I had a hair appointment with another salon at 4pm on May 8. The lady called me the week before my wedding and said she could not do my hair because she leaves work at 5. No other time available. I called around and talked to Dane at V3 and she was able to squeeze me in on My 8. VERY happy about that! I got there and it was awesome to hear the stories of how they started. Super friendly and seemed to be knowledgeable about hair. She was telling me how my hair would look great this way and throwing color numbers at everyone. I went in for a color and blonde highlights. I was excited to see my hair. When I was done it was really shiny and looked good from all the product that they put in while straightening. In the end I came home, washed it the next day. On my wedding day May 12 my hair was BROWN. I asked my sisters if it looked like I had just had a $150.00 hair color. All said NO and neither did I! VERY DISAPPOINTED!! NOT AT ALL WHAT I WANTED!!!

My family use to love this place, we've been dedicated customers for years.  It seems every time I go the prices increase and the quality decreases.  They don't allow you to sample their new soup anymore which I feel they are using COVID as an excuse. On our last visit We found a hair in my sons soup, they gave us the wrong salad dressing and the soda machine was out of more than one option. This will Probably be our last visit to a once favorite restaurant.
Good clean facility with great technicians. They are kind and always take the time to make sure they are treating the whole area well.  Very reasonable pricing.

First time eating here. Went through drive thru and ordered two 3 piece fish and chips dinner and a side of Onion rings. 
When I got home and looked in the bag I didn't receive my onion rings. I was very disappointed. 
I called the store right away and explained what had happened and the employee on the phone offered to send me a coupon by mail for the next time I go back there. 

Over all had great and friendly service and the fish and chips were very good! Best I have ever had.

So, I went in person to the store to see a dining table I really wanted. The price online was for $559. In the store they tried to sell me the EXACT same dining table for the elevated price $770. I was NOT happy about that so I walked out without ordering. BUT - I did like the dining table enough that I ordered it online and with out the extra pricing.

The table has not arrived yet so I have no update on the quality. But I'm praying it'll be gorgeous because I'm not sure how the return process would be with the store.

Long story short - 1) go in person to see quality and colors if needed 2) Order Online 3) use Honey to get an extra discount automatically applied. I got an extra $110 taken off of my order from it. 
Code: www.joinhoney.com/ref/ocmnli
4) Save money and get the same furniture.

I recently re-visited GoodWood. I felt that I had to update my review and offer new information. My review of Goodwood over the years has steadily dropped. Goodwood used to be my place of choice to go for good Brisket. 

They also have had a pretty good Chicken Fried Steak (CFS), chicken fried Chicken (CFC), Smoked Turkey, and Nachos.

This time I ordered the brisket sandwich, which is my usual. The brisket was weird, both in the look of it and the taste. It was fatty and greasy. I was not impressed at all.

I left poor feedback on Goodwoods web site and got a call from one of the managers there. Here is what has happened to GoodWoods BBQ and why I have been forced to downgrade their ratting.

According to one of the managers at Goodwood, they (Assuming the owners) took a trip to Austin recently. On this trip, they discovered that in Texas, the common way to cook brisket is with a full fat cap in place and GoodWood Decided that they wanted to do the same. 

Let me explain.

I am front Texas, so I know what they are talking about. I cook brisket a lot and have experimented over the years with several different methods myself. Brisket is smoked for 10 to 15 hours, or more, depending on the size of the brisket. Bigger briskets have to cook longer. 

Most everyone in Texas leaves the Fat Cap on the brisket. 

The fat cap is a very thick layer (1/2 to 2" or more. Most butchers and markets trim down the Fat Cap so its not too thick) of white fat that is on one side of the brisket. 

The brisket is cooked with this Fat Cap still on and Fat Cap side up. As the brisket cooks, this Fat melts (Renders) and drips down into the meat. This happens throughout the entire cooking process. The result of this constant "Fat bath" is that the meat comes out very tender, but is also greasy and fatty. 

Even after 10 to 15 hours or cooking, the entire Fat Cap does not melt. A lot of it will remain on the meat, unless the place that cooks it decides they wish to trim it off, or has done this enough to know the exact thickness of fat to leave on that will fully render.

The downside of this process is that the meat tastes greasy, fat is left on the meat, and there is no crust on the meat. If there is crust, it is a very fatty and greasy crust. 

The other method of cooking brisket, which I use and GoodWood used to use, is to remove all or almost all of the fat cap. 

The result of this process is a slightly less tender meat, but a more healthy meat since it is not fatty (Either on top of the meat or of the meat itself). The other result of cooking without this fat cap is a nice crust on the outside that is not greasy, but is smoky and delicious. 

So the bottom line here is I no longer can recommend Goodwoods Brisket. If you do like a greasy and fatty brisket, you will like it here. But if you are like me and need to eat healthier, and dont like greasy brisket, you might want to start looking elsewhere for your brisket fix.

I also noted on my most recent visit that their CFS is gone down hill. Most of the CFS is good and fork tender as it should be, but on every visit, I have had about 25% of so of the CFS that is not tender and in fact grisly.

The CFS is ok, but needs improvement. The CFC is pretty good, so I still recommend this. The smoked Turkey is now my recommendation here as it is still good. The Nachos here are good and among the best in town.

Well, I have to get on the bandwagon and agree with the overwhelming love this restaurant seems to continually receive.  It just goes to show that having the right combination of elements is what makes a restaurant, THAT GOOD!  It's not all about having the best prices, or the hippest joint, but the experience as a whole.

Service here is personable and beyond friendly.  It is very apparent there are numerous repeat diners here, and the waitstaff has an impeccable memory of these individuals.  As other reviews have mentioned, they really do treat you like you've entered their home for dinner.

Reservations are absolutely highly recommended.  The dining room is small and the frequent return customers is definitely high.  In fact, I wouldn't be surprised to learn that there our families out there with set reservations on a monthly basis.

This is not a restaurant for a quick bite to eat.  So maybe not the best location for a first date . . . as you will either have TONS to talk and fill in the void of wait time between courses.  OR it will be so awkward by the end, your first date would probably be your last too.  There are 3 courses included with your meal, and of course the option of appetizers and dessert to add on, so 2 hours is not out of the question.

Everything I had or tasted was amazing.  I grew up cooking with my Romanian great grandmother, and so I feel like I can spot true home cooking when I taste it.  The food here definitely hits that bar.  The trade-off: rich food made with rich ingredients; so probably not the best place for someone on a strict low-fat diet.  I was so full when we left, I still wasn't hungry for breakfast the next morning.

Items I tried:
Crouquetas:  Delicious
Creamy Shrimp/ Lobster Soup:  Scrumptious.  Probably could of ate just a big bowl of this and been satisfied.
Sizzling Garlic Shrimp:  Rich and filling.  
Sides of the night (they change) roasted red potatoes and asparagus.  Mouth watering.
Dessert:  Our table pretty much ordered one of everything, and there wasn't anything that I didn't wish I had more room to order one for myself.  

All in all, a restaurant like none other.  Definitely worth bookmarking and visiting at least once, maybe for a special occasion.

Much more my husband's and my lane for ambiance and format than the Bodo-downtown location of mothership Bodovino, the primary drawback for us for this satellite is its' location in The Village. (Yes.  I am one of 16 people in the Treasure Valley who don't  'get' this Meridian mall.)  There is also wood to chop for food quality and correct wine service here.  Yet, were this in our neighborhood with it's casually upscale and unpretentious vibe, it could be a regular stop for a glass of vino if not food.  There is potential.

FEWER VINO MACHINES:
A concept I've never embraced, auto-wine-dispenser machines are here in about half the numbers as the Bodo mothership.  (I am not alone in skepticism about Enomatic machines: here is a good article.  http://www.eater.com/2012/11/15/6521867/rage-against-the-enomatic-wine-dispensing-machine )   As example, there was a problem one bank of machines when we were in and a Willamette Valley Vineyards Pinot Noir and Coppola Patagora, glasses from bottles held in the same machine bank, were far too warm and ruined.  Nebbiolo from another bank was the right temp.  (See Friendly Staff for outcome.)

OPTION TO ORDER OFF A WINE LIST:
One can also order off a well structured wine list, (Reds offered old world and new world, Whites offered foreign or domestic), if one prefers this over the machines. (We do.)  List has options by bottle or glass.  Good news for sparkling wine lovers, there are several choices by the glass.  Prosecco pours were ample sized and perfectly chilled.

FULL BAR:
Cocktail options at full service bar.  Coffee service is offered on menu but was unavailable when we ordered it at dessert.

TABLE SERVICE:
Unlike the "musical chairs" arrangement of downtown Bodovino (you get up to get another sample from the machines and your seat is snagged by another wino, umm...customer while you're away), this location has table service for libations and food.   Sign at entry says "please wait to be seated".  I like it. 

FOOD:
Creative menu from a kitchen headed up by former staff from Brick 29 but execution is very poor.  Menu includes several starters and contorni that can be put together to graze through a meal.  Entree service is a la cart. Some entree pastas can be ordered in "side portions".  Good concepts BUT fine tuning is needed for quality and many of our choices were a salt lick.  Examples...

...goat cheese gnocchi was doughy with only a hint of goat cheese and SO over salted that we could not finish the very small portion.
...pork braciole was served uncut so resembled a turd on the plate; it should be sliced and fanned out for service.  
...artichoke risotto was creamy and toothsome but far too salty to finish.
...wild mushroom saute was good but had clearly sat and cooled in kitchen waiting on risotto. 
...cacio e pepe completely inedible due to salt was returned to kitchen, chef agreed and made again with better outcome.
...eggplant in the caponata was spongy-underdone and too sharp with vinegar to pair with wine.

All portions were quite small.  A blessing given how over-salted all was.

VALUE: 
Prices reflect The Village's high rent.  With wine (two full pours, three half pours) and food, small plates for two without dessert clocked in at $85 after tax.

SEATING:
High perch seating at counter and some communal design tables (seating 10ish)  in and out.  (At least the high stools have backs.) Also some standard height tables in and out.  On both visits, those were well used and almost no one using the high seating.  Makes one wonder why so many places use so much of it.

FRIENDLY STAFF:
A warm welcome for guests.  And when we reported to our server the too warm wine pours from one bank of wine machines, the manager appeared at our table to say sure enough, she found the machine in question out of order and "bottles are warm to the touch".   She offered us additional glasses on the house.  Nice of her, but we declined the free extras as we had enough to drink at that point and simply wanted her to be aware so she could have fixed what was broken.   

ACCESSIBILITY:  
More accessible than Bodo location for path of travel.  Level in the door.  Standard height seating options.  Didn't check the loo. For winos on wheels, increasingly me these days as I've had MS for decades, heads up. 

PARKING:
ARRRGGGHHH...The Village parking is always a challenge.  Although less a challenge than downtown Boise, I guess.  

TIMING IS EVERYTHING:
HH starts at 3:00.  Some machine wines are 50% off and they have a HH plate or two. You need to time a visit carefully to avoid crowds even now and once folks figure out this is here, it should be even more bustling.  No reservations taken.

Is Epi's closing?  Changes are afoot as noted on Epi's Facebook page in a post by longtime server Bridget Murphy.  "There are upcoming changes in this beloved house. I will be retiring May 11 as I posted a few months ago. Chris will be retiring at the end of July. As far as whether or not Epi's will remain open, the answer to that is unclear at this time. As Chris says, she is leaving the answer to that question in God's hands  We love you, our Epi's family."

This was confirmed in reporting by Michael Deeds in this morning's (5/3/19) Boise newspaper.  For those who want to read his article, I have inserted a link at the end of this overdue review.  

Which is not a review, really, but a love letter, of sorts, to owner Chris Ansotegui and all the people who make Epi's so special in the times my husband and I enjoy being well fed, well served and feeling loved as guests for authentic Basque food in a restaurant named after Chris' grandmother and located in old house on Meridian's main street.

I don't need to write about the delicous food or the wonderful warm welcome extended in the space that feels like being in someone's home, as this once was, and gracious service as others have done that so well. 

I don't even need to offer tips that reservations are essential and this is a place to come when you have time for a leisurely meal and that the wood chairs can feel pretty hard by meal's end so if you're visiting with an aged relative or friend who has 'sit problems' they might want to know up front to bring their own cushion.

But I might mention that Chris has created such a wonderful place where everyone feels so welcome that my husband and I know a young couple who were married there.  They wanted to hold the ceremony in the restaurant because Epi's had become a special place for them during their 'courting' time for the loving spirit extended by Chris and the staff to everyone.

And I will absolutely mention that when Chris converted this house to a restaurant in 1999 (she celebrates Epi's 20th year of business this year) she made it wheelchair accessible for ramp to the door and seating inside.  As a person who has mobility limits myself (I have had MS since college) I appreciate that Chris followed the rules of the 1990 passed Civil Rights law that is known as ADA to ensure all people have equal access to enjoy Epi's.   You would be astounded to find how many restaurants and bars in the Treasure Valley, including brand new ones and newly remodeled ones, ignore that civil rights law, even now in 2019 when the law is 29 years old, which means people in the 11% of Americans with mobility disabilites are excluded from participation. How wonderful Chris thought of inclusion.  I thought of that on one visit when a child using a wheelchair was fully included at the table with her family. 

In the news article linked below Chris' brother, Dan, (currently with Basque eatery Txikiteo in Boise) says what makes Epi's so special is the spirit Chris has created and one feels "You get a hug either coming or going."  Indeed.  To that end, to see the heart of this restaurant, I have also inserted below a video of Chris speaking to customers that she posted on New Year's Day 2019, the kick off to Epi's 20th year.  

If you have not yet experienced Epi's now is the time to make a reservation and go.  James Beard was once asked what was his favorite restaurant.  His reply went something like this.  "The same as yours.  The one that loves you the most."  With that in mind, it is easy to see why so many people have Epi's on their favorite restaurant list. 

Chris' comments on New Year's 2019 at start of Epi's 20th year:  https://www.facebook.com/722146377847629/videos/2057306051002778/

News article:  https://www.idahostatesman.com/entertainment/ent-columns-blogs/words-deeds/article229860749.html

I have been searching for a good Mexican food restaurant in Idaho for 16 years now. When it comes to Mexican food, it is very very subjective. 

I am from Texas, so when I was growing up, we had Mexican food 2 or 3 times per week. I like my Mexican food with lots of flavor, and a good amount of heat. Most native Idahoans like their food more on the bland side with very little to no heat.

Traditional Mexican food is often pretty greasy, fatty, does not have a lot of flavor and little to no heat at all. 

What we have here in the US is usually called Tex-Mex, though Im not really sure why. Tex-Mex refers to a blend of Mexico and Texas. 

If you live in Idaho, would you call ours Idaho-Mex?

If you travel across the US, trying Mexican restaurants in every state, you will have vastly different experiences with the food. Interestingly enough, the best Mexican food, as well as other cuisines, I have had was when I lived In Colorado.

I had very high hopes for this new addition to Meridian. The outside is very non descipt. It gives you no idea at all what to expect when you walk through the doors. If I were the owners here, Id work on doing some work on the outside to make it look more festive like the inside.

On the inside, I found lots of color and some of the best decorations of any Mexican Restaurant I have ever been too. I felt as if I was actually in Mexico, which is something I expect of a restaurant experience. When I go to a Chinese Restaurant, I want to feel like im in China, when in an Italian Restaurant, I want to feel like im actually in Italy etc...

The chairs all have very colorful decorations on them which match the walls. The only part I did not like was the bar area. It does not match the rest of the restaurant at all. It looked like it was just an after thought. 

All of the staff here was very friendly, which is something that I have found in very very few Mexican Food places. In most that I have been too, its almost as if you are an annoyance and they just want to get your money and be rid if you. Im very happy to say this was not the case here. I felt like I was wanted.

On to the food. The salsa was...well not very good at all. It tasted like chunky Tomato Sauce from a can. Even my wife hated it, and she is native to Idaho, so she has more of a bland pallet.

I had a Chicken Chimichanga and my wife had Chicken Fajitas. I will start with the better dish. The fajitas were good, but there was very little Chicken. The chicken there was was in small bits, not like a full Breast that was cut up. The flavor of the chicken was good though. It had a good smokey taste. 

The Chimichanga, like the salsa, had no flavor what-so-ever. I used my wife's Guac Sour Cream and piled it on the top to give it flavor . I had a taco on the side. This is not your regular ordinary Taco. 

It was whats known as a street taco, so its very very small. The flavor was.....interesting. I asked for ground meet. I am not really sure what the meat was, but it was not hamburger. I think it was Chirizo, which is a traditional meat in Mexico. The taco had a lot of Cilantro on it, which I love. For me though, I would not have this again. 

The highlight of my meal was desert. I had Sopapillas. They were hot, with honey, cinnamon and raspberry on and in them. They were excellent.

I give the Chicken Chimi a 1 out of a possible 10. I give the fajitas a 5 out of 10, and I give the salsa a -3. I give the Sopapillas a solid 8. 

If I was to rate the outside, Id give it a -1. If I was to rate the inside, Id give it a 10. I give the wait staff a solid 10 as well. 

So because my ratings were all over the place, the best overall rating I could come up with was 3 stars.

The bottom line here is that whether you like this place, love this place, or hate it is going to depend on your taste in Mexican Food. Its like finding a good woman to love. The women you fall in love with is very subjective. 

The women you like might bore me to death and I might totally hate her, and the one I love might bore you and you might hate her. So like a good women, find the Mexican place that you love and never let it  go. As for me, my search continues.
